News.title: M25 fire - live: Motorway in St Albans closed as 'shut windows' warning issued
News.content:
Part of the M25 has been closed as a major fire has erupted at an industrial estate in St Albans, sparking risks of a 'secondary explosion'

A large fire is raging next to the M25 after breaking out at an industrial estate in St Albans.

Emergency services have ordered a full closure of the motorway as the blaze has sparked risks of a "secondary explosion", with smoke and debris also affecting the carriageway, National Highways said.

The motorway is currently closed between junction 21A and 22. Road closures are also in place in Colney Street and Old Parkbury Lane near to the centre of the fire.

Locals have been urged to keep their doors and windows closed, and to avoid the area while firefighters tackle the blaze. Dramatic footage has captured the heavy smoke plume drifting into M25 this morning.

Herts Fire & Rescue said: "We are currently responding to an incident in Ventura Park, Old Parkbury Lane, Colney Street, St Albans. If you live locally, we advise to keep doors and windows closed and please avoid the area while emergency crews carry out their work."

News.title: Drivers warned common hot weather aircon mistake could trigger sudden £110 fine
News.content:
Drivers warned common hot weather aircon mistake could trigger sudden £110 fine

The continued hot weather can mean scorching temperatures inside vehicles but keeping them cool might prove expensive

View 3 Images Being parked in the summer heat can quickly see temperatures inside a car becoming unbearable (Image: GETTY)

As summer temperatures continue to soar, with more record-highs expected, motorists have been warned that a common mistake when using their car’s air conditioning could result in a major fine and may force them to find other ways to cool down their vehicle when it’s at its hottest.

‌



The issue is due to anti-idling rules, which forbids drivers from running their engine unnecessarily while parked on a public road. It’s meant to help tackle roadside pollution and can trigger a fine even if the engine is only on to power the aircon unit.

‌



Temperatures inside a parked car can quickly become dangerously hot, with motorists warned never to leave children, vulnerable adults or pets unattended in a parked vehicle, even for a short time, as internal temperatures can rise dangerously quickly.

‌



View 3 Images Keeping the air conditioning running while parked can trigger a fine (Image: GETTY)

Graham Conway, managing director at Select Car Leasing, said: “Sitting in a parked vehicle with the engine running simply to power the air conditioning could result in a penalty. Being inside the car does not automatically make idling acceptable.

“The message is not to avoid using air conditioning while driving. It is to avoid leaving the engine running unnecessarily once you are parked, protecting yourself from an unexpected fine while also reducing wasted fuel and local pollution.”

‌



The temperature inside parked vehicles can quickly soar during the summer months, particularly if there’s no nearby shade to shield them from the sun. Mr Conway revealed some other ways motorists can keep their parked cars cool without risking a penalty notice.

It will be easier to cool the inside of the car while you are travelling so make the most of this before having to stop and then switch the engine off. Parking in the shade or using a windshield sunshade can help keep temperatures down for a bit longer. Once you are stationary, opening the doors can allow hot air trapped inside the car to escape or head outside the car yourself if it’s safe to do so.

Under the anti-idling rules, local authorities may be able to issue a fixed penalty notice although the value can vary between different councils. Generally, it starts at around £20 for motorists that continue idling even after being asked to switch off their engine.

‌



View 3 Images There are other ways to cool down a vehicle without turning on the aircon (Image: GETTY)

This fine can increase to £40 if it is left unpaid for too long. However, in some areas like Islington, the council confirmed drivers could face a £110, reduced to £55 if paid within 14 days.

Mr Conway explained: “Drivers should not assume the penalty will always be only £20. In London especially, councils are under considerable pressure to reduce roadside pollution, so motorists could find idling rules enforced more firmly in known problem areas.”

Article continues below

These rules do not apply if you’re sitting in ordinary traffic, waiting at lights, defrosting a windscreen or temporarily at a standstill because of traffic. In all of these situations, motorists are usually allowed to keep their engines running despite being stationary.

He said: “Try to park in shade where possible, use a windscreen sunshade and open the doors briefly before getting inside to allow trapped hot air to escape. If you need to wait for somebody, it may be safer and more comfortable to leave the vehicle and find a shaded or air-conditioned building rather than sitting in a rapidly heating cabin.”

News.title: Taxi driver jailed after driving teen passenger to secluded spot before rape
News.content:
Taxi driver jailed after driving teen passenger to secluded spot before rape

Taxi driver Abdul Nabizada picked up the 19-year-old woman after a night out before launching the sickening attack

View Image Abdul Nabizada moved from Afghanistan to Scotland (Image: Alan Simpson)

A private hire taxi driver who had worked as a translator for the British Army has been jailed after raping a teenage passenger.

Abdul Nabizada, who came to Scotland from Afghanistan, picked up the 19-year-old woman after a night out in November 21. Instead of driving her home, he took her mobile phone from her and drove to a secluded area of Joppa, near Edinburgh.

There, he attacked her, with the High Court in Edinburgh told that he detained the victim against her will before raping her. The court also previously heard that, before raping her, Nabizada also touched the victim's body and struggled with her.

The young woman escaped from the vehicle and contacted her friends, who found her distressed and frightened a short time later. Nabizada is seen repeatedly returning to the area after the attack on CCTV footage from Queens Bay Crescent.

Calling the attack a "crime of opportunism", Judge John Morris KC said: "The jury has unanimously convicted you of committing a serious sexual assault on a vulnerable woman. The offence is an extremely serious one."

Nabizada was sentenced to seven years in prison at the High Court in Edinburgh today after he was found guilty of the rape at a trial last month. Judge Morris told the 36-year-old that his attack has had a "long-lasting impact" on the victim.

He said: "[She] was particularly vulnerable because she was intoxicated and that should have been obvious to you. The [assault] occurred when you were responsible for transporting her home."

Defending, lawyer David Taylor told the court that Nabizada moved to Scotland after working for the US, Danish and UK militaries, primarily as an interpreter, in his native Afghanistan. He currently holds indefinite leave to remain in the UK and had applied for British citizenship.

Mr Taylor told the court Nabizada is now concerned about getting deported due to his conviction. Nabizada, a "family man" with four children, attended his sentencing in a black suit and was accompanied by a translator.

Judge Morris said the number of positive references submitted on behalf of Nabizada ahead of the sentencing, as well as the fact he had no previous convictions and that he was a "family man" were taken into account. Apart from his prison sentence, Nabizada was placed on the sex offenders register indefinitely and ordered not to contact or approach the victim.

Faye Cook, Procurator Fiscal for High Court sexual offences, said the conviction is the result of the victim’s courage in coming forward and the determined work of police officers. She said: "Officers had to piece together evidence from a range of sources to identify the offender and build the case that was presented in court."

She added: "The victim should have been able to trust that her journey home would be safe. Instead, she was seriously sexually assaulted by a taxi driver who took advantage of her vulnerability and abused his position resulting in a deeply traumatic experience." Ms Cook continued: "While stranger offending is rare, Scotland’s prosecutors treat every report of sexual abuse with the utmost seriousness, recognising the profound and lasting impact these crimes have on victims and communities. I hope this conviction provides reassurance that reports will be thoroughly investigated and that COPFS will work with policing partners to ensure offenders are held accountable." Detective Inspector Kirsty McArthur said: "This was a shocking attack on a woman in the city, and Nabizada will now face the consequences of his despicable actions. We remain committed to tackling sexual crimes and bringing those responsible to justice.

Article continues below

"I’d encourage anyone who has been a victim of such crimes to come forward and report it to us. We’ll thoroughly investigate and have specially trained officers and partner agencies to support you throughout to ensure those responsible are brought to justice."

News.title: Energy bills forecast to rise again but experts say 'don't wait' to save cash
News.content:
Energy bills forecast to rise again but experts say 'don't wait' to save cash

Energy analysts have warned of another bill rise when the price cap updates again in October - just as temperatures start to drop

View 2 Images Energy bills look set to go up again this winter

Energy bills are forecast to rise again this winter in another blow for millions of households.

‌



The Ofgem price cap went up by 13% in July after the conflict in the Middle East caused a spike in wholesale costs.

‌



But analysts have warned of another bill rise when the price cap updates again in October - just as temperatures start to drop and households begin to turn on their central heating.

‌



Energy research and consultancy firm Cornwall Insight currently predicts the Ofgem price cap will go up by another 2%.

Ofgem has also updated its methodology to reflect that people are now using less energy as a way to save money.

View 2 Images Ofgem will update its price cap in October (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

‌



Under its previous calculations, the current price cap is set at £1,862 a year and Cornwall Insight predicts this could rise to £1,906 in October.

But based on its new lower estimates, the current price cap is set £1,663 a year and analysts say it could increase to £1,699 in October.

Ofgem will confirm its October price cap on August 26, so forecasts may change slightly before then.

‌



How to save money now

Comparison site Uswitch has urged households to take action now and considering locking into a cheaper fix.

Sabrina Hoque, energy expert at Uswitch.com, said: "Every forecast we're seeing points to a more expensive October than last winter – it's just a question of how much more.

"Don't wait until you’re hit with a bigger-than-expected bill to realise you're paying too much. Lock in a cheaper fixed rate now – you'll beat every current prediction, and you'll still get October's VAT cut automatically."

‌



Get the best deals and tips from Mirror Money WHATSAPP GROUP: Get money news and top deals straight to your phone by joining our Money WhatsApp group here. We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

The warning comes despite Prime Minister Andy Burnham announcing a temporary VAT cut on domestic energy bills from October.

The Government claims it will save a typical household about £45, though analysts say rising wholesale energy caps are likely to offset any saving.

‌



Ms Hoque continued: "The VAT cut is welcome and will provide some relief over winter, but it only applies to electricity, and it's modest next to what suppliers are predicting for the price cap."

What is the Ofgem price cap?

Despite what its name suggests, the price cap does not actually limit how much you pay for gas and electricity.

Instead, it sets a cap on what you can be charged for unit rates and standing charges - so your energy bill is still based on how much gas and electricity you are using.

‌



The unit rate for gas is 7.33p per kilowatt hour (kWh) while the standing charge is 29.04p. The unit rate for electricity is 26.11p per kWh. The standing charge for electricity is 57.19p a day.

The price cap figure represents what the typical direct debit household with average energy consumption can expect to pay.

There are different unit rates and standing charges for prepayment customers and those who pay on receipt of bills.

Article continues below

You are covered by the price cap if you are on a variable energy tariff, so if you are not fixed into a deal.

News.title: Mum, 61, with 35-year-old boyfriend says relationship works – as they barely see each other
News.content:
Mum, 61, with 35-year-old boyfriend says relationship works – as they barely see each other

A couple with a 26-year age gap have spoken about the secret to how they make their relationship work and how their families responded to the news of their love

View 3 Images Sundari and Maxi have spoken out about their age-gap relationship (Image: @elamorestemporal/Instagram)

A mother who is dating a man 26 years her junior has said their relationship works because they don't see each other very often.

‌



Mum-of-two Sundari, 61, fell in love with 35-year-old boyfriend Maxi. Sundari lives with her two children from a previous relationship in Pilar, Argentina, while Maxi lives around 40 minutes away with his mother in the city of Avellaneda

‌



Speaking to TN, wellbeing coach Sundari said that after the end of her relationship with her ex - the father of her two children - all of her subsequent partners had been younger, something she’s put down to her friendship circle being filled with younger people.

‌



The pair, who met around 18 months ago during a cacao ceremony - a mindful ritual based around drinking pure, ceremonial-grade cacao - have since spoken about the secret to their strong relationship.

Maxi and Sundari were invited to the ceremony by people and Sundari was asked to lead the gathering.

View 3 Images Sundari and Maxi met 18 months ago (Image: @elamorestemporal/Instagram)

‌



Sundari revealed the secret to his and Maxi’s enduring love, and it was simply a question of scheduling. She explained: “On Saturdays, Maxi comes round and stays with us until Monday.

"During the week, we send each other lots of little love messages in the morning and before bed. We’re very respectful of each other’s time. It’s lovely to see each other again at the weekend.”

It is this deliberate distance, explains Sundari, that means the pair can enjoy some autonomy during the week. She said: “Plans might come up during the week, but we mostly see each other at the weekends.

‌



“I like it this way. I like having my own time. I was married and lived with my partner for 20 years. I’ve never lived with anyone since, and I love having a boyfriend.”

Maxi said he had strong feelings for Sundari from the first moment he saw her.

He recalled: “When I arrived, she was singing. Afterwards, we chatted for a while, and I asked for her Instagram. Her presence blew me away. I loved watching her sing.”

‌



View 3 Images Sundari and Maxi (Image: @elamorestemporal/Instagram)

Maxi also addressed the age gap, but explained that although he thought Sundari was younger than she was, that when her true age was revealed, he was even keener to get to know her.

He said “Then we started talking about our lives, and at one point she told me how old she was. I thought she was 45. When she told me she was 60, it didn’t cross my mind at all. No sense of rejection. On the contrary, I felt even more enthusiastic. I thought: ‘Wow, I can’t believe it’.”

‌



When it comes to acceptance, both Sundari and Maxi have the support of those they love. Sundari explained that whilst it was a bit of a shock to her two sons, she said that “they want to see me happy and support me in all my decisions”.

She added: “When Maxi comes round at the weekends, my youngest son is at home, and it’s all very harmonious, very lovely.”

Maxi explained that his family was also accepting of his relationship and how his mother had no point commented that Sundari was old enough to be his mother. He said: “She never once said, ‘She could be your mum’. She sees that I’m doing well, she sees that I’m happy, and that’s all that matters to her.”

Article continues below

Sundari rejects any backlash they’ve received. She said: “This has always happened. There have always been relationships between older women and younger men.

“The thing is, in the past, it was so taboo that nobody made them public. I love the fact that today they can be brought into the open and that everyone can live the life they want to live.”

News.title: New ibuprofen warning for people in five groups this week - full list
News.content:
New ibuprofen warning for people in five groups this week - full list

A pharmacist has explained what you should do instead

View 3 Images Millions take ibuprofen for pain and inflammation

As the ongoing heat pushes more Brits to reach for ibuprofen to soothe heat-induced aching joints, pharmacists are warning that for some people, it could do more harm than good. The MHRA reported that common painkillers such as ibuprofen and naproxen can increase the risk of sun sensitivity, but pharmacists say that’s not the only risk to watch out for.

‌



“Some people notice their joints feel more swollen, stiff or uncomfortable during hot weather. Higher temperatures can cause blood vessels to dilate and may contribute to fluid retention in some individuals, potentially making existing joint symptoms feel worse,” said Hanna Yusuf, Prescribing Pharmacist at Chemist4U.

‌



View 3 Images The common pills cost pennies in shops across the UK

‌



Hanna warns ibuprofen should be avoided by certain at-risk groups during prolonged spells of hot weather:

Pregnant, especially after 20 weeks: ibuprofen can affect the baby's development, including the heart and the amount of fluid around the baby, so it should only be taken if a doctor says it's okay.

Living with heart failure or liver disease: ibuprofen can make these conditions worse by causing the body to hold onto extra fluid and salt, adding strain to an already weakened heart or liver.

Living with kidney disease: ibuprofen adds extra pressure to kidneys that are already struggling, which can push them closer to failing to do their job properly.

Taking blood-pressure medicines (ACE inhibitors, ARBs or diuretics): mixing these with ibuprofen is known as the "triple whammy" because together they can reduce blood flow to the kidneys and cause sudden kidney damage.

Reacted badly to ibuprofen/similar painkillers before: if you've ever had a reaction, your body has already shown it doesn't tolerate this type of medicine well.

‌



Hanna said: “Ibuprofen is one of the most reached-for painkillers in the country, and for most people, taking it occasionally isn’t something to worry about. The problem is that hot weather can increase your risk of becoming dehydrated, and dehydration is one of the factors that can make ibuprofen harder on your kidneys. That’s particularly important for people who already have kidney disease, heart failure, liver problems, or take certain blood pressure medication.

“We’re not saying that people should stop taking prescribed medication or throw away their ibuprofen. The key thing is that if you’re one of these higher-risk groups, it’s worth speaking to a pharmacist about the safest option for you during a heatwave. In many cases, paracetamol may be a more suitable choice.”

View 3 Images People in some groups may need to reconsider this week

News.title: M55 closed in Lancashire as motorist spots dead body on hard shoulder
News.content:
M55 closed in Lancashire as motorist spots dead body on hard shoulder

There was a report of concern for the welfare of a woman on the M55 in Lancashire last night, just 10 minutes before a body was spotted

View Image The M55 was closed after the incident (file) (Image: National Highways)

A woman's body was spotted on the hard should of a motorway as a concerned motorist drove past.

‌



Concerns for the welfare of a woman on the M55 in Lancashire were first raised at around 10.20pm last night, with another report made just 10 minutes later. This came from another driver who was travelling towards Blackpool on the motorway.

‌



The motorist explained they saw what they believed to be a body on the hard shoulder. Officers were sent to the scene between junctions one and two, near the Broughton interchange.

‌



The body of a woman was found and the M55 was closed for around five hours while enquiries were carried out. Officers continue to work to establish the circumstances around the woman's death, LancsLive reports.

In a statement, Lancashire Police said: "We were called at 10.20pm yesterday (Aug 10th) to a report of a concern for welfare of a woman.

Article continues below

"Ten minutes later at 10.30pm we received another call after a motorist driving towards Blackpool on the M55 reported seeing what they believed was a body on the hard shoulder of the motorway.

"Officers attended the scene, between junctions 1 and 2 near to the Broughton interchange, where very sadly we can confirm they found the body of a woman. Enquiries are ongoing into the circumstances.

"The motorway was closed for around five hours."

News.title: Strictly Come Dancing announces John Nellis as 14th star joining BBC line-up
News.content:
Strictly Come Dancing announces John Nellis as 14th star joining BBC line-up

Strictly Come Dancing has revealed that John Nellis has officially joined the line-up for the upcoming series, joining an Olympian, an EastEnders legend and even Kim Kardashian's close friend

View 4 Images Social media star John Nellis has signed up for Strictly Come Dancing

John Nellis has been announced as the 14th contestant for Strictly Come Dancing. The star social media star will be taking to the dancefloor later this year in a newly revamped edition of the BBC dancing programme, with Johannes Radebe, Josh Widdecombe and Emma Willis fronting the show for the first time.

‌



YouTube star John said: "I'm still in disbelief that I've been selected for Strictly and, if I'm honest, I'm a little nervous as I've never danced before! It's such an incredible opportunity, and I'm going to throw myself into every moment. I can't wait to meet everyone, learn a new skill, and, hopefully, be much better at family parties by the end of it!"

‌



Former air traffic control officer John left his job to take on content creation full-time. Since then, he's rapidly become one of the leading stars in his field, having won Sport Creator of the Year at the 2024 TikTok Awards UK and Ireland.

‌



4 View 4 Images John quit his job in air traffic control to persue being a full time YouTuber (Image: FIFA via Getty Images) 4 View 4 Images The online star has amassed over 20 million followers (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Over the course of his career, he's amassed a combined audience of over 20 million followers and billions of views. His videos have even featured the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappé.

The creator, originally from Newcastle, County Down, has travelled across the world for his job, collaborating with the likes of Erling Haaland, with his video amassing more than 60 million combined views.

But the news hasn't gone down too well with fans. One said: "Who are these people it's not celebrities." While a second went on to write: "Worst line up in years and I'm normally not the one complaining about the line up." "Are they limited on actual celebrities this year!!?" asked a third. "I love Strictly but damn they are scraping that barrel for all they are worth this year," fumed a third.

‌



However, the news did go down well with the Strictly pros. Dianne Buswell exclaimed: "Welcome to Strictly," alongside a clapping emoji. Amy Dowden wrote: "Welcome x." Shirley Ballas added: "Welcome @johnnellis," alongside a red heart emoji. Motsi Mabuse gushed: "Welcome to Strictly," alongside two red hearts and a fire emoji.

The announcement comes just days after Team GB Olympian Tabby Stoecker was announced as a contestant. The athlete who won gold at this year's 2026 Winter Olympic Games, and recently joined BBC's Gladiators, said of her decision to join: "I am over the moon to be joining the cast of Strictly 2026.

‌



"I've had the wildest year of my life so far, so to be rounding it off with a childhood dream of dancing in the Strictly ballroom is surreal, and I can't wait to get stuck in!"

While Tabby only made her debut in the sports five years ago, she's gone on to take home some incredible trophies, including being a World Cup race winner, a European Championship medallist and a double World Champion medallist.

View 4 Images He joins Olympian Tabby Stoecker (Image: BBC Studios/PA Wire)

‌



When she scored the historic gold medal earlier this year, Tabby was partnered with Matt West in what was the inaugural mixed team skeleton event. For Tabby, the news comes in the same week that she was announced as joining the Gladiators lineup, which is currently being filmed in Sheffield.

Elsewhere, Emmerdale's Lawrence Robb, who plays Mackenzie Boyd on the ITV soap opera, has also been announced. Speaking about joining the show, the actor said: "I don't know who’s more excited about this, me or my Mother.

"I can't quite believe that I am going to be getting my dancing shoes on this September on one of my favourite shows of all time! It's a dream come true, and I can't wait to bring my all to the ballroom. Wish me luck, and any advice is very welcome - trust me, I'll need it!"

‌



Graeme 'The Dogfather' Hall has also been confirmed as a star who is best known for sharing advice and caring tips for dogs said: "I can't believe I am joining the cast of Strictly for 2026.

"I have always loved dancing, so to have the opportunity to learn from the best in the business is a dream come true. I have watched the show for years, so to be a part of it feels like a very exciting challenge, albeit more than a bit nerve-wracking! I can't wait to get started. Bring it on!"

Elsewhere, former footballer Shaun Wright-Phillips, Lacey Turner, House of the Dragon's Bethany Antonia, actress Jaime Winestone, Dany Dyer, Cach Mercer, Delta Goodrem and Chris Appleton will also be showcasing their best moves when Strictly returns.

News.title: Amber Met Office extreme heat warning issued as temperatures could reach 38C
News.content:
The Met Office has issued a rare amber weather warning for extreme heat, external for parts of England on Thursday, where temperatures could peak at 38C.

The highest temperatures will be in parts of the east, south-east and the Midlands and may lead to impacts on transport, infrastructure and health.

The last time we saw temperatures above 36C in August was 2020 when 36.4C was recorded at Heathrow and Kew Gardens.

The Met Office warning runs from 0900 BST until 2359 on Thursday, which is when the summer's latest heatwave reaches its peak.

If the temperature does hit 38C, it would equal this year's top temperature of 38C recorded at Lingwood in Norfolk on 26 June.

News.title: Councils to get more powers to stop vape and betting shops, PM announces
News.content:
New vape shops will require planning permission and councils will get more powers to block new betting shops, under government plans aimed at improving high streets.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said town centres had been "hollowed out" by decades of decline and "for many people, the high streets they grew up with have become unrecognisable".

BBC News has exposed organised crime on high streets across the country, revealing shops selling illegal cigarettes and vapes, selling cannabis and cocaine, enabling illegal working and suspected money-laundering.

The Conservatives and Reform said the proposals would lead to "more empty" shops, without tax relief for other small businesses.

Burnham said the measures will give councils more power to control what businesses open in town centres.

The proposals come as the prime minister embarks on a tour of the UK, with Downing Street saying he will be in "listening mode" during his visits as he works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

The plans announced by the government include:

Changes to planning law which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open (England only)

Tightening the definition of a vape shop to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer (England only)

Scrapping a rule known as "aim to permit", which currently restricts councils' ability to refuse new betting shops and 24-hour slot machine shops (Great Britain-wide)

Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines (England only)

New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops found to be selling illegal tobacco or up to twelve months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer (England and Wales)

The National Crime Agency (NCA) estimates that at least Â£1bn of criminal cash is laundered through high street stores in the UK each year through businesses connected to the sale of fake goods, tax evasion, illegal working and illegal drug supply.

Burnham said "the rise of vape shops, betting shops and rogue operators have replaced the shops, services, and community spaces that people are crying out for".

He added: "That's not on. I said we would improve Britain's high streets, and that's exactly what we are starting to do.

"We're putting communities back in control and giving local people a real say over what opens on their high street."

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday that many people were frustrated at vape and gambling outlets "popping up even near schools and some of them are linked to illegal activity and crime".

News.title: 'I started in my 20s and made £8,000': Why women are often better investors than men
News.content:
It can be "largely attributed to culture", according to Gillian Fleming, co-founder and managing director of UK-based Mint Ventures, a women-led angel investment firm.

"Men historically have been more likely to make family investment decisions, and women have also historically not owned the balance of wealth, but that is changing now," she says.

"Also, money and wealth creation is not a topic that women often discuss, and we would like to change that."

Teleri says she has noticed a shift of late. "Investing is definitely something that women are talking about more, which is always a good thing," she says. "That's the case with my friendship group."

When women do invest in stocks and shares, analysis by Fidelity International found that over three years its female personal investing customers recorded cumulative returns of 50%, compared with 47% for men. The analysis does not identify the reason for the difference, but why may it be the case?

One possible clue to women's slightly higher long-term returns lies in how often they buy and sell their investments, with Barclays data showing that women trade around half as frequently as men.

News.title: Perseid meteor shower reaches peak: When and where to catch a glimpse
News.content:
The best annual meteor shower has once again returned to our skies, and the Perseids dazzling display is set to peak on Wednesday night.

But skywatchers will be treated to not one, but two, impressive astronomical events within just a few hours of each other.

A deep partial solar eclipse will be also visible in the UK in the early evening before the Sun sets and the stars emerge. While the two events are unrelated, their timing makes for an exceptional night of stargazing.

Astronomer Dr Becky Smethurst said it was "the perfect cosmic coincidence of events".

Here is when to look up and where you will have the best views of the meteor shower.

News.title: Call with No 10 gives us hope, PC Harper's mother says
News.content:
Cole and Bowers were sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter in 2020. Under changes to the Sentencing Act made this year, they will become eligible for release from custody next January.

They are in a category of prisoners - those who have committed certain serious violent or sexual crimes - who until now would have had to serve at least two-thirds of their sentence in jail before being considered for release.

Downing Street had earlier warned it would not be possible to exclude "one or two offenders" convicted of manslaughter from the early release scheme.

However, the BBC has been told that Burnham has now instructed his justice secretary to find a way to exclude Cole and Bowers from the scheme designed to ease prison overcrowding.

In a later statement, the PM said he was "increasingly confident" that work to increase space in the prison system "will allow us to reduce the number of people released early".

He added: "And, in the case of the most serious offenders like those convicted of the killing of PC [Andrew] Harper, prevent their early release altogether."

Adlam said the conflicting reports had been making her "more and more angry" and the uncertainty had left her family "in turmoil".

Of the phone call she received, she said. "I think the fact it's actually come from Downing Street, I've got to try and have some faith in it, but at the same time I've got to protect my own feelings."

Thames Valley Police officer PC Harper, 28, from Wallingford, Oxfordshire, died in 2019 when he was dragged behind the getaway car of three teenagers who had fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

Adlam said: "Everybody is watching this. This is obviously extremely personal to us but it's to do with the country as a whole really. This is really vital to get right, it feels like a hash, like a rush job."

Speaking about Cole and Bowers, she added: "They weren't given extreme sentences and I'm only asking for them to do what they were given, I'm not asking for anything more than they were sentenced."

News.title: Trump says it would be 'terrible mistake' to remove Infantino
News.content:
US President Donald Trump says it would be a "terrible mistake" if under-pressure Fifa president Gianni Infantino was ousted from his position.

Trump's backing followed Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) issuing an open letter accusing Infantino of breaking trust "through deception" with his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

Trump's comments mark the first time he has come out in defence of Infantino since the FFE plans came to light on 28 July.

"Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino," Trump wrote on social media.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again."

The 2026 World Cup was co-hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico this summer, with Spain crowned champions after beating Argentina in the final.

When addressing the FFE proposals for the first time on 31 July, Trump said he had not spoken to Infantino about the plans.

Thrive Eternal was expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE.

Thrive is an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner - the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared.

Infantino has a close relationship with Trump and awarded him the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize in December 2025.

News.title: Antisemitism towards Jewish children 'shocking', government expert tells BBC
News.content:
Headteachers of some Jewish schools are spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than on educational matters, a review into antisemitism in schools and colleges has found.

Sir David Bell, speaking for the first time about his ongoing government-commissioned independent review, told the BBC he had been struck by how many leaders of Jewish faith schools had told him security was their main concern - and that "sometimes education takes second place to that".

The extent of antisemitism directed at children and young people was "shocking" he said.

The report, due ithis autumn, examines experiences of Jewish pupils and staff in faith and secular schools and colleges in England.

Sir David said he found that pupils were "subject to regular harassment and abuse".

He said Jewish children and young people "are facing a pressure - and indeed one might say even a crisis - that is not the experience of other communities in this country".

The review is likely to recommend dedicated training for all teachers and improved education about antisemitism for pupils, the BBC has been told.

The BBC has spoken to several headteachers and staff at Jewish schools. All asked not to be named because of concerns over their security and that of their schools.

One headteacher said: "In recent years [security] has become an overwhelming priority and increased a significant amount. There have been weeks where approximately 90% of my time has been spent on security-related matters.

"Security concerns can become one of the many things that headteachers carry with them beyond the school day and, quite literally, can be among the things that keep me awake at night."

News.title: England set to eliminate hepatitis C
News.content:
Hepatitis C is spread through contact with blood infected with the virus, such as by sharing needles with someone who has it.

Donor blood is already screened for it.

It is a silent disease, meaning people often have no symptoms until much later.

Untreated, it can cause serious and potentially life-threatening liver damage.

NHS England says that since 2015, more than 100,000 people have been diagnosed and treated for hepatitis C, meaning the country is already meeting that target.

Another goal - a 65% reduction in hepatitis C-related mortality compared with 2015 levels - has yet to be met, but might be before the 2030 target date.

Around 50,200 adults are living with hepatitis C, figures for England in 2024 suggest.

Estimates indicate 84.6% of those living with hepatitis C have been diagnosed - just short of the 90% target.

The Hepatitis C Trust says England is "on the cusp" of one of the most significant public health achievements in our country's history.

Prof Frankie Swords, NHS national medical director, added: "England is now leading the world in the mission to eliminate this disease and on course to beat the WHO's 2030 target, but we are determined to keep up the momentum and finish the job.

"We are committed to finding and treating everyone who needs support and would urge those at greater risk to come forward by ordering a free and confidential home-testing kit online."

Adults born in Ukraine, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Albania, Lithuania, Bulgaria, Czechia or Slovakia are particularly urged to test, as some may have been infected through medical or dental procedures before 1991.

People can order a free, confidential NHS home self-testing kit, external without needing to speak to a GP.

News.title: GB's Hunt comes of age with European 100m gold
News.content:
Amy Hunt had her coming of age moment as she stormed to 100m glory to claim her first senior international title and deliver Britain's first gold medal of the European Athletics Championships.

Hunt announced herself on the sport's global stage last year with world 200m silver in Tokyo - the first individual international medal of her senior career.

Having backed that up with Commonwealth 100m silver two weeks ago, the 24-year-old would not be denied gold this time in Birmingham.

"I have had such a string of silvers and I was starting to get a bit fed up with it, so I thought it was time for gold," Hunt, who won in 11 seconds flat, told BBC Sport.

"My parents gifted me these gold earrings to finally level up, because I wear all-silver jewellery.

"They said it was time for gold - they left me that note two nights ago - so it made me quite emotional.

"It was definitely time for me to come of age here."

It was Britain's second medal on the opening day of action after the hosts took silver in the mixed 4x400m relay.

Yemi Mary John held off Dutch athlete Myrte van der Schoot on the home straight to bring a British quartet also featuring Ben Jefferies, Charlotte Henrich and Toby Harries home in three minutes 10.47 seconds, behind winners Norway (3:09.62).

News.title: London Heathrow no longer Europe's busiest airport
News.content:
Heathrow has lost its position as Europe's busiest airport to Istanbul, new figures show.

The west London airport said 7.86m passengers passed through its four terminals in July, whereas Istanbul Airport in Turkey's largest city recorded 8.15m passengers.

The US-Israel conflict with Iran has had an impact on Heathrow's passenger traffic with Middle East routes in July down 20.2% year-on-year.

Annual figures from trade body Airports Council International show Heathrow was Europe's busiest airport from 1996 to 2019. It lost that title in 2020 amid coronavirus travel restrictions before regaining it in 2023, holding it ever since.

Heathrow continues to operate its two runways at near-full capacity and is seeking government permission to build a third.

News.title: Cocaine worth £232m found in banana shipment
News.content:
Cocaine with a street value of Â£232m was discovered hidden in a large shipment of bananas from South America.

The 2.9-tonne (2,900kg) haul was smuggled into London Gateway Port in Thurrock, Essex, on Thursday.

Border Force intercepted the cocaine at the port and removed it from a trailer, before the drugs courier took the empty load to an address near Buntingford, Hertfordshire.

Nine men allegedly connected to the bust were then arrested and later released on bail.

Border Force had been tipped off about the illegal consignment by the National Crime Agency.

News.title: Treasury contributed to woman's death, inquest hears
News.content:
The death of a Treasury worker who took her own life the day after a meeting with her managers was "materially contributed" to by her employers, an inquest has heard.

Chloe Moffat, 26, a personal assistant to a Treasury director, died on 20 May last year, after she was told of allegations she had shared sensitive confidential information about colleagues, which she denied.

Surrey Coroner's Court heard the Treasury did not apply written disciplinary policy which would have made clear that if the allegations were proven, the likely penalty was a written warning, not dismissal.

A spokesperson for the Treasury said it was "considering the findings carefully".

In a statement to the press, Moffat's family said they believed the Treasury failed in its duty of care.

"When she needed support, reassurance and fair treatment, she was left frightened, isolated and convinced her career and reputation had been destroyed," they added.

The inquest, in which a conclusion of suicide was recorded, heard that on 19 May Moffat went to what she thought was a routine one-to-one with her line manager, but a more senior manager was also present.

She was told of allegations she had shared sensitive personal information about colleagues, obtained as part of her job.

Moffat, from London, denied this.

News.title: Vandals target playground before it has even opened
News.content:
A play area that cost more than Â£178,000 was vandalised days before it was due to open.

Knowsley Council leader Graham Morgan said he was "absolutely furious" that every piece of play equipment at the Finch Woods play park in Halewood, Knowsley had been spray painted with graffiti over the weekend.

Trees and safety surfacing were also damaged and rubbish was left strewn across the site, with the cost of the damage estimated to run into thousands of pounds.

Morgan condemned the "mindless vandalism", saying "it is the cost to the community that sickens me the most".

News.title: Antiques stolen in 16th Century manor house raid
News.content:
More than 20 antiques were stolen from a National Trust (NT) property during a break-in last month, it has been revealed.

The silver, pewter and brass items were taken from the 16th Century manor house at Baddesley Clinton in Warwickshire, on 30 July.

The most notable piece of the 25 taken was a Georgian silver salver engraved with the coat of arms of the Ferrers, the family who resided at the house for about five centuries, the NT said.

"We very much hope the objects will be returned, so they can be enjoyed by everyone," a spokesperson added.

News.title: Great-grandad with cancer risks his health to help others on 460-mile journey
News.content:
A great-grandfather with bladder and kidney cancer is walking 462 miles (743km) for charity, despite knowing it could impact his own treatment.

John Eryl Parry, 78, from Pontypool, Torfaen, began his coast-to-coast journey at the UK's most easterly point in Lowestoft, Suffolk, on 21 June, and is due to reach St David's Head in Pembrokeshire on 11 August.

He found out he had cancer after he fell off a ladder and was taken to hospital.

John admitted he had not told his oncology team about his challenge, but said he was warned by a doctor that his body would "change" during it, and it could impact his treatment plan.

News.title: MSP apologises for hurt caused by rape 'demonisation' comments
News.content:
A newly-elected MSP has apologised for the hurt caused by comments in which they talked of the "demonisation" of rape.

Scottish Green Party politician Q Manivannan has also faced criticism for suggesting rape is a "spectrum of things" during a podcast recorded before they were elected to the Scottish Parliament.

Earlier, the Scottish Rape Crisis Alliance (SRCA) - which represents four rape crisis centres - said there is "no hierarchy of rape" and warned the MSP not to minimise sexual violence.

In a statement, Manivannan said clips from the podcast had been "selectively edited" but said they were "sorry" for the upset, and insisted they would never seek to diminish a rape survivor's experience.

The comments, which were made during The Subjective Space podcast , externalrecorded last year, sparked fury after they re-emerged online at the weekend.

News.content:

The prime minister has vowed to resolve the “long-running injustice” of indefinite jail terms as part of measures to ease prison overcrowding and stop PC Andrew Harper’s killers from being freed early.

Andy Burnham said he is “increasingly confident” that plans to free up prison cells will mean the number of prisoners being released early can be reduced.

Options being considered include the release of “lower risk” prisoners serving Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) jail terms, he said on Tuesday. The comments offer fresh hope for prisoners trapped on the open-ended sentences which were outlawed in 2012.

The Independent has long campaigned for the unjust jail terms - which have left thousands languishing without hope of release - to be reviewed.

open image in gallery Burnham said IPP sentences were a ‘long-running injustice’ ( PA Wire )

In a statement issued on Facebook, he said he has asked justice secretary Alex Norris to fast-track a plan to create more headroom in the prison estate.

The plan will be based “on a range of options”, Mr Burnham said, including “increasing the rate of removal of foreign national offenders from the prison estate to their country of origin; finding an early resolution to the long-running injustice of IPP sentences, which could allow for the release of lower-risk prisoners; and making greater use of the entire prison estate including using the female estate for male offenders”.

He continued: “I am increasingly confident that a more focused approach along these lines will allow us to reduce the number of people released early and, in the case of the most serious offenders like those convicted of the killing of PC Harper, prevent their early release altogether.”

The development comes as the government faces legal action over the jail terms after the United Nations found Britain is unlawfully detaining a number of over-tariff IPP prisoners in a scathing legal opinion issued last month.

open image in gallery PC Andrew Harper was killed while on duty in 2019 ( Thames Valley Police )

The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention called for Britain to urgently act in relation to five men handed the jail terms, warning their imprisonment long beyond their original tariff amounts to arbitrary detention under international human rights law and they are entitled to compensation.

Lawyers are now preparing to submit a rare habeas corpus legal challenge to the High Court, which will force the government to justify the prisoners' continued incarceration to senior judges.

The open-ended punishments were scrapped in 2012, but not retrospectively, leaving thousands languishing in prison without a release date for years beyond their tariff, including some for minor crimes. Once released, many find themselves trapped in a cycle of indefinite recall for minor breaches of strict licence conditions.

The architect of the flawed sentence, Lord David Blunkett, has since admitted that ushering in the draconian punishments under Tony Blair’s Labour government is his “biggest regret”.

In 2022, the cross-party justice committee inquiry found the sentences were “irredeemably flawed” and called for all IPP prisoners to be resentenced. Despite 96 people taking their own lives in custody after losing hope of release, successive governments have so far refused.

open image in gallery Clockwise from top: Wayne Williams, Leroy Douglas, Josh Mcrae, Shaun Lloyd and Abdullahi Suleman ( Supplied )

Four of the five cases condemned by the UN are still incarcerated, including Leroy Douglas, who has served almost 20 years without release for street robbery of a mobile phone; Abdullahi Suleman, who is still in custody 20 years after he was handed an IPP for a laptop robbery; Wayne Williams, who has spent more than 19 years in prison without release for a 23-month jail term for attempting to injure a police officer in a fight; and Shaun Lloyd, 39, who was recently hauled back to prison for the fifth time, having served more than 12 years for two street robberies.

Sadly, Joshua Mcrae, died in prison aged 34, having served more than 16 years for a four-year tariff for grievous bodily harm.

They are among almost 2,300 people still in prison on the controversial jail terms.

This week the chair of the Criminal Cases Review Commission, Dame Vera Baird, joined calls for the government to take “wholesale” action to address the scandal. Judges have recently quashed a string of indefinite sentences handed to children and young men and the CCRC is reviewing hundreds more.

Following Mr Burnham’s comments, Dame Vera, who is also a former victims’ commissioner, said debate around the early release scheme had brought an urgency to solving the problem.

“We are harming a lot of people with a leftover that international human rights institutions have condemned as torture,” she told The Independent.

“The CCRC is working as fast as possible to send cases to the Court of Appeal following some recent hopeful precedents from them, but, as multiple agencies have said, the way to grip the issue is to embark on a re-sentencing exercise. I imagine the complexities of working that through have played a role in deterring ministers.

“However, given the problems in the early release scheme, there are now two reasons to tackle IPP's, since many people are likely to be freed, creating much needed space in the prison system.”

Labour peer Shami Chakrabarti, the former director of Liberty, added: “It is extremely positive to see a prime minister personally trying to grip our long-term prison crisis. The scandal of IPP prisoners in particular- still taking up prison places long after they should have been released based on the seriousness of their offending, is one that should be urgently ended.”

Housebuilder Bellway has called for the Government to cut stamp duty immediately to help support a recovery in the UK property market.

It came as the FTSE 250 firm warned that demand is “uncertain” in the short term amid continued pressure from rising building costs and caution among consumers.

The Newcastle-based company is among housing firms to have seen demand for new homes dented by elevated mortgage costs and pressure on consumer finances.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham last month ruled out a major overhaul of stamp duty at the Autumn Budget.

open image in gallery Prime Minister Andy Burnham (left) sits next to Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey during a National Economic Council meeting at No 10 North, located in Heron House, central Manchester (Christopher Furlong/PA) ( PA Wire )

However, Bellway chief executive Jason Honeyman said action is needed to reinvigorate the housing market and help support potential new homeowners.

“With the near-term outlook remaining uncertain, we call on the Government to act now to improve access to housing across all tenures, both by helping first-time buyers onto the property ladder and supporting the delivery of affordable and social housing for those who need it most,” he said.

“In order to ease affordability constraints and stimulate demand, an immediate reduction in stamp duty alongside a Government-backed deposit support scheme for first-time buyers would both drive economic growth and accelerate the delivery of much-needed new homes across the country.”

On Tuesday, the company reported that housing competition grew by 10.8% to 9,695 homes over the year to July 31, compared with a year earlier.

It also revealed that underlying operating profits are set to have increased to around £320 million from £303.5 million last year.

Bellway said it saw positive trading in the early part of the spring selling season, but has seen a “moderation” in customer demand since April due to the uptick in mortgage rates.

Mr Honeyman added: “Bellway has delivered a robust performance and growth in volume output, despite ongoing headwinds for our industry.

“Our sharp focus on operational improvement and drive for capital efficiency has provided resilience and supported a strong increase in cash generation and shareholder returns.”

The bout marks Makhachev’s first defence of the belt, which he won by dominating and outpointing Jack Della Maddalena in November, after giving up the lightweight belt following a record-breaking four successful defences.

And the Russian, 34, faces an intriguing test against the divisive Machado Garry, 28, who enters the fight with just one professional loss to his name.

The price of gold has been on the rise once more, reversing a months-long downward trend which saw the precious metal’s value fall by more than a quarter.

Investors have had a tough time predicting what markets will do this year, with uncertainty from the Iran war hitting inflation, currency markets remaining volatile and and growing concerns over the amounts the largest firms are spending on artificial intelligence.

In such times, previously investors might have turned to gold, seen as a safe haven in troubled times - but instead, the precious metal appeared to mirror some of those other markets with a steep decline in the first half of 2026.

Gold hit an all-time record price of more than $5,600 (£4,147) per ounce in late January. Through to mid-March it still traded at above $5,000 - but across the following five months it fell to a few dollars below $4,000, more than a 28 per cent drop from high point to low.

However, since the start of August it has started to rally once more, up 8 per cent over the past week alone to sit at $4,373.

“One of the stranger developments of recent days has been the pick-up in precious metals. After two months of outflows, gold ETFs attracted inflows in July, and the price of gold increased by more than 7 per cent last week,” said Jemma Slingo, investment expert at Fidelity International.

“It is tricky to pin down exactly what is driving the bounce, which follows a tough few months for gold. The metal did not behave like a traditional safe haven during the early stages of the Middle East conflict, but the changing outlook for interest rates could be moving the dial. If the last year is anything to go by, however, investors should be prepared for a bumpy ride.”

Interest rates potentially moving up in the US and beyond - analysts are split over the Bank of England’s likely movement - can decrease the likelihood of people buying gold, as it is easier to get a return from holding cash because gold pays no dividend.

Labour has overtaken Reform UK in yet another poll, as the party continues to see a surge in support after Andy Burnham entered Downing Street.

The latest YouGov survey put Labour on 24 points, two points ahead of Nigel Farage’s party on 22 per cent – the first time a YouGov poll has put Labour ahead of Reform in more than a year.

It is also Reform’s lowest score since March 2025, with the party losing ground to the Conservatives.

The latest survey is the fifth national poll Labour has topped since Mr Burnham became prime minister, ending the run that saw Mr Farage’s party lead in the polls for more than a year.

open image in gallery Labour continues to see a surge in support after Andy Burnham entered Downing Street ( AFP/Getty )

The polling put the Green Party on 12 per cent, down by one point compared to August 2-3, while the Liberal Democrats were also down by one point on 11 per cent.

The Tories were up two points, putting them on 21 per cent - just one point behind Reform.

The polling will come as another blow to Mr Farage’s party as they spend their final few days campaigning in a crucial by-election in Clacton.

The Reform leader dramatically quit as an MP earlier this summer – before Labour’s ‘Burnham bounce’ in the polls – and could find himself left without a seat in Parliament if he fails to win on Thursday.

When Sir Keir Starmer stood down in June, just 49 per cent of voters who backed the Labour Party at the last general election said they still backed the party. This has now risen to 60 per cent in the latest poll.

Meanwhile, the number of Labour voters who said they would lend their vote to the Greens has fallen from 9 per cent in June to just 8 per cent, the polling commissioned by The Times has found.

Anthony Wells, head of politics and elections for YouGov, told the newspaper that Mr Burnham has gone some way to reunite the left.

open image in gallery The polling will come as a blow to Nigel Farage ( PA Wire )

"What you see in the numbers is not only that Labour has increased its vote share but both the Greens and the Liberal Democrats have seen a substantial drop in their support, which had been boosted by Labour defectors,” he said.

“At the same time there are signs that, for the moment at least, Reform has peaked and is now losing some of the support it picked up from disaffected Tory voters who are now returning to Kemi Badenoch.

“However, more broadly the polls shows that the public are still deeply divided, with just three points separating the top three parties — which is within the margin or error.”

It comes just one day after an Ipsos poll put Mr Burnham’s party on 28 per cent, three points ahead of Reform on 25 per cent, Labour’s best position in an Ipsos poll for more than a year.

The survey also found Mr Burnham has a significant lead over his political rivals including Mr Farage, when asked who would make the best PM.

Some 36 per cent chose the Labour leader, more than double the 15 per cent who picked Mr Farage or the 13 per cent who selected Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch.

The YouGov polling spoke to 2,417 adults on August 9 and 10.

News.title: Man killed in shooting outside London pub
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

A man has died after a shooting outside a pub in London.

Emergency services were called to Landor Road outside the Landor Pub in Clapham, southwest London, just before 10pm on Monday evening, according to London Ambulance Servuce (LAS).

Paramedics arrived within three minutes, but said a man was later pronounced dead at the scene.

Pictures show a visible police presence outside the pub on Tuesday morning, with a white forensics tent in place.

The exact circumstances surrounding the incident are not yet clear.

A London Ambulance Service spokesperson said: “We were called at 9:59pm on Monday 10 August to reports of a shooting on Landor Road, SW9.

“We sent resources to the scene including an ambulance crew, an incident response officer and paramedics in fast response cars. We also dispatched a trauma team in a car from London's Air Ambulance.

“Our first paramedics arrived in three minutes. Sadly, despite the best efforts of our crews, a man was pronounced dead at the scene.”

The Independent has approached the Metropolitan Police for comment.

This is a breaking story. More to follow...

News.content:
