Europe is bracing for another scorching heatwave set to sweep across the continent, once again driving up the threat of devastating wildfires.

Spain could see temperatures as high as 42C later this week in what will be Europe’s fifth heatwave of a record-breaking summer, which has seen several countries suffer a record-breaking number of fires due to persistent dry conditions and extreme heat.

France and Italy will also see scorching temperatures, before the heatwave moves eastwards into Central and Eastern Europe, with temperatures set to near the 40s in Hungary, Serbia and Romania early next week.

The extreme heat has led to 25,000 related deaths this year, according to Bloomberg research covering Spain, France, the UK, the Netherlands and Switzerland. Wildfires have scorched more than 550,000 hectares of land across the continent during the same period.

open image in gallery Western Europe will see scorching temperatures as high as 43C on Thursday ( Ventusky.com )

Western Europe is in the midst of its hottest ever summer, with a record-breaking 24-hour average temperature of 21.62 degrees for June and July recorded this year, according to a report the EU’s Copernicus climate change service released on Monday.

This is 2.79C above the average temperature during the 1991 to 2020 period, smashing the previous heat record set in 2022.

Spanish forecaster Aemet says that tourist hotspots in Spain including Cordoba (42C), Sevilla (40C), Granada (39C), and Madrid (39C) will all see temperatures in the region of 40C on Thursday, while other touristy areas including Barcelona, Malaga and Alicante are all forecast to be in the low-to-mid 30s in the coming days.

Large parts of Spain, barring the eastern, southern and northwestern coasts, will be placed under yellow and amber warnings for the next three days.

open image in gallery Spain will experience scorching temperatures, especially on Thursday ( Ventusky.com )

France will see temperatures in the mid-to-high 30s, Meteo-France says, including in Paris (35C), Toulouse (36C) and Bordeaux (39C), which was the site of a vast wildfire last month that forced 200,000 people from their homes.

Meteo-France has placed much of the country’s south east under an amber heatwave warning, with the rest of the country, barring the north, under a yellow warning. On Wednesday, almost the entire country will be under an amber warning, other northern areas.

Last Thursday, all 27 Italian cities that are monitored through the Health Ministry’s national heat surveillance system were placed on red alert.

In the next three days, Rome (38C), Milan (37C), Florence (37C) and parts of central Sardinia (40C) will be among the hottest parts of Italy in the coming week, Italy’s Meteo Agency said.

It comes after Slovakia recorded a temperature 42.2C, becoming the latest country, including Hungary and Austria, to set an all time record.

open image in gallery France has suffered several intense heatwaves in 2026, causing thousands of excess deaths ( Ventusky.com )

open image in gallery Italy's Health Ministry put 27 cities on red alert last week ( Ventusky.com )

Greece, which earlier this month was battered by dramatic wildfires in which several people were killed, is set to avoid the worst of the upcoming heatwave, with temperatures not expected to surpass the mid-30s.

Three consecutive months of exceptional heat in western Europe are the result of persistent high-pressure systems which have trapped heat over the region, a weather event also known as a ‘heat dome’, said Dr Samantha Burgess, deputy director of the Copernicus Climate Change Service.

Half of England and Wales have already been plunged into drought, with more regions likely to be declared on Monday afternoon when officials meet at the National Drought Group, before temperatures soar as high as 36C later this week.

open image in gallery Greece battled huge wildfires earlier this month ( Reuters )

“The extreme temperatures also amplified widespread drought,” said Dr Burgess. “As soils dry out, they lose their ability to provide natural cooling, allowing heat to build more readily. This is a clear example of how climate change is intensifying heat extremes, with heat and drought increasingly reinforcing one another.”

Eastern Europe is also currently in the grip of an intense heatwave, with temperatures as high as 36C in Serbia and Hungary on Tuesday, and set to hit 38C on Tuesday.

After a brief midweek reprieve, scorching temperatures will return to Croatia, Hungary, Serbia and Romania this weekend, as most of France and Spain cool into the mid-to-low 30s.

Some parts of Hungary, Romania and Serbia - particularly around the borders where the three countries meet - are also bracing for an ‘extreme danger’ of wildfires this week, according to the Copernicus European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS).

open image in gallery A firefighter battles a wildfire in Deliblatska Pescara (Deliblato Sands), near the village of Dubovac, some 70 kilometres northeast of Belgrade, Serbia ( AFP/Getty )

The danger will peak on Wednesday, after a spell of extreme high temperatures this week. Towards the end of the week, large parts of Spain and patches of France will be under ‘extreme’ and ‘very high’ wildfire danger warnings.

“Climate change is increasingly bringing the kinds of hot and dry conditions that favour large, high-intensity wildfires in southern Europe while extending the fire season northwards,” said Laurence Rouil, director of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) at ECMWF.

“Larger fires produce more smoke and inject it higher into the atmosphere, meaning it can travel further and impact air quality not only locally, but across the wider region.

open image in gallery Much of the continent remains at risk of further wildfires, AccuWeather warns ( AccuWeather )

“Countries that experience relatively few wildfires may be increasingly impacted by long range transport of smoke, even if they are thousands of kilometres away.”

The threat from wildfires in western Europe far from over, with vast swathes of the continent under extreme wildfire warnings, as experts warn that the wildfire season is increasing in length and intensity each year.

In France and Spain, more than 300,000 people were forced to flee their homes, in an evacuation operation that now ranks among the largest the continent has seen since World War II.

The fires have already cost the continent up to £16.4 billion in economic costs, estimates published by forecaster AccuWeather showed on Thursday. This includes the cost of emergency response, damage to property, and health impacts.

The cumulative number of wildfires in France, Spain and Italy this year dwarfs the average from the previous two decades, figures from Copernicus’ European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) show.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

Sports.title: David Beckham tipped to reunite greatest strikeforce ever at Inter Miami as Neymar’s contract winds down
Sports.content:
DAVID BECKHAM could pull off football’s ultimate reunion by bringing Neymar to Inter Miami to revive the legendary MSN strikeforce

The Brazilian superstar could be heading for a blockbuster reunion with Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez, with former Brazil midfielder Felipe Melo claiming he has been told Neymar will move to Miami when his Santos contract expires.



Speaking on YouTube, Melo said: “I talked to a friend of mine who passed me some news about Santos before. He told me Neymar is going to play in Miami. Starting in January, Neymar is going to Miami.

“If it happens, I was the first one to break the news here. Let’s wait and see what happens.”



Neymar’s future has become one of the biggest talking points in world football, with his Santos contract set to expire on December 31, 2026.

The 34-year-old has been linked with a move to Turkish giants Galatasaray, but Melo’s comments have sparked fresh speculation that Inter Miami could be his next destination.



And if Beckham can make it happen, it would reunite the famous MSN frontline that terrorised Europe with Barcelona.

Messi, Neymar and Suarez formed one of the deadliest strikeforces football has ever seen between 2014 and 2017, combining flair, pace and ruthless finishing.

Together they lifted nine trophies at Barcelona including the Champions League, two La Liga titles and the Club World Cup.

Their first season together produced a historic treble under Luis Enrique, and the trio scored a staggering 122 goals across all competitions.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Messi led the way with 58 goals, Neymar added 39 and Suarez contributed 25 as Barcelona swept aside opponents with one of the most feared attacks in football history.

Now Beckham’s Inter Miami could provide the stage for one final chapter.

Messi and Suarez are already in Florida, while former Barcelona team-mates Sergio Busquets and Jordi Alba have also been part of Miami’s ambitious project.

A Neymar arrival would not only create a mouth-watering reunion on the pitch but would also deliver a huge commercial boost for MLS and Inter Miami.



The biggest question, though, is whether Neymar can still produce at the highest level.

The Brazilian’s career in recent years has been disrupted by injuries, limiting his consistency, although his ability and star power remain unquestionable.

There is currently no agreement between Neymar and Inter Miami, and the forward still has decisions to make about the final years of his career.



But with Messi and Suarez already together, and Neymar potentially available as a free agent, the dream of seeing MSN together again is no longer impossible.

For Beckham, it could be the ultimate statement signing.

The greatest strikeforce of their generation may yet have one more story to tell, this time under the Miami sun.

Sports.title: Dwight McNeil joins Crystal Palace in swap deal after owner Steve Parish held clear-the-air talks with his girlfriend
Sports.content:
CRYSTAL PALACE and Everton have sensationally swapped Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson.

The remarkable deal was completed after Eagles owner Steve Parish held clear-the-air talks with McNeil’s girlfriend.



McNeil, 26, was close to joining Palace in January on an initial loan, which the South Londoners would have been obligated to make permanent for £20million.

The deal dramatically fell through, with the winger’s girlfriend Megan Sharpley subsequently writing a scathing message on social media.



An excerpt of the post read: “We live in a world where everyone is aware of how big a problem mental health is..

“So, in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money and that’s OK to mess and toy with their mental health and that it’s just part of the job?”

According to The Times, Parish spoke to Sharpley ahead of the transfer going through in order to clear the air.

McNeil, 26, subsequently signed a four-year contract at Selhurst Park, with Johnson doing the same at Everton.

Johnson, 25, only joined Palace in a £35million deal in January.

He did not score a single goal in 26 appearances under Oliver Glasner and was left on the bench during the Conference League final.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

After featuring in pre-season under Glasner’s replacement Pierre Sage, Johnson was deemed to surplus to requirements.

McNeil for Johnson is the Premier League’s first official swap deal since 2018.

On that occasion, Arsenal traded Alexis Sanchez for Manchester United‘s Henrikh Mkhitaryan.

McNeil joined Everton from Burnley in 2022 and went on to play 128 times for the Toffees, scoring 15 goals and laying on 19 assists.



Last season his prominence waned, however, and he started just 14 Premier League games.

Johnson, meanwhile, was Tottenham’s Europa League hero just 15 months ago, scoring the winning goal in the final against Man Utd in Bilbao.

The Wales international bagged 18 goals during the 2024-25 season under Ange Postecoglou, but lost his place following the arrivals of Thomas Frank and Mohammed Kudus.

After scoring in Spurs’ opening two Prem games of last season, Johnson did not net again last term.



McNeil and Johnson will quickly reunite with former acquaintances, as Everton host Crystal Palace on the opening day of the Premier League season.

Upon signing for Palace, McNeil said: “I’m really happy to be here, and looking forward to the challenge ahead.

“The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It’s something that I want to be a part of, so I’m really looking forward to getting started.”

Parish, 61, added: “It is wonderful to finally welcome Dwight – a player with proven ability in the Premier League – to South London. I’m looking forward to seeing him in action at Selhurst Park.”



After arriving at Everton, Johnson said: “I’m so excited to be here. The Club speaks for itself – it’s a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.

“There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in.

“You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I’m a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

“I want to come in and show what I can do. The manager spoke to me about getting back to the form that I’ve shown previously, and that’s a massive thing for me – the fact he knows and believes in what I can do.

“For me, listening to him – a manager who is so experienced and someone who has been so successful – it was really nice to hear.



“I want to bring all of my attributes. First and foremost, I’ll work for the team, the fans, and represent the club properly.

“I know that’s something that’s definitely appreciated and a non-negotiable here. They can expect that from me. On top of that, I think I can bring speed, goals and everything I’ve got.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sports.title: Premier League team of the 2020s revealed as Arsenal have chance to climb up table this season
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY have picked up more points than any Premier League side in the 2020s – but Arsenal are threatening to close the gap.

The Gunners were crowned champions for the first time in 22 years last season.



And Arsenal, who splashed the cash on Bruno Guimaraes last week as they aim to defend their crown, have now taken their tally to 494 points from their last 246 top-flight showdowns.

But the North Londoners are still only THIRD in the race to be the best Premier League side since the start of the decade.



City are leading the way with a mammoth 548 points after bagging four titles in the last six seasons.

And the Sky Blues have entered a new era following legendary boss Pep Guardiola’s decision to quit at the end of last term.



City are a whopping 50 points clear at the top of the table – meaning they will remain in the driving seat unless they have a horror campaign.

Liverpool, who have been involved in one more clash than their rivals, are in second place after notching 498 points.

The Merseyside giants were formidable under boss Jurgen Klopp and, having got their hands on the Premier League trophy in 2020, did it again with Arne Slot at the helm.

But Arsenal will move to within one point of Liverpool in the race for the summit if they beat newly-promoted Coventry in their season opener.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Manchester United and Chelsea are the only other sides to have broken the 400-point barrier.

And Aston Villa, who ended their trophy drought by winning the Europa League last term, complete the top six for the 2020s.

Tottenham and Newcastle have accumulated 367 and 359 points respectively.

Brighton, fresh from increasing the capacity at the Amex Stadium, could push to overtake them in the coming months.



West Ham complete the Premier League’s top ten since the start of the decade.

But they will not add to their 315-point haul this season after suffering a shock relegation to the Championship.

Sports.title: Donald Trump says Fifa axing Gianni Infantino would be ‘terrible mistake’ after ‘most successful World Cup ever’
Sports.content:
DONALD TRUMP says axing Gianni Infantino as Fifa president would be a “terrible mistake”.

Infantino, 56, has come under increasing pressure following the collapse of his disgraceful scheme to sell off a chunk of the World Cup to private investors.



Yesterday, Uefa and their Asian and North American counterparts, the AFC and Concacaf, teamed up to release a damning statement against Infantino.

It accused the Swiss football administrator of “breaking trust through deception” and was seen as a call on him to resign.



US president Trump, however, feels that an Infantino Fifa exit would be the wrong move.

The American posted on Truth Social: “FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino.

“He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented.

“If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DJT”.

Infantino and Trump grew their relationship during the build up to the World Cup in North America earlier this summer.

Last December, Infantino controversially awarded Trump with the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He also met Trump at the Oval Office for meetings, with the pair going on to sit together at the World Cup final last month.

Trump’s son-in-law’s brother Joshua Kushner was believed to be the front-runner to buy a stake in the World Cup for $4.2bn (£3.1bn).

But the deal collapsed as the scheme was KO’d amid outrage from the football community, in particular from Uefa, whose nations promised to boycott the World Cup if it went ahead.

Yesterday’s furious statement was co-signed by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, AFC chief Sheikh Salman Bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa and Concacaf boss Victor Montagliani plus their organisations’ general secretaries.



It read: “This is about something more fundamental: the integrity of the game, and the integrity of those elected to lead it.

“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held.

“It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.

“Fifa’s recent letter to its Vice-Presidents and 211 Member Associations acknowledges that mistakes were made in the process.



“It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment.

“A proposal advanced on a compressed timeline, without meaningful consultation, and pushed toward a deadline before Member Associations could properly review its terms is not the product of an oversight — it is the product of a design intended to limit scrutiny.

“It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong.

“There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the Fifa World Cup was a profound failure of judgment — not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions Fifa exists to serve.”



The letter also called for an independent commission to review Fifa’s recent conduct, rather than an internal committee.

And it pointed out that only one election official was part of the Fifa crisis meeting in Morocco last week – with no Fifa Council members or member associations invited to contribute.

SunSport understands Concacaf, Uefa and the AFC are pressurising Infantino to resign with immediate effect and not run for re-election for a fourth term in March.

Fifa released a strong statement of their own last week blasting a “concerted and ongoing effort” to undermine their boss.



It read: “The Fifa President was democratically elected by Fifa’s Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate.

“It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president.

“Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s Member Associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes.

“Fifa welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

On Friday night it was reported that Uefa paid off a six-figure sum to an alleged mistress of married Infantino while he was general secretary, prior to his election as Fifa president in 2016.



And SunSport yesterday revealed that even Infantino’s hometown club Zug 94 in Switzerland are refusing to back his crumbling leadership.

Sports.title: Donald Trump comments are laughable - HE was already Gianni Infantino's big mistake
Sports.content:
With friends like Donald Trump, who needs enemies?

Not that Gianni Infantino is short of those.

But the fact the root cause of Infantino's soiled and stained reputation as FIFA president is now attempting to support him, does nothing but add more fuel to a blazing footballing fire.

As ironies go, Trump offering his backing to his big mate during his darkest hours, is right up there. The startling arrogance of the powerful duo means it might be lost on them both.

‌



But it shouldn't, when it comes those who genuinely love the game in general. Trump insists it would be a "terrible mistake" if Infantino was ousted from his position.

Gianni Infantino cornered as three federations pile pressure on under-fire FIFA boss READ MORE :

"FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino", Trump said.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again."

The US president has waited more than a week to lend his support to someone battling to remain in office.

‌



After UEFA, CONCAF and the Asian Football Federation (AFF) accused the Swiss of breaking trust "through deception", with his aborted proposal to flog the commercial and ticketing rights of future World Cups to private investors.

View 3 Images UEFA have turned on the FIFA president (Image: Getty Images)

Trump discussing the merits of "terrible mistakes" is akin to Lance Armstrong discussing the merits of clean sport.

The greatest mistake Infantino made was getting into bed with Trump in the first place. Repeating the one he made when doing the same with Russia president Vladimir Putin back in 2018.

‌



It's about the company you keep.

Infantino has a close relationship with Trump, and awarded him the inaugural FIFA 'Peace Prize' in December 2025. While the man running the investment group behind Infantino's shameful plan, just happens to be the brother of Trump's son-in-law.

Which makes Trump's support more transparent than water. If someone could name me two men more motivated by money than Trump and Infantino, I'm all ears.

View 3 Images Infantino cosied up to Trump in the Oval Office, before laughably awarding him the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Trump even references the fact in his social media post, claiming a future World Cup would never be as "profitable again" without Infantino.

The truth is, Infantino needs Trump's support like a hole in the head. Because it means nothing, coming from one of the most divisive men ever to walk the planet.

Trump has had a huge role in getting Infantino into this deep hole in the first place. And we must now hope Trump keeps on digging, to the point where his mate cannot ever get out of it.

Aston Villa are set to have a new-look attack next season and have been linked with a high-profile move for Real Madrid forward Endrick

View 2 Images Aston Villa have been linked with a move for Endrick (Image: Hannah Peters - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Aston Villa have been linked with a shock move for Real Madrid star Endrick as Unai Emery continues to reshape his squad. The Villans have previously had a stable side but selling Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers means that fans will be watching a new-look team next season.

‌



Villa capped off their Europa League victory by finishing fourth in the league last term, though success also led clubs to target their key players. The further sale of left-back Lucas Digne to Paris Saint-Germain, plus Amadou Onana sustaining an injury at the World Cup, has forced Villa into a reshuffle.

‌



Joao Gomes is expected to partner Boubacar Kamara in midfield after his £35m move from Wolves. In attack, Villa fans already have reasons to be hopeful after signing Johan Manzambi, who starred for Switzerland at the World Cup, as Rogers’ replacement from Freiburg for an initial £52m. Meanwhile, Emery will be determined to help Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho fulfil his potential.

‌



Villa supporters’ pre-season excitement has been ramped up by the club reportedly expressing interest in a loan move for Endrick, as the Real Madrid forward searches for regular minutes. Spanish publication AS reports that the 20-year-old is listening to loan offers after finding himself down the pecking order at Los Blancos, both as a wide option and a centre-forward.

‌



Endrick flourished as a winger during his recent Lyon loan spell, scoring eight goals and providing eight assists in 21 games. While his versatility could offer Emery another option up front, the Madrid star will also face fierce competition for his spot on the wing from club captain John McGinn. Whether at Endrick’s expense or otherwise, few would bet against the skipper quickly forcing his way back into the team.

Johan Manzambi will take up the mantle of replacing Rogers, who joined Chelsea for an eye-watering £117m, in the attacking midfield role. The Switzerland international, who is currently out injured, faced many of his new team-mates in the Europa League final.

Sports.title: Forgotten ex-Man Utd star reveals Bruno Fernandes gesture that shows his true colours
Sports.content:
Forgotten ex-Man Utd star reveals Bruno Fernandes gesture that shows his true colours

Bruno Fernandes has been a key player for Manchester United since joining the club in 2020 and a former team-mate has spoken about a classy gesture

View 3 Images Brandon Williams says ex-Manchester United colleague Bruno Fernandes still checks up on him (Image: Getty)

Brandon Williams says former Manchester United team-mate Bruno Fernandes still messages him and helps him get match tickets. Williams is currently without a club after leaving Hull City in February.

‌



Since 2023, Fernandes has been United's skipper and for all intents and purposes, the face of the club. But it's not just on the field where he is influential.

‌



Defender Williams, who joined the club's academy ranks at the age of seven, left United in 2024 after the expiration of his contract and has faced legal trouble in the years since. But the 25-year-old is still in contact with some of his former team-mates at Old Trafford and Fernandes in particular showed his class with a kind act.

‌



Williams told The Athletic how Fernandes still keeps in touch with him and arranges match tickets. He said: "That's why he's the captain, he's an unreal guy."

The left-back is presently a free agent. He worked his way through United's youth set-up before making his senior debut in 2019. That season, with Luke Shaw and Ashley Young battling fitness problems, he secured meaningful minutes and penned a fresh four-year contract in 2020.

‌



A loan switch to Norwich City in 2021 was followed by another temporary stint with Ipswich Town. While he failed to truly shine during these spells, his career trajectory shifted in 2023.

Eyewitnesses described seeing him drive recklessly, tailgating, braking sharply and holding a balloon to his mouth, although prosecutors emphasised there was no proof he was legally impaired. He lost control and smashed into a Ford Fiesta at around 74mph before careering into the central reservation.

He originally denied the charges but admitted guilt in March 2025 and was sentenced in May to 14 months' imprisonment, suspended for two years, a three-year driving ban and an unpaid community work order of 180 hours. As Williams tries to rebuild his career, he claims that if he still fancies going to watch his boyhood club, Fernandes can lend a hand.

Manchester United still have several squad holes in need of filling between now and the end of the transfer window. Michael Carrick has been hard at work overhauling his midfield, but the Red Devils have certain needs in defence and attack that require attention.

‌



United appear to be hard at work attempting to resolve those positions, too. However, the Ineos-led operation are taking a different tack to previous transfer windows as value for money looks to be taking greater precedence this summer.

‌



And United continue to demonstrate that approach after fresh links with a surprise name. Mirror Football discusses that and more in the latest transfer headline round-up.

‌

Joaquin Seys contact

As questions persist as to whether United will succeed with a move for Lewis Hall, the club are forced to consider alternative names. Hall, 21, has been incessantly linked as the new heir to Luke Shaw but Newcastle are holding firm in their not-for-sale stance.

Man Utd decide on giving Marcus Rashford new shirt number in clear hint on future READ MORE :

That's led United to make a host of enquiries elsewhere, with Club Brugge's Joaquin Seys the latest target added to the shortlist. The Sun reported the Red Devils have already reached out to his club regarding his availability, while Arsenal and Aston Villa have also been in contact.

‌



Seys, who is also 21, has impressed in the Pro League and even made a surprise run into Belgium's World Cup 2026 squad. There, he featured in the quarter-final loss to eventual winners Spain.

After moving Patrick Dorgu into a more effective wing role, Diogo Dalot is the only natural left-back alternative at Carrick's disposal at present. Shaw, 31, is now in the final year of his contract at Old Trafford and it remains unclear as to whether the club will extend his stay.

The Sun has suggested Club Brugge will demand £30million for their player, though that isn't expected to be a major hurdle. However, competitive interest from Premier League champions Arsenal in particular could pose a problem.

‌

View 2 Images Youri Tielemans has been hailed a "f***ing steal" by ex-Premier League star John Obi Mikel (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Premier League icon John Obi Mikel has hailed United for their capture of Belgium's Youri Tielemans. And the former Chelsea star cannot get over how his old rivals were able to get hold of the playmaker for just £35m.

One day after signing Andrey Santos from Chelsea in a £48m move, it was announced a deal had been struck for Tielemans. United activated the player's release clause and it was reported Tielemans impressed bosses with just how motivated he was to complete the transfer.

‌



Now, Champions League-winner and four-time FA Cup champion Mikel has ranked the move among his best of the summer. And he struggled to wrap his head around why Aston Villa would agree to insert such an affordable clause into their star's contract.

"For me, it’s Youri Tielemans," said Mikel on The Obi One Podcast when asked to judge the best midfield signings already made this summer. However, Tutto Juve reports that Yildiz is “considered unsellable” by the Italian club. Arsenal are claimed to have significant interest but Juventus want to “build the new team” around the Turkey international.

The club’s stance is reportedly unchanged from when the Gunners made an initial approach for Yildiz in June. Arteta’s side were also linked with the forward last summer, with Juventus previously valuing him at around £85m.

In February, the left winger signed a fresh contract until 2030. Yildiz scored 10 and assisted seven goals in 36 Serie A games last season.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy could be offered return to English football aged 39 after £15m bid rejected
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy could be offered return to English football aged 39 after £15m bid rejected

Jamie Vardy is a man without a club after leaving Cremonese and West Ham have him on their shortlist as they seek to add a new striker before the transfer window closes

View 2 Images Jamie Vardy could find himself back in England at the age of 39

West Ham are considering making a move for veteran frontman Jamie Vardy if they are unsuccessful with their pursuit of Troy Parrott.

‌



The former Leicester City forward wants to remain playing and is a free agent after his contract with Italian side Cremonese expired. It was his first spell playing outside of England and the Hammers could present the 39-year-old with the chance to return.

‌



Currently West Ham, who are gearing up for a first year in the Championship for more than a decade, have their sights on Parrott, formerly of Tottenham. The Irishman is now playing for AZ Alkmaar, where he has scored 51 goals in his two seasons.

‌



The Times reports that they've had a bid of £15million rejected and, if the Dutch side hold firm and refuse to sell their striker, then it could open the door for Vardy to make a move to the London Stadium. Another player on their shortlist was Wilson Isidor, but Sunderland have insisted he is not leaving.

9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem READ MORE :

Vardy spent the bulk of his career with the Foxes and was on their books when they won promotion from the Championship in 2014, he scored 16 times that year. Within two years he was a Premier League winner and proved himself to be a prolific marksman in the top flight.

Vardy scored 145 times in the top flight, putting him 14th on the all-time list, whilst he also won the Golden Boot in 2020. The former Fleetwood striker would win another Championship title with Leicester in 2022, scoring 20 times, and his experience could prove an asset for the Hammers as they seek an immediate return to the Premier League.

‌



The Hammers have just announced the signing of Manor Solomon, who penned a three-year deal after finalising a £7m switch from Tottenham. The winger was on loan at Leeds when they won promotion from the Championship in 2025.

View 2 Images West Ham are currently chasing Troy Parrott, but AZ Alkmaar have rejected their bids so far

West Ham are heavy favourites to win the Championship. They've managed to retain England international Jarrod Bowen whilst Nuno Espirito Santo has chosen to remain as manager. He won the second tier with Wolves back in 2017.

Article continues below

The Hammers began their season by beating Portsmouth in the first round of the Carabao Cup at the weekend. They will play fellow relegated side Burnley on Sunday at Turf Moor as they kick off their Championship campaign with one of their more challenging fixtures.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho admits his family have a better time when he's not around
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho admits his family have a better time when he's not around

Football manager Jose Mourinho rarely comments about his family life but says it remains important even if he seems football obsessed in new Netflix series.

View 2 Images Jose is back managing at Real and that mean there is unlikely to be much family time in the coming months. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Jose Mourinho has admitted he doesn’t spend a lot of time with his family but insists his wife and kids enjoy life more when he is not there.

‌



The football manager has been married to his childhood sweetheart Matilde “Tami” Faria for more than 35 years, and they have two children – Matilde, 30, and Jose Mario Jr, 26.

‌



But the family seldom travelled with him around Europe as he managed Benfica, Porto, Chelsea, Manchester United, Roma, Inter Milan and Real Madrid over 25 years. He lived in the Lowry hotel in Manchester alone for much of his time there. For the majority of their upbringing the children lived in the West London family home while Jose travelled.

‌



In a new interview, Mourinho, 63, says: “Sometimes you have a feeling of, ‘I should be there, I’m not there.’ But I don’t want you to think that family means something less important to me. They are in a place that they cannot even be compared with football.

View 2 Images Mourinho in new Netflix doc (Image: Courtesy of Netflix)

“But to tell the truth, I know that they enjoy life much more without me. That’s real. It’s true. If they go to a restaurant with me, it’s different than going without me.”

‌



But Mourinho has continually stressed the importance of his marriage and family life. In 2014 he told the Mirror: “My wife trusts me, my wife knows me. She has been with me since I was 17 and she was 15 – everything is so crystal clear for us.

“My social life doesn’t exist. I have my professional work and I have my family life. I am not the kind of guy with a social life and I am so happy the way I am. The secret in everything is love. If you’re success- ful in any job, I believe it is because you are in love with that job.

“And if you have a successful family it is because people are in love with each other. Love is the basic.”

‌



Jose often credits Tami for his success as a manager. Speaking in a new Netflix documentary on his family as photos of them appear on screen, he says: “I try to protect as much as I can, but many times, of course, I fail. It’s not easy.

“The mum[Tami] is a great mum, and they understand that to be what I am in football, this is my way. They need to understand it. You are pushing me to speak about myself, which I don't want to.

“I think your happiness, your unhappiness, your problems, you leave it in the door of the training ground. Probably, it's an old-fashioned way of looking at things, but that's who I am, and in the end, I don't want to change. It's too late.”

‌



Mourinho is much more comfortable discussing his career and his coaching at clubs like Inter, Chelsea and Real where he had much success. He is now back at Real for a second stint as manager. In the documentary series he is shown joking that he is “peaceful” whilst on a walk by the coast where he is carrying two mobile phones to make calls and send messages to his team about matches and transfers.

Now back at Real, he also explains football is his life and says: “Football is a job that absorbs me. That's the way I am. No gardening, no cooking, no cleaning, no golf, no paddle, no nothing.”

Mourinho is also happy to play the villain in football and is not one to shy away from controversy. He says he does not regret criticising referee Anders Frisk who ended up getting death threats and quit football following a controversial Champions League game in 2005 between Chelsea and Barcelona.

‌



Mourinho said: “People say I spoke too much after that match, but I will do it again. That's the way. So I'm not nice. I'm not nice. Just the way it is.”

Ask how it feels to admit he is not nice, he adds: “I do it in a pride way, and you think to help your team to get results.”

* The three-part series Mourinho drops on Netflix today(August 11).

Sports.title: Trump warns of 'terrible mistake' if FIFA replaces Infantino
Sports.content:
US President Donald Trump has warned FIFA would be making a "terrible mistake" if it got rid of Gianni Infantino as head of world football’s governing body.

Infantino has come under pressure following his doomed plan to sell off stakes in the men's World Cup to private investors.

But in a post on his Truth Social social media site early on Tuesday, Trump said removing the FIFA president would be a costly move.

The US president wrote: "FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented.

"If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!"

Infantino apologised for his proposal to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of FIFA's tournaments, with an idea to sell off around 20 per cent to private investors.

But UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC hit out at "deception" and a "fundamental breach of trust" around Infantino's botched plan, the three continental associations each signing a new open letter to the "football family" on Monday, without naming Infantino specifically but referring to a leader who "abandoned their duty" by breaking trust "through deception".

In the three-page document they again criticised the president's World Cup sale plans and rejected FIFA's claim that they had been a "mistake", adding: "There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup was a profound failure of judgment - not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol on whether Infantino can continue as the president of FIFA

UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC had been the three confederations to reject Infantino's plan before it was scrapped, while UEFA went further and announced a boycott of FIFA competitions - and last week confirmed the threat remained while Infantino is still in post.

The associations also hit out at the manner of a FIFA management committee meeting held in Morocco last Wednesday - a meeting which ended with a statement publicly backing Infantino - for not instead addressing FIFA's wider senior leadership at its base in Switzerland.

"It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him," the letter read. "There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness."

US Soccer and Canada Soccer - two of the three federations which hosted the World Cup - also called for meaningful change.

A US Soccer statement read: "US Soccer, Canada Soccer, CFU (Caribbean Football Union) and UNCAF (Central American Football Union) stand together, along with our colleagues around the world, in calling for meaningful change that strengthens FIFA's governance, transparency and accountability."

The UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC letter came around 24 hours after FIFA itself had hit out at "a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine" the governing body and president Infantino over claims surrounding his conduct at UEFA.

UEFA confirmed on Saturday a "departure payment" was made to a female employee alleged to have been in a relationship with Infantino when he was the European organisation's general secretary.

The Daily Telegraph reported the woman received a six-figure sum and UEFA confirmed a payment was made along with covering the fees for an MBA course, adding it was "in line" with regulations at the time.

The allegations intensified the position of Infantino, who worked at UEFA for 16 years and was its general secretary between 2009 and 2016 before being elected FIFA president, following his aborted plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Image: FIFA president Infantino

While not directly referencing UEFA's statement, FIFA accused Infantino's critics of trying to weaken his authority and have him removed from his role without a due re-election process.

A statement said: "It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its president.

"Those who do not have the support of FIFA's member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA's established democratic processes.

"Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its president. Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.

"The FIFA president has dedicated more than 30 years of his professional life to European and world football, contributing to significant change in the game and, in particular, to broadening access, resources and opportunity across world football

"Change inevitably challenges established interests, but disagreement with that change cannot justify efforts to undermine the democratic mandate of FIFA's president or the institution he was elected to lead.

"FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously.

"FIFA's responsibility is to its 211 member associations and to football around the world. We will not be distracted or diverted from strengthening the organisation, delivering for our member associations and continuing the work of making football truly global. Through the FIFA president and the FIFA administration, our focus remains firmly on that mission, and we are more determined than ever to fulfil it."

Sports.title: Refreshed Rory returns for FedExCup Playoffs as he targets fourth title
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy returns to action at the FedEx St. Jude Championship this week, live on Sky Sports, with the world No 2 targeting a big finish to the PGA Tour season and a record-extending fourth FedExCup title.

McIlroy heads into the first of three FedExCup Playoffs 12th in the season-long standings, with only the top 50 after this week progressing to the BMW Championship and then the top 30 qualifying for the season-ending Tour Championship.

The back-to-back Masters champion skipped last year's FedEx St Jude Championship but is part of this year's 69-man field at TPC Southwind in Memphis, where world No 1 Scottie Scheffler and defending champion Justin Rose also feature.

FedExCup Playoffs schedule All tournaments live on Sky Sports August 13-16: FedEx St. Jude Championship (TPC Southwind, Memphis, Tennessee) August 20-23: BMW Championship, (Bellerive Country Club, St. Louis, Missouri) August 27-30: Tour Championship (East Lake Golf Club, Atlanta, Georgia)

McIlroy has only played six events - and three outside of the majors - since successfully defending his Masters title in April, claiming tied-19th at the Truist Championship, tied-12th at The Memorial and a share of seventh at the Genesis Scottish Open.

But Brad Faxon, McIlroy's putting mentor, told the Sky Sports Golf Podcast that the 37-year-old has earned the right to cherry-pick his tournaments.

Faxon said: "After back-to-back Masters titles, he is like, 'not only financially can I afford to do this but mentally, too'.

"Rory is not physically tired after playing a round of golf but it is the mental fatigue of always being on, always in the spotlight, never getting a break. Whether it's walking into the gates or going to dinner at night, somebody is always coming up to you.

Image: McIlroy is a three-time FedExCup champion

"I have never seen anybody more patient in that situation than Rory but for him to go to the Greek islands with some of his closest friends, that's a way to get away from the game.

"When Rory said to his daughter, 'Poppy, I need to go and practise. Her great quote was, 'you already know how to play, daddy'. Rory hasn't forgotten how to play and had a pretty good track record in the playoffs.

"In the brutal summer months that you get in the south, you are going to have to be in very good physical shape these next few weeks to contend for the FedExCup."

How do the FedExCup Playoffs work?

Image: World No 1 Scottie Scheffler heads the FedExCup standings, ahead of Mathew Fitzpatrick, Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark and Chris Gotterup

All season long, players have earned points based on how they have performed in PGA Tour events, with extra points available for the signature events and majors.

Only the top 70 in the standings have reached the FedEx St Jude Championship (August 13-16), with just the top 50 then progressing to the BMW Championship (August 20-23) and then only the top 30 making it to the finale, The Tour Championship (August 27-30).

Winners of the first two play-off events earn 750 points apiece - the same as The Players and the majors - before the points reset to zero ahead of the Tour Championship.

In the closing event, all players begin at even par with the starting-strokes model based on FedExCup placings at that point axed in 2025.

The winner of the Tour Championship becomes FedExCup champion for 2026, earning $10m (£7.4m) dollars and a five-year PGA Tour exemption.

What else is at stake?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Brennan wrapped up a FedExCup Playoffs spot with victory at the Wyndham Championship on Sunday

Those who have qualified for the FedEx St Jude Championship are guaranteed to retain their PGA Tour card for 2027 and also clinch a spot at The Players, while the 50 to make the BMW Championship earn places in next term's signature events.

For the 30 who make it to the Tour Championship, they can look forward to a two-year PGA Tour exemption and teeing it up at the Masters at Augusta National. Spots in the US Open and Open are also set to come their way.

Why you should keep an eye on Koivun

After winning the 3M Open in just his third start as a pro after staying cool amid a charge from Scheffler, Jackson Koivin, 21, went on to wrap up a FedExCup Playoff spot after just five events, matching Tiger Woods' record.

Faxon added of the hot prospect, who he says would be great fit for USA at the away Ryder Cup in Ireland next September: "Koivun dominated college and he is the hardest working kid I have ever seen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jackson Koivun, 21, won the 3M Open a few weeks ago

"He comes blessed with a great putting stroke and a great putting attitude.

"I spend a lot of my time at the Titleist Performance Institute, where you can do all the testing of your equipment. I first met Jackson there and talked about his game.

"Every single guy who did the club fitting and ball fitting, was saying, 'nobody is close to what this guy is doing'. We have seen how good he hits the iron as well so I am excited for him.

"I am a long-term believer in Jackson Koivun."

Sports.title: England's World Cup place guaranteed but West Indies need to qualify
Sports.content:
Panic over, England fans - your team will NOT have to qualify for the 2027 Cricket World Cup.

England's drop-off in 50-over cricket had seen them plummet down the rankings and leave them at risk of missing out on automatic entry into next autumn's event in Africa.

However, the rot was stopped with successive come-from-behind series wins - over Sri Lanka earlier this year and then at home to India in July - leaving Harry Brook's men inside the required top eight in the rankings ahead of the September 30 cut-off.

With South Africa, who are certain of a place as co-hosts, sitting fourth in the standings, ninth-placed Bangladesh also secure direct passage to the tournament proper.

Zimbabwe are in, too, as they are another of the competition's co-hosts.

India, New Zealand, Australia, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Afghanistan - who secured their place with victory over Ireland - are the other guaranteed entrants.

Teams 12, 13, 14 in round-robin ‘Super Series’ Top team progresses to Round Two

Two groups of six teams (30 matches) Top three teams in each group plus next best across both qualify

West Indies headed for qualifying tournament once more

That means two-time champions West Indies, ranked 10th, will have to take part in the qualifying event for the third successive 50-over World Cup.

West Indies - World Cup winners in 1975 and 1979 - successfully reached the 2019 edition in England but then lost in qualifying for the 2023 showpiece in India.

The Caribbean side still have two more ODIs, in India, before September 30 but even if they win those two matches, they cannot move into the top nine in the rankings.

Image: Scotland will be in the qualifying tournament next year

West Indies are now headed for the qualifier in February and March, alongside Ireland, Netherlands, Scotland, USA and five yet-to-be-determined teams.

Under ​a new format for 2027, the ​winner of the qualifier will advance directly ​to the second stage of the World ⁠Cup, while the teams placing second, third and fourth will feature in the first round known ⁠as the Super Series.

That late switch was criticised in a joint statement from the Scottish and Dutch cricket boards, who accused the ICC of "weakening the integrity and credibility of international cricket."

Sky Sports News has contacted the ICC for comment.

Sports.title: Everton sign Johnson from Palace in transfer swap for McNeil
Sports.content:
Everton have signed winger Brennan Johnson from Crystal Palace in a transfer swap deal that sees Dwight McNeil move to Selhurst Park.

Both players have signed four-year deals, with Johnson departing Palace having only signed in January from Tottenham for £35m, but they have landed McNeil, who nearly joined them on Deadline Day in that same window, but the move broke down because paperwork wasn't submitted in time.

Johnson, 25, becomes the fifth summer signing for David Moyes' Everton after Merlin Rohl's loan obligation was activated along with the additions of Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Christian Norgaard.

McNeil, 26, joins defenders Oscar Mingueza and Takehiro Tomiyasu in signing for Palace this summer, having sold centre-back Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea.

"There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join - the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in. You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I'm a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

"I want to come in and show what I can do. The manager spoke to me about getting back to the form that I've shown previously, and that's a massive thing for me - the fact he knows and believes in what I can do. I know that's something that's definitely appreciated and a non-negotiable here. They can expect that from me. On top of that, I think I can bring speed, goals and everything I've got.

"The incredible fanbase that Everton has, whether it's home or away, is something I've always felt. It's a massive honour to be here and play for them now."

McNeil scored 15 goals and provided 18 assists in 130 appearances for Everton.

He said: "I'm really happy to be here, and looking forward to the challenge ahead.

"The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It's something that I want to be a part of, so I'm really looking forward to getting started."

Sports.title: Rashford set for reintegration at Man Utd - but is it a good idea?
Sports.content:
All eyes will be on Marcus Rashford this week.

He has not featured for Manchester United in the Premier League since December 2024 and has since had loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona.

Barcelona chose not to activate their £26m option to buy Rashford permanently this summer, meaning what seemed an unlikely reunion for the majority of last season has now become a reality.



With Rashford's expected return, he does provide Michael Carrick with a much-needed option at left wing and an alternative through the middle. Benjamin Sesko has yet to feature in pre-season as he continues to recover from injury and questions remain over Patrick Dorgu's best position.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ashley Young says there is no one better as a winger than Marcus Rashford and thinks Michael Carrick will get best out of him if he returns to Manchester United

United were potentially looking to add another forward option this summer, but with Rashford's return Carrick has a player who has scored 87 Premier League goals in 287 appearances and a different, perhaps more direct profile of player compared to Matheus Cunha on the left flank.

Rashford's return is one that Carrick is seemingly welcoming with open arms.

"We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together. Marcus is part of that," Carrick confirmed.

Question marks will remain as to whether Rashford can regain the form he showed after the World Cup in 2022 after a barren spell before his loan at Aston Villa.



Rashford had fallen out of favour with the last two Manchester United head coaches in Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, however, there is hardly anyone better to understand and coach Rashford than Carrick.

Rashford will be fully reintegrated into the United side as they continue their pre-season preparations in Dublin this week.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 3: Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 12th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 6th

Prospects

It was the day after the final game of last season at Bournemouth’s secluded, swish training base and, before clearing his belongings on his last day in the building, the departing head coach, Andoni Iraola, spent a couple of hours in his office chewing the fat with his successor, Marco Rose, talking players, pubs and tactics. The story goes that, with time moving on, Tiago Pinto, the club’s sporting director, knocked on the door to advise them there were other things to tackle.

It was an interesting scenario that speaks volumes of the respect between the pair. Long before joining Bournemouth, Iraola cited Rose’s Borussia Mönchengladbach side as one of his favourite teams to watch, the German’s “vertical football” helping them qualify for the Champions League in Rose’s first season in charge.

Rose accepts that Iraola, in absorbing the sales of key players totalling more than £250m last season and qualifying for Europe for the first time, has set a high bar. Remarkably, Bournemouth did not lose a game after the sale of Antoine Semenyo in the second week of January. Rose put it succinctly during pre-season in Austria. “Andoni didn’t leave a lot of space to improve,” he said. “Pressure’s on.”

In his first session, Rose told the players he loved the way they attacked the Premier League last season. Playing in the Europa League, however, represents uncharted territory for a team in the second tier as recently as four years ago. It is why Bournemouth’s hierarchy contacted peers at Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest to understand the realities of juggling the Thursday-Sunday rhythm the competition will bring. Rose is close friends with Oliver Glasner, who is now at Forest, but won the Conference League last season with Palace. “We are not going to Europe just to enjoy, we want to be competitive,” Rose said. “We are not there just to watch.”

Unlike last summer, so far they have retained all key players, chiefly Alex Scott, Rayan and Eli Junior Kroupi, the 20-year-old forward who breezed into double figures in his debut Premier League season and the club consider a generational talent. Kroupi attracted serious interest from Paris Saint-Germain, among other European superpowers, but a freak foot injury during a pre-season drill means he is sidelined for at least three months.

At the end of the season, Bournemouth earmarked a centre-back to replace Marcos Senesi and a striker to compete with Evanilson as key priorities and by the start of August the club had recruited Álvaro Rodríguez, whom Rose wanted to sign at Leipzig, and António Silva from Elche and Benfica respectively. Juanlu Sánchez joined from Sevilla to provide competition for Adam Smith, the evergreen 35-year-old into his 14th season at the club, and will also fill the void left by Álex Jiménez, who has joined Fiorentina on loan with an option to sign permanently because he remains suspended in England while under investigation by the Football Association.

Off-field picture

The smallest stadium in the Premier League has been a building site this summer, with the club working to ensure their 11,357-seater ground complies with Uefa regulations. There has been a wider facelift, too, with every seat being replaced, while they are filling in two corners to increase the capacity by 800 this season. Playing in Europe brings the challenge of meeting Uefa’s squad-cost ratio (SCR) rules, which caps on-pitch spending at 70% of a club’s revenue. Bournemouth finished the 2025-26 season at 82% and they continue to work towards meeting the threshold. Last month the academy was awarded category one status, four years after being category three.

Owner-fan relationship

The American billionaire Bill Foley described himself as a dictator upon buying the club approaching four years ago, but supporters are grateful for his naked ambition. Foley, who made his fortune in insurance, is forthright and somewhat prophetic. In 2023, he said the club would play in Europe within five years – and achieved it in three. It was a similar story with Vegas Golden Knights, whom he vowed would win the Stanley Cup within six years of him launching the ice hockey franchise in 2017 – they won it in their sixth season. Foley recently added rugby union’s Exeter Chiefs to his sporting stable, which extends to Lorient, Auckland FC and Moreirense. Not every decision is universally popular but Foley, who turns 82 in December and predominantly splits his time between California and Vegas, puts his money where his mouth is.

The manager

As a defender, Marco Rose was schooled by Jürgen Klopp and Thomas Tuchel at Mainz, and Ralf Rangnick at Hannover, so had quite the education before beginning his coaching career at home town club Lokomotive Leipzig. Klopp told Rose, after promotion to the Bundesliga in 2004, that he would excel in the dugout and he has since managed some of the biggest names: Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham at Borussia Dortmund, Dominik Szoboszlai and Dani Olmo at RB Leipzig. Rose has been compared to Klopp and, naturally, Iraola, given his appetite for high-energy tactics. Bournemouth routed Genoa 10-1 in pre-season so, could his style be even more aggressive than Iraola’s? “I would say [to be] even more aggressive than Andoni is quite difficult,” came the reply. His grandfather, Walter Rose, represented Germany in 1937.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen António Silva has all the attributes to be a bargain buy for Bournemouth. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images

These days, £50m is about the going rate for an elite defender. Tottenham paid £52m to sign Jan Paul van Hecke. Chelsea paid the same fee to take Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace. Bournemouth pocketed £50m when Dean Huijsen joined Real Madrid last year, though that price was set by a release clause. They are deals that make Bournemouth’s £25.7m purchase of António Silva, a 22-year-old who has been a regular at Benfica since breaking into the team and has experience in the Champions League, Europa League and 20 caps for Portugal, appear a snip. Silva, who is right-footed but prefers to play as a left-centre back, is a direct replacement for Senesi.

Stat attack

Bournemouth scored nine goals from Opta-defined counterattacks last season, the joint most in the Premier League. But their threat was varied; in only two of their preceding eight top-flight campaigns did they score more set-piece goals than the 14 they managed in 2025-26. It is very rare for a team to be so productive on both fronts.

Set for a breakthrough

It was a November night of ecstasy when Scotland qualified for the World Cup for the first time in 28 years, but for Ben Gannon-Doak it was a bittersweet evening and one that curtailed his club season. The 20-year-old was forced off after 21 minutes, replaced by Kenny McLean who capped the scoring in style. A £25m arrival from Liverpool last August, Gannon-Doak featured in all three of Scotland’s World Cup matches, starting the first and last, and has impressed in pre-season. After being limited to 113 minutes in eight league appearances as a substitute last campaign, there is optimism Gannon-Doak will make his mark.

World Cup impact

Rayan became the first Brazilian teenager to start a World Cup match since Marco Antônio in 1970 when he was named in Carlo Ancelotti’s starting XI for their Group C game against Scotland. The then 19-year-old, signed from Vasco de Gama in January, set up Vinícius Júnior for Brazil’s opener in the 3-0 win and afterwards swapped shirts with Gannon-Doak. Tyler Adams enhanced his reputation, impressing for the USA en route to the last 16. Two new members of Bournemouth’s coaching staff, the set-piece coach, Nicolas Gagnon, and goalkeeping coach, Frederic de Boever, worked with Canada and Belgium respectively. Alex Scott’s inclusion in Tuchel’s pre-World Cup training camp in Florida spoke volumes of the Guernsey-born midfielder’s wider standing.

Sports.title: Donald Trump says it would be a ‘terrible mistake’ to replace Fifa’s Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
US president Donald Trump has warned Fifa would be making a “terrible mistake” if they get rid of Gianni Infantino as the head of world football’s governing body.

Infantino has come under pressure following his doomed plan to sell off stakes in the men’s World Cup to private investors.

But in a post on his Truth Social social media site early on Tuesday, Trump said removing the Fifa president would be a costly move.

The US president wrote: “Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino.

“He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!”

Uefa and two other confederations have held initial talks about organising competitions themselves amid the backlash against the embattled Fifa president.

Europe’s governing body, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf, which oversees football in the ‌Caribbean, North and Central America, have accused Infantino of “deception” and while it is understood they want to give him the chance to resign and leave his position with dignity without seeking re-election in March next year, they want to insulate themselves from the unfolding crisis.

Uefa has previously threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions.

Infantino apologised for his proposal to create Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of Fifa’s tournaments, with an idea to sell off around 20% to private investors.
