But an open letter signed by the heads of Uefa, AFC and Concacaf has urged Fifa to hold an independent review into Infantino’s scheme, while not naming the Swiss directly.

“Leadership in football is not a possession,” the letter said. “It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

Sports.title: League Two 2026-27 preview: the contenders, hopefuls and strugglers
Sports.content:
Contenders

Salford meekly lost the playoff final and that was the end of days for Karl Robinson as he was sacked. Peter Cklamovski was not the obvious replacement, but the Australian left behind the Malaysia national side for a crack at League Two with the rebranded Ammies, who are back in their traditional orange. Macaulay Langstaff has arrived with the task of providing the goals to finally get Salford up and few would bet against the striker.

Chesterfield fell short in the playoffs, too, but Paul Cook remains one of the best managers at this level, although the loss of Armando Dobra could be significant. Securing the veteran forward Andy Cook was important for Grimsby as they seek to push on and his influence could be telling if he plays enough games. Lee Grant did not get much chance to prove himself at Huddersfield so will be desperate to do so at Walsall, especially after a promising start by knocking Championship side Bristol City out of the EFL Cup. The former goalkeeper will be hoping he is the man to ensure the Saddlers do not stop playing in winter, as has been the case in recent years.

Of those who have dropped down, Rotherham are the more intriguing bet, having brought in Steve McClaren as director of football and Alex Bruce as head coach in an attempt to revitalise the club. Losing Sam Nombe was a blow, but his transfer fee should allow investment. Jon Brady knows what he is doing and could do nothing to keep Port Vale up, but arguably has the most complete squad at this level with Max Watters and Kyle Dempsey standout summer signings.

View image in fullscreen Rotherham will hope to utilise the experience of their director of football Steve McClaren to bolster their chances of promotion into League One. Photograph: WhiteRosePhotos/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

Hopefuls

An end‑of‑season slump kept Crewe out of the playoffs last time round, but the returns of Luke Offord and Joe White provide much‑needed quality. Barnet were two points off eighth having returned to the EFL and have kept their developing squad together – apart from Ryan Glover who was sold to Stockport – to give Dean Brennan real belief that his side can improve. Oldham made a steady return to the fourth tier and have added the guarantee of Elliott Nevitt’s goals alongside Oliver Norburn, who was a key member of the Notts County side that went up from this division.

Colin Kazim-Richards has his feet fully under the table at Crawley and has overseen one of their traditional busy summers in an attempt to avoid a relegation battle. The former Sunderland goalkeeper Vito Mannone was an eye‑catching signing, while the talented Malcolm Ebiowei will be aiming to turn his career around. If these two shine, it could make them a surprise package. Relegation and problems off the pitch have put Exeter on a downward spiral, which does not look like being arrested without further incomings. “Absolute tinpot garbage” was Ian Holloway’s view of Swindon’s friendly performance against Bristol City, which suggests the team still have levels to go. Gareth Ainsworth wants high‑pressing Gillingham to maintain energy levels over the course of the campaign to give them an outside chance of challenging.

George Burley’s son-in-law Chris Hogg joined Northampton in May for his first managerial role and, after sunning himself in Greece, is primed to test himself, but the Cobblers may rue the departure of Cameron McGeehan as they aim to rebuild after relegation. Gavin Cowan transformed Shrewsbury from no-hopers to comfortably staying up but he faces a tricky second album.

John Terry is not the Colchester owner, as the sale of the club rumbles on without a solution. Steve Evans will ensure Bristol Rovers are competitive, but whether that means they can push themselves higher than 14th place last season remains to be seen.

Strugglers

The promoted teams start on the backfoot after managerial changes, as Rochdale lost Jimmy McNulty, while York decided to sack Stuart Maynard midway through preseason, much to the consternation of the fans. Diligence in recruitment, however, gives them optimism, especially Dale bringing back Cian Hayes.

Tranmere survived by a couple of points last time round but will be hoping for an uplift under Darrell Clarke, who has persuaded Will Vaulks and the former Watford winger Tom Ince that Prenton Park is a sensible place to continue their careers. Newport County were also forced into a change in the dugout when Christian Fuchs decided Rodney Parade was not the place he wanted to call home having kept the team up, leaving the club in flux as Chris Todd oversaw preparations for the campaign. The Exiles brought in plenty of experience in the shape of Harrison Biggins and Christian Doidge to strengthen the squad.

The inexperienced Matt Lawlor is set for a challenging first full season in charge of Fleetwood, who are boosted by the signing of Andy Cannon from Wrexham. Steve Cotterill revitalised Cheltenham almost a year ago, but five of their first six summer signings were relegated in May, which does not inspire confidence. After finishing comfortably in midtable, Accrington Stanley may not fear the drop and Cole Stockton is a clever signing but there is a nagging doubt about the club’s efficacy.

View image in fullscreen Managerial inexperience may prove challenging for Matt Lawlor (left) who has much to prove in his first full season at Fleetwood Town. Photograph: Phil Oldham/Shutterstock

Ones to watch

Maldini Kacurri, Grimsby, 20 After starting last season on loan at doomed National League side Morecambe, the Albania international may have wondered if life outside Arsenal was really for him. The defender shone when he stepped up to League Two with Grimsby, guided by David Artell, proving himself capable of coping with the physicality in the lower tiers.

Patrick Mlynarski, Crewe, 18 A Wales youth international, the recently-turned 18-year-old is now in his first year as a professional. The winger made his debut in the EFL Trophy last season, but is yet to feature in the league. Previously part of Everton’s academy, Mylnarski is skilful and powerful, playing on the left, possessing the ability to cut in or beat defenders on the outside.

Will Gray, Shrewsbury, 17 The midfielder made four starts last season and signed his first professional contract in the summer. His manager, Gavin Cowan, has praised his mentality and ability to keep things simple in the centre of the park.

Sports.title: Liverpool owners close to £1.35bn sale of 30% stake to consortium including Jeff Bezos
Sports.content:
A consortium including the Amazon founder, Jeff Bezos, is close to completing a deal for a 30% stake in Liverpool after months of talks with Fenway Sports Group. The investors are led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of the Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and who previously was a shareholder and director at Queens Park Rangers.

The Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is another member of the group who will pay in the region of £1.35bn. The deal is effectively agreed, but may take up to a month to complete.

Bezos has a personal fortune of around $257bn (£190bn), according to Forbes, making him the fourth-richest person in the world, while Saverin is reportedly worth $32bn. This will be Bezos’s first investment in football, but he has previously looked into bidding for NFL franchises. The 62-year-old will receive equity as part of the deal, which Deloitte has advised on.

Bezos is the executive chair of Amazon having relinquished day-to-day control when he stepped down as chief executive five years ago. Under his leadership, the online retailer has diversified into being an entertainment provider and has bought numerous sports rights for its streaming service.

Amazon had live UK rights for 20 Premier League games each season for six seasons until the end of last year and broadcasts the Champions League in several European countries, as well as some NFL games in the US.

FSG bought Liverpool in 2010 and have overseen two Premier League titles. FSG sold 3% of the club to the US private equity firm Dynasty Equity in 2023.

It has been a summer of change at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola replacing Arne Slot as head coach, Mohamed Salah left on a free transfer and has joined Trabzonspor and Michael Edwards departed his role as chief executive officer at FSG.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton seal Brennan Johnson-Dwight McNeil swap deal
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace and Everton have agreed a straight swap for Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil – six months after McNeil’s partner accused Palace of messing with his mental health after pulling out of a deal.

McNeil and Johnson, who became Palace’s record signing when he joined in January from Tottenham for £35m, only to be surpassed by the arrival of Jørgen Strand Larsen from Wolves for an initial £43m a few weeks later, have agreed four-year contracts with the option of a further 12 months.

“There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in,” said Johnson. “You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I’m a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.”

McNeil, who had entered the final year of his Everton contract, appeared to be moving to Selhurst Park in February after Palace agreed a £20m fee on transfer deadline day. But the collapse of Jean-Philippe Mateta’s £30m move to Milan, after the France striker failed a medical, prompted Palace to change their offer to an initial loan with an obligation to buy at the end of the season.

They submitted a deal sheet to the Premier League, but then pulled out. McNeil’s partner, Megan Sharpley, wrote an emotional post on Instagram saying there had been “radio silence” from Palace and that the player’s mental health had been affected.

“Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you,” she wrote at the time. “We live in a world where everyone is aware of how big a problem mental health is. So, in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money and that’s OK to mess and toy with their mental health and that it’s just part of the job?”

On Tuesday the Palace chair, Steve Parish, said: “It is wonderful to finally welcome Dwight – a player with proven ability in the Premier League – to South London. I’m looking forward to seeing him in action at Selhurst Park.”

Johnson had been disappointing at Palace, failing to score in 18 Premier League appearances. Given he signed a four-and-a-half-year contract in January that is believed to be worth more than £100,000 a week, Palace will take a significant hit on the fee they paid, but remove one of their highest earners from the wage bill.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Vardy to West Ham? Madrid move for Zubimendi?
Sports.content:
When did the summer of 2026 transform into a midfield merry-go-round? Now Bruno Guimarães has rocked up at Arsenal and Manchester United have a couple of new signings, it stands to reason that more midfielders will be on the move soon and Real Madrid appear to be chasing Gunners metronome Martín Zubimendi.

It seems odd that Arsenal would sanction a sale, given they spent most of the 2024-25 campaign coveting the former Real Sociedad star, but Mikel Arteta has forward and defensive targets to land instead. Pedro Neto is the latest winger to be linked, though Liverpool and Tottenham are also in the queue for the Chelsea flyer. Tricky Juventus wide man Kenan Yildiz has also been mentioned in relation to Arsenal.

Meanwhile, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Reiss Nelson are on the departures list at the Emirates Stadium to make room for a new attacker or two. A loan to West Ham could be on the cards for Nelson, who is now 26 and seemingly set to embark upon his third successive London loan. Roma and Galatasaray like the look of Martinelli, while Napoli want Jesus.

It might be 2026 but Chelsea still have a “bomb squad” and they are trying their best to offload the likes of Benoît Badiashile, Axel Disasi and David Datro Fofana for a few quid. Badiashile could join Jesus at Napoli, having been squeezed out under a succession of Stamford Bridge bosses.

Manchester United have turned their attention away from Newcastle’s Lewis Hall, who is deemed to be too expensive, instead locking their sights on RB Leipzig left-back David Raum. The eternal search for a Luke Shaw competitor goes on. Raum will hope to fare better than Brandon Williams, Alex Telles and Tyrell Malacia in that regard. Racing Santander youngster Jorge Salinas has also been linked.

Leeds United have quietly completed some good business this summer and central defender Nico Elvedi of Borussia Mönchengladbach could add to that tranche of incomings. Forward Joe Gelhardt may be heading to Wrexham to balance the books.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

And speaking of Championship transfers, could Jamie Vardy be set for a stunning return to English football? A move to West Ham is apparently on the cards. The Leicester legend spent a year in Italy with Cremonese but is a free agent again and, at 39, could he do a job for the Hammers? Start the party.

Sports.title: Are Manchester United returning to relevance under Michael Carrick? | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Manchester United finally seem to have something that resembles stability in the dressing room under Michael Carrick. I feel with quality signings in defence and midfield, they could mount a decent challenge for the Premier League next season. How do you feel they will fare? – Sterling.

There’s an odd sense that Michael Carrick’s level of achievement last season was at precisely the most awkward level for the board. United didn’t produce indisputably brilliant football under him but equally 12 wins and three draws in 17 games was good enough that they pretty much had to give him the job. But it’s one thing to turn out those kinds of results when the pressure’s off, you’re already out of both cup competitions and you don’t have any European football; it’s quite another to do it in the heat of a full season. United don’t have to have an especially amazing season to play 15 more games this season than they did in 2025-26.

That’s not to say that Carrick won’t be successful. There was much that he did last season that was very impressive. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans bolster an area of the squad that desperately needed to improve. A left-back seems almost certain to arrive before the end of the month and there’s probably the need for one more high-class experienced central defender. It’s not clear what Marcus Rashford’s future is after his return from loan at Barcelona, but he has two years left on his contract and could add dynamism and finishing to the left side of the attack. It’s probably not a title-winning squad, but it’s certainly one that should qualify for the Champions League.

Two questions remain that will only be answered as the season goes on. First, Carrick himself: can he cope with the churn of two games a week, and operating with a squad that is at least as fatigued as their opponents? And second, where is the club psychologically? Part of the problem for United, a familiar trait of big clubs who have fallen from grace, is that they have got into a routine of failure, that no success can ever quite be trusted, and every setback is seen as a further example of the terminal decline (although just as damaging would be suddenly believing everything is fine if United were to win, say, their first three games of the season). Retaining clarity of thought and making realistic assessments are perhaps the greatest challenges for a club that has known greatness but is struggling to return to those heights.

What do you see the broader impact of the VAR changes that Fifa made this year being? Do you think that other soccer leagues will see the increasingly automated, faster but less human approach taken by Fifa this summer and choose to adopt it? (I am aware that the Premier League has already chosen to reject much of it) – Dennis.

The most notable changes implemented before the World Cup allowed VAR to review and overturn incorrectly awarded corner kicks, certain attacking fouls and clear mistakes relating to red cards given from a second yellow. The only one of these adopted by the Premier League is to allow VAR to overturn a second yellow leading to a red (VAR cannot recommend that a referee should award a second yellow that would lead to a red). If we have to have VAR, that seems reasonable enough; nobody wants to see a team incorrectly reduced to 10 men.

At the World Cup, the corner issue only rarely came up, but it always seemed slightly odd that incorrectly awarded goal kicks could not be turned into corners. Personally, I would scrap VAR, or at least this form of it, but if incorrect decisions can be corrected quickly and unobtrusively then they probably should be. I understand, though, why the Premier League, aiming for a “light touch” – good luck with that – would be resistant.

Greater use of VAR, though, seemed to be the direction of travel. I suspect relatively soon offsides will be almost fully automated, which probably makes sense so long as it’s almost instantaneous. Whatever doubts there may be about margins of error and frame rates, it’s still going to be more accurate than a 40-year-old running the line 30 yards away, peering through a thicket of players.

More significant is probably the Premier League’s adoption of regulations against timewasting: speeded-up substitutions, players who receive treatment having to remain off the field for 60 rather than 30 seconds, an outfield player having to be withdrawn for 60 seconds after a goalkeeper receives treatment, and a five-second clock on throw-ins and goal kicks. All should speed up the game and improve the spectacle. It’ll be interesting as well to see the level of tolerance for grappling in the box, particularly by attacking players, which was an area in which the Premier League seemed out of step with the rest of Europe last season.

Which of the Premier League’s promoted sides have the best chance of staying up, and why? – Nicholas.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The achievements of Sunderland and Leeds last season, finishing seventh and 14th, will have heartened the promoted sides, but the truth is it will be extremely difficult for all three. Both those sides invested heavily in a way that is impossible for Coventry, Ipswich or Hull. It’s very hard to see how Hull, who were promoted unexpectedly, can survive. Coventry, perhaps, with the euphoria of their Premier League return and the Frank Lampard factor can give it a go, but their summer spending has been modest. Ipswich, with recent Premier League experience, have a chance and have made some intriguing signings in Daizen Maeda, Abdul Fatawu, Issa Diop and Chuba Akpom, but they’ve lost the manager who got them up, with Kieran McKenna opting for a break rather than another Premier League campaign. Gary O’Neil perhaps feels he has unfinished business, but if any of the promoted sides are to survive, they need another club to have a dreadful campaign.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Marinakis sues Crystal Palace over fan banner
Sports.content:
The Nottingham Forest owner, Evangelos Marinakis, is suing Crystal Palace for defamation after supporters of the south London club displayed a banner depicting him holding a gun to the head of the England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

Almost 12 months since the banner appeared midway through the first half of Palace’s 1-1 draw with Forest at Selhurst Park, lawyers for Marinakis lodged the claim for defamation against CPFC Ltd and “persons unknown” at the high court on Monday.

The banner showed the Greek shipping magnate pointing the gun at Gibbs-White, who had been set to join Tottenham last summer before Forest pulled out of the deal, and also featured the message: “Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match‑fixing, drug trafficking or corruption.” Marinakis has previously rejected all those allegations. Lawyers for Marinakis were approached for comment. A spokesperson for Palace did not comment.

Palace were fined £50,000 by the Football Association in February after being found guilty of failing “to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) didn’t behave in an improper, offensive, abusive, insulting and/or provocative way at this match”. The FA added in its statement: “The fact that Crystal Palace had a policy to prevent banners being smuggled into the stadium demonstrates that it was aware of the risk.”

Last summer, Palace and Forest were at loggerheads after Forest wrote to Uefa to voice their concerns that Palace could be in breach of multiclub ownership rules. The FA Cup winners ended up being demoted to the Conference League, with Forest – who had finished seventh in the Premier League and originally qualified for the Conference League – promoted in their place. Palace went on to win that competition under Oliver Glasner, while Forest reached the Europa League semi-finals.

Glasner has since joined Forest after leaving Palace at the end of his contract in a move that has surprised both sets of supporters. The Austrian said this week that Marinakis had persuaded him to change his mind over dinner in Athens after previously rejecting Forest because they were not in Europe next season.

“Then I had a more detailed look and there are two reasons why I changed my mind and I told him,” Glasner said. “No 1 is I think there is more potential in the squad than they have shown. And No 2 is you, it’s your ambition, because I am very ambitious.”

Sports.title: Djed Spence edges closer to Tottenham exit with top club aiming for £25m deal
Sports.content:
Djed Spence edges closer to Tottenham exit with top club aiming for £25m deal

Inter Milan have reopened talks with Tottenham Hotspur over the signing of Djed Spence, talkSPORT understands.

The Italian champions are willing to spend up to £30million on the England international this summer.



3 Inter have re-opened talks with Spurs over the signing of Spence Credit: Getty

Spence is open to a move away from Spurs before the transfer window closes.

Having been offered to several clubs, Inter have now returned to the table to discuss a potential deal.

Cristian Chivu's side want to pay between €30m (£25m) and €35m (£30m) for the 26-year-old.



Meanwhile, Spurs' asking price at the start of the window was set at €50m (£42.7m).

Inter's renewed interest comes after talkSPORT revealed Liverpool were not working on a deal to sign Spence despite recent reports.



Spence future

Spurs are open to offers for the versatile full-back as they look to fund their summer spending spree.

Roberto De Zerbi has already spent over £200m ahead of the new season, with the club's transfer record broken twice.



Spence also finds himself behind Pedro Porro in the pecking order at right-back despite his World Cup heroics.

He featured in all seven of England's matches in North America, including four starts, as they finished third.

Due to those commitments, Spence did not return to Spurs for pre-season ahead of their tour of New Zealand and Australia.

3 Inter are prepared to pay up to £30million for Spence this summer Credit: Getty



The defender was also not involved in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Getafe on Saturday, with his side concluding their summer schedule at home to Hoffenheim this weekend.

Having signed a new deal last summer, Spence currently has three years remaining on his Spurs contract.

Where would Spence play for Inter?

Inter's interest comes with the club facing a potential crisis at wing-back going into their title defence.

Although Chivu prefers to deploy a 3-5-2 formation, he is currently without a recognised senior right-sided defender.



Spence is capable of playing both as a full-back and wing-back on both sides of the pitch.

Whilst he has only briefly appeared at wing-back for Spurs, he has featured in the role previously for Genoa, Nottingham Forest and Middlesbrough.

3 Spence starred for England at right-back and left-back during the World Cup Credit: Getty

His time at Genoa is Spence's only prior experience of Italian football.



He spent the second half of the 2023/24 campaign with the club, making 16 Serie A appearances.

Sports.title: Everton and Crystal Palace complete rare swap deal
Sports.content:
Everton and Crystal Palace have completed a swap deal involving Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson.

The two clubs announced the deal on Tuesday morning that sees McNeil head to the Eagles and Johnson to the Toffees.



4 Johnson has struggled since joining Palace from Tottenham in January Credit: Getty

4 Johnson is now an Everton player Credit: Everton FC

Wales international Johnson only joined Palace in January from Tottenham in a £35million move.

He briefly held the mantle of the Eagles' club record signing before it was broken weeks later for now-teammate Jorgen Strand Larsen.



The 25-year-old has struggled badly since swapping London's north for south, having failed to score in 26 appearances for Palace.

The former Nottingham Forest star was then an unused substitute in his new club's Conference League final triumph over Rayo Vallecano.



It is a rapid fall from grace from the heights of the 2024/25 season in which Johnson finished as Tottenham's top scorer with 18 goals - which also included the winner in the Europa League final as Spurs ended their 17-year trophy drought.

He found the net just four times across 22 appearances under Thomas Frank in the first half of last season before heading to Palace.



Johnson said: “I'm so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it's a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.

"There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in. You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I'm a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

"I want to come in and show what I can do. The manager spoke to me about getting back to the form that I've shown previously, and that's a massive thing for me – the fact he knows and believes in what I can do. For me, listening to him – a manager who is so experienced and someone who has been so successful – it was really nice to hear.

"I want to bring all of my attributes. First and foremost, I'll work for the team, the fans, and represent the club properly. I know that's something that's definitely appreciated and a non-negotiable here. They can expect that from me. On top of that, I think I can bring speed, goals and everything I've got.



"The incredible fanbase that Everton has, whether it's home or away, is something I've always felt. It's a massive honour to be here and play for them now."

Palace and Everton completed Johnson and McNeil swap deal

Johnson could have been joined at Selhurst Park by McNeil, who looked set to seal a deadline-day switch to the club in January.

A loan deal with a £20m obligation to buy was agreed with Everton, only for the transfer to be aborted at the 11th hour.

talkSPORT previously reported that the relevant paperwork was not submitted to the league in time, despite McNeil completing a medical and Palace submitting a deal sheet to be granted extra time.



The 26-year-old's partner, Megan Sharpley, subsequently accused Palace of messing with his mental health and breaking promises.

Sharpley criticised the Conference League winners over a lack of communication and labelled their handling of McNeil as 'cruel'.

4 McNeil would have been keen to get his future sorted after a roller coaster year Credit: Getty

talkSPORT revealed in the days afterwards that Palace did not intend to abandon the deal and were sympathetic to the player's plight.



It has also been reported that Palace held clear the air talks with McNeil's partner.

Rare swap deals

McNeil had entered the final 12-months of the five-year deal he signed upon his arrival on Merseyside from Burnley in 2022.

Straight swap deals between two Premier League clubs, meanwhile, are proving increasingly rare due in part to amortisation (PSR Rules).

Teams are less likely to replicate the Alexis Sanchez-Henrikh Mkhitaryan swap and instead line up pseudo-swaps that go down on the balance sheet as two separate transfers - such as the individual deals which saw Luka Vuskovic join Brighton while Jan Paul van Hecke headed in the opposite direction to Tottenham.



Other recent examples included Everton and Aston Villa sending their academy products Tim Iroegbunam and Lewis Dobbin to each other in separate deals for a reported £9m each.

4 McNeil and Sharpley both took to social media to comment on his failed switch to Palace earlier this year Credit: Getty

Villa also flogged Omari Kellyman to Chelsea for £19m days after landing the Blues' homegrown defender Ian Maatsen for £37.5m.

The most infamous of them all saw Elliot Anderson leave his boyhood club Newcastle for Nottingham Forest in July 2024 for £35m.



Yet Forest effectively paid only £15m on the balance sheet, given goalkeeper Odysseas Vlachodimos moved to Tyneside for £20m.

talkSPORT verdict

McNeil's former manager at Everton Sean Dyche is intrigued to see how both players adapt.

“Maybe it’s a good fit in a different way. It gives Dwight a different feeling coming to London,” Dyche told talkSPORT on Sunday.

“Would he be affected by that? I’ve mentioned before that some players are and some love it and they fit and hand in glove and others find it a bit tricky.



Equally with Brendan, he could be better off going outside London, there’s a different feel to a northern club… it’s a different feel, different people, different cultural feel.

“So it might suit both in a different way. It’ll be really interesting to see if this happens how them two players do.”

Sports.title: James McClean ‘to turn up for training’ despite new club’s attempts to terminate contract after just seven months
Sports.content:
James McClean ‘to turn up for training’ despite new club’s attempts to terminate contract after just seven months

James McClean will not leave Derry City without a fight amid reports his hometown club wish to rip up his deal.

The 37-year-old returned to the League of Ireland Premier Division side in January to bring an end to his two-and-a-half-year stay at Wrexham.

2 Former Wrexham star McClean could soon be on the lookout for his next club Credit: Getty

McClean first joined the Northern Irish outfit in 2008, where he proceeded to score 18 goals in 88 games - earning him a move to Premier League side Sunderland in 2011.

But after nearly 15 years playing in the English football pyramid, an emotional return to link up with younger brother Patrick at the Ryan McBride Brandywell Stadium was an opportunity he couldn't turn down.

However, to say his move back home hasn't gone to plan would be an understatement.

Why might James McClean be leaving Derry City?

According to the Irish Independent, Derry are bidding to terminate his contract.

It has been claimed that the club have informed McClean of their intention to do so, citing that the veteran midfielder lacks the required 'physical capacity'.

Though McClean, who has started just 12 of Derry's 27 top-flight games this season, disputes this claim.

And it is said that the retired Republic of Ireland international will report back for training as he looks to prove his fitness.

In recent days, McClean has taken to Instagram to show himself working out.

While he also took to his story on Monday showing himself climbing Errigal Mountain.

McClean has been left out of Derry's last two league matchday squads since starting in their FAI Cup second round win over Tolka Rovers on July 19.

2 McClean departed Wrexham in January after featuring on 108 occasions for the Welsh outfit Credit: Getty

What has James McClean said about Derry City?

McClean has failed to bite his tongue when discussing his unhappiness since returning to his boyhood side.

During World Cup punditry duty for RTE in June, McClean declared that broken promises were made when convincing him to join.

He said: "You have a lot of conversations on the phone, and then you come home and quickly realise that what you hear on the phone is not what you see in reality.

"There are a lot of factors that have contributed to that. I'm going to leave them for another day."

The former Stoke star also issued a cryptic message hitting out at the club following their Conference League qualifying exit at the hands of Rijeka.

He posted: "[Shamrock] Rovers, Bohs [Bohemians], Shels [Shelbourne], Larne have all progressed through ties in Europe this year.

"We played four, lost four, and sorry, it needs to be said, we have every much as good, if not better, a squad on paper

If you watch the games, the lads aren’t losing these games based on lack of effort, so clearly there is an issue somewhere.

“Given [I] am around it every day and have the CV to give my opinion, I think I’ll give it whether anyone likes it or not.

“If you don’t like it, then you’ll excuse me for not caring about your opinion, given that 99.9 per cent that have a lot to say have never played a professional game in their lives.”

And earlier this month, he went on a TikTok rant to address comments made by former Derry boss Roddy Collins - brother of former world champion Steve - that he was the 'worst signing' made in the club's history.

He subsequently proceeded to mock Collins' managerial career, while also having a pop at his son Roddy Jr.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis sues Crystal Palace over gun banner
Sports.content:
Evangelos Marinakis is suing Crystal Palace over a controversial fan banner.

The Nottingham Forest owner lodged a defamation claim in the High Court on Monday with CPFC Limited among the two defendants named.

3 Evangelos Marinakis has owned Nottingham Forest since 2017 Credit: Getty

It comes nearly a year after the banner was displayed which showed him holding a gun to Morgan Gibbs-White’s head.

This was unfurled by fans at Selhurst Park during a 1-1 Premier League draw between Palace and Forest last August.

The banner also had the sarcastic message which read: "Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match-fixing, drug trafficking or corruption."

Marinakis has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to these allegations.

Palace were later charged by the FA with failing to ensure that supporters did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or provocative way in November 2025.

They were alleged to have failed to ensure that supporters did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or provocative way, though the banner was not named as the specific reason for the charge.

The message displayed referred to Forest talisman Gibbs-White's high-profile transfer saga in the 2025 summer transfer window.

The England international had looked set to leave the City Ground after Tottenham appeared to trigger his £60m release clause.

But in a shock turnaround, Gibbs-White ultimately signed a new contract to stay at the club, and later spoke about his decision during an interview alongside Marinakis.

Tensions had been building between Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace, after the London side lost their place in last season's Europa League for breaking UEFA's multi-club ownership rules.

3 Morgan Gibbs-White was at the centre of a huge transfer saga in the summer of 2025 Credit: Getty

Forest ended up taking their spot in the competition, with Palace demoted to the Conference League, which they went on to win.

Marinakis' representatives have been approached for comment.

Nottingham Forest's new season

It has been all change at the City Ground this summer with Oliver Glasner now at the helm.

The Austrian signed a three-year contract having left Palace at the end of last season.

He has inherited a Forest side which finished 16th in the Premier League last season, avoiding relegation by six points.

The East Midlands side also reached the semi-finals of the Europa League before losing to eventual winners Aston Villa.

3 Glasner joined Forest on a three-year contract Credit: Getty

Glasner will be aiming to get Forest competing at the other end of the table, but will have to do so without Elliot Anderson.

The England midfielder completed a then British-record move to Manchester City in July.

Speaking to talkSPORT from their pre-season camp in Portugal, Glasner said: "It was decided that he will leave and I think that's what we have to accept and we are not at the end of the food chain in football.

"Probably our best players will always have big offers and then it is when. And at the end if we decide that we sell a player there are always two reasons.

"So number one is you need the money due to financial reasons. That was not the case here at Nottingham.

"Or the second part is that you believe that you can strengthen your team, but that doesn't mean just on this one position.

"I think it's not possible to get a better player right now than Elliot Anderson was for Nottingham Forest, but maybe we can add one or two more players on other positions where we can get better as a team and that's what we try to do."

On his relationship with Marinakis, Glasner admitted his ambition made the job an attractive one.

He added: “It was one of the crucial parts, his ambition is that he wants to bring Nottingham Forest back where it has been step by step

“We have a very good relationship, we have a very honest relationship, that's what I told him.

“I never tell somebody what he wants to hear, I always tell him my honest opinion. I think that's what everybody deserves and also Mr Marinakis.

“That doesn't mean that we always have the same opinion and then we discuss.

“But so far we have a great relationship because we have one big goal together and that is improving Nottingham Forest and making step by step into the top half of the Premier League.”

Forest begin their season at home to Leeds on August 22.

Sports.title: Troy Deeney: Jose Mourinho gave me direct advice after I beat Manchester United, then nearly signed me at Tottenham
Sports.content:
Troy Deeney: Jose Mourinho gave me direct advice after I beat Manchester United, then nearly signed me at Tottenham

Troy Deeney once received a foul-mouthed piece of advice from Jose Mourinho after beating his Manchester United side.

The former Watford striker had been on the scoresheet in a Premier League triumph at Vicarage Road.

5 Deeney was given some surprise advice by Mourinho after beating his United side Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Mourinho's side were beaten 3-1 back in September 2016 as he suffered a third successive for the first time in 14 years.

The Red Devils side that day featured the likes of Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Marcus Rashford, Wayne Rooney and Paul Pogba.

However, they were unable to see off the Hornets, with Deeney scoring a stoppage time penalty to cap off their victory.

It was one of four goals he scored in ten meetings with United for Watford.

Deeney only scored more Premier League goals against Aston Villa (six) and Bournemouth (five) during his career.

Mourinho advice

His performance was also enough to impress Mourinho, who spoke to him in a chance encounter after the full-time whistle.

Speaking to talkSPORT.com in 2024, Deeney recalled: "He’s a legend because he's straight talking as well, whenever I've encountered him.

"My first encounter with Jose, we beat Man United at Vicarage Road. 3-1, we beat them. And I scored.

"I remember I went up to the family bit, I had some friends there and said hello.

"Then I was coming back down the stairs to go across to my family in my box. He was on the phone on the stairs, and I just stood waiting.

5 Deeney scored in a 3-1 home win for the Hornets against a United side featuring Rooney, Rashford and Pogba Credit: Getty

"I didn't want to interrupt him or ask him to move. And then he clocked me, said to whoever on the phone to give him a second or whatever, he's speaking Portuguese.

"He said to me, ‘You okay?’ I was like, ‘Oh yeah, I just wanted to get past, I didn't want to interrupt you’.

"And he said, ‘You just beat us 3-1, you can do whatever the f*** you want’.

"I was like, ‘Oh cool’. Then we just laughed and joked, but he told me, you played well, good luck for the future. And I said the same.

"That was when United had Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Wayne Rooney up front. It was proper.

"With Marcus [Rashford] on the left, [Marouane] Fellaini and Pogba in the middle. It was a proper outfit."

5 Mourinho was subjected to a third successive loss in September 2016 by Deeney's Watford Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Deeney to Spurs

Following the win over Mourinho's United, Deeney came close to playing under him several years later.

Having been sacked by the Red Devils in December 2018, he returned to England 11 months later as Tottenham Hotspur manager.

During the following summer transfer window in 2020, Mourinho was keen to sign a centre forward to serve as back-up to Harry Kane.

Although his priority target was then Benfica striker Carlos Vinicius, a move for Deeney was also considered, he revealed.

Recalling Mourinho's interest, he added: "Vinicius was their main one, and it got to a point that if that didn’t happen, then we'll bring Troy in.

5 Deeney was told he can do 'whatever the f*** he wants' by Mourinho after the match Credit: Getty

"I had a chat with Mourinho, and it was like, what do you want to do? How do you want to do it?

"I remember it was a quick turnaround as well, from the COVID season ending in July, and then we played again in September.

"So, it was more like, would you be able to go from being a main man to one of the squad? Because I was the main man at Watford, and I was captain. And my conversation was like, ‘Look, if I get the opportunity to play, then I'll play’.

"Because I was trying to think, remember the big Spanish striker that went there from Swansea [Fernando Llorente]. He kept scoring, didn't he? Every time, League Cup and all that.

"And I was thinking, if I can do that, my job's good. I said, all I'm going to do is push Harry to be the best version that he can, and be his biggest cheerleader. Playing for Spurs is massively beyond my dreams.

"He said, OK, if we can't get this done, then we'll get that one done. Because obviously Vinicius was younger, age profile...

5 Mourinho called Deeney to discuss a move to Spurs in 2020 Credit: AFP

"I understood it, and he was straight with me, which was easy. And then, unfortunately for me, they got the Vinicius deal done."

Spurs would go on to sign Vinicius on loan, whilst Deeney scored seven goals in 19 matches to fire Watford to promotion back to the Premier League.

Sports.title: Jason Cundy stuns talkSPORT hosts as he storms into studio before making huge Chelsea statement
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy stuns talkSPORT hosts as he storms into studio before making huge Chelsea statement

Jason Cundy is back from his holiday, and he's come steaming in to tell the world that the Premier League title is Chelsea's this season.

The huge Chelsea fan and former player has been away from talkSPORT Towers since the World Cup, but his first appearance back hosting The Sports Bar saw him go out on a limb.



4 Cundy is backing the club he loves to spoil Arsenal's Premier League title defence

He's backing his beloved Blues to end their ten-year wait for a title, citing a 'cheat code' that they have on their rivals.

Cundy backs Chelsea to win Premier League

“I’m going to make a statement now. There is no reason why Chelsea cannot win this title. In fact, I’m going to say it. Chelsea will win the title," Cundy said on Monday night's Sports Bar.

“There is something about Chelsea. We have got a cheat code. I’m not proud of it but we can win the title for a number of reasons.



“Have you seen our front three? Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer - Palmer’s had a rest, Joao Pedro’s had a rest.

“Our midfield, the recruitment at the back. It almost certainly looks like we could be playing three at the back with someone in Xabi Alonso who knows how to win a title.



“One game a week, we saw how beneficial that could be when Antonio Conte came in, went to three at the back. Win the title.

“History is going to repeat itself. I never go out on a limb when I talk about Chelsea but I said Arsenal will win it for the last three seasons and eventually they did.



“Gooners, you should be fearful of Chelsea. Yes, you’re favourites, I get it. You’ve got an unbelievable team.

“But I’ve got to tell you there’s a cheat code and that’s Chelsea playing one game a week and a manager in Xabi Alonso who knows how to win a title.

“There are only two managers in this league that have won a title - Xabi Alonso and Mikel Arteta. Liverpool, new manager. Andoni Iraola doesn’t know how to win a title.

4 Chelsea boss Alonso guided Bayer Leverkusen to Bundesliga glory for the first time ever in the 2023/24 season, the team going unbeaten for the entire league season Credit: AFP



“De Zerbi at Spurs, what’s he won? Carrick, what’s he won?"

Cundy admitted he still has reservations about Robert Sanchez still being Chelsea's first choice goalkeeper, before putting those worries to one side and bellowing: “CHELSEA win the Premier League title.”

The Blues have bought well and spent a lot of money, with Morgan Rogers the standout recruit following his British record transfer from Aston Villa to add another attacking option.

Veteran Premier League stars Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson bring experience, while the defence is being bolstered as well.

Marco Palestra and Maxence Lacroix have both made the move to west London.



Full-back Palestra made the £47million move from Atalanta, while Lacroix will offer proven quality following his arrival from Crystal Palace in a deal worth £52million.

4 Alonso comes with pedigree and he's been backed in the transfer window, signing Rogers on a British record deal Credit: Getty

Cundy unveils new look

Earlier in the evening, Cundy made an appearance on Transfer Insiders, where he copped a dig from hosts Flex and Abbi Summer for being away for so long.

And that prompted Cundy to storm into the studio and take a seat, although it was his transformation with his barnet following a hair transplant that blew Summers and Flex away.



As he walked in, Flex said: "Who is this? It's a new man. You look incredible. I am being deadly serious

Clearly chuffed with the results, Cundy responded: "It's nuts, isn't it. It's got body and a little lift."

Sports.title: Every Premier League club ranked as final 2026/27 league table predicted
Sports.content:
The most open and unpredictable Premier League season is almost upon us as another season of twists and turns awaits.

Champions Arsenal unofficially kick off the season against FA Cup winners Manchester City in the Community Shield, live on talkSPORT.



9 Will it be Arsenal and Man City going head-to-head for the title once more? Credit: Getty

The two teams finished first and second in the table last year and are many neutrals' pick to duke it out for the title again in 2026/27.

However, City are among the nine of the 20 top-flight teams that will begin the new campaign with a different manager.

The World Cup has also wreaked havoc on many clubs' pre-season plans, with some stars reporting to training late and others carrying varying degrees of injuries.



It's also important not to hold too much stock in friendly results: Liverpool lost three such matches in the summer of 2019 ahead of winning 26 of their first 27 league games en route to lifting the title.

Arsenal, meanwhile, have just lost back-to-back fixtures this month - but remain the bookies' favourite to defend their crown come May.



With that in mind, here is where all 20 sides rank in talkSPORT's predicted Premier League standings (insert apology for your respective team's position here).

Arsenal

The Gunners held off a spirited challenge from Man City to win the club's first Premier League title in 22 years last season.



Mikel Arteta may have missed out on a few key targets since then, most notably Vinicius Junior extending his stay at Real Madrid.

But, Arsenal have signed one of the best Premier League midfielders in Newcastle skipper Bruno Guimaraes.

And, with the exception of Leandro Trossard, they have also kept the core of the squad widely regarded as the deepest in the division.

With the added experience from both manager and players in how to get over the line, Arsenal remain the favourites to defend their title.



talkSPORT Prediction: 1st

9 Arsenal will be preparing for a title-defending campaign Credit: Getty

Aston Villa

Unai Emery has worked miracles at Villa Park since his arrival and again overperformed last season to finish fourth.

The Spaniard has since seen stars plucked from his ranks once more, with Morgan Rogers completing a £117million move to Chelsea, while Manchester United snapped up Youri Tielemans for £35m.

Set-piece coach Austin MacPhee has also departed the club, with Ezri Konsa the latest to be linked with the exit door.



The arrival of Alejandro Garnacho has done little to inspire fans, and considering Villa slipped to sixth the last time they were in the Champions League, it looks an uphill battle for Emery once again.

talkSPORT Prediction: 7th

9 Unai Emery has lost a number of key players this summer Credit: Getty

Bournemouth

The Cherries will play in Europe this season for the first time in their history after going on an epic 18-game unbeaten run in manager Andoni Iraola's final few months.

The Spaniard has since taken the reins at Liverpool, with Marco Rose tasked with juggling Europa League commitments this campaign.



In Bournemouth's defence, they have still not even lost a Premier League game since January and have resisted the mass exodus of their stars this summer that has plagued the club in recent years.

But Eli Junior Kroupi will be missing for months after undergoing surgery, and the extra fixtures coupled with a manager new to English football suggest the south-coast outfit could struggle.

talkSPORT Prediction: 14th

Brentford

Keith Andrews surprised all the critics who tipped the Bees for relegation last season by masterminding a European push.

Brentford ultimately fell short of a historic campaign by finishing ninth, and it could prove to be a massive case of what if for the club - with Jordan Henderson also ripping up his contract to join Chelsea.



Their alarming dip in form at the end of last season can't be ignored either - with their only win in their final 10 Premier League games from the start of March coming against relegated West Ham.

Igor Thiago also scored over 40 per cent of the Bees' 55 goals, the highest per cent any individual contributed to one term in 2025/26.

Brentford have never had a player score over 20 Premier League goals in multiple seasons, and a drop in his output could prove hugely damaging for Andrews' side - with back-up Callum Wilson only managing seven in the top-flight last year.

talkSPORT Prediction: 17th

9 Brentford won just one of their final 10 Premier League games Credit: Getty



Brighton

The Seagulls boasted the seventh best home record in the Premier League last season en route to qualifying for Europe in eighth.

Yet Brighton proved their issues coping on two fronts in 2023/24, when their Europa League adventures saw them finish 11th.

And it might prove to be a similar story for Fabian Hurzeler's men this season, despite the coup signing of Luka Vuskovic from Tottenham, replacing Jan Paul van Hecke, who moved to Spurs in a separate deal.

But Brighton have lost Danny Welbeck after the best goalscoring return of his career, with long-time servants Adam Webster and Solly March exiting on free transfers and James Milner retiring.



talkSPORT Prediction: 11th

Chelsea

The Blues will have ambitions of being the league's dark horses despite finishing out of Europe for the second time in six years.

Antonio Conte won the title in 2016/17 with no European football, with Mauricio Pochettino also improving the team by six places and 19 points from 12th in 2022/23 in similar circumstances.

Xabi Alonso has been backed heavily, with a transfer record for a British player spent on Rogers alongside £52m for Maxence Lacroix.

Crucially, Chelsea now also have several experienced heads in the dressing room in English pair Henderson and Welbeck, similar to how Alonso utilised Granit Xhaka and Robert Andrich in his dominant Bayer Leverkusen side.



However, World Cup winner Marc Cucurella officially departed Stamford Bridge in June, and it seems a tall ask for a developing team to instantly challenge for the top honours - securing Champions League football should be the main aim.

talkSPORT Prediction: 4th

9 Chelsea have completed the £117million signing of Morgan Rogers this summer Credit: Getty

Coventry City

Frank Lampard will always have credit in the bank with the Sky Blue faithful after ending their 25-year wait to regain top-flight status.

Club captain Matt Grimes even told talkSPORT that the Chelsea legend is one of the world's best coaches.



However, the omens are far from ideal - only in four of the Premier League's 31 seasons have the three relegation spots not been occupied by a promoted club.

And Lampard's recent record as a Premier League manager doesn't read pretty - a win percentage of just 27.27 per cent at Everton, while he won only one of his 11 games during his second Chelsea stint.

Coventry have also had a relatively quiet window, while it remains to be seen whether the trio of Haji Wright, Brandon Thomas-Asante and Ellis Simms can replicate their Championship goal-scoring feats at the top level.

talkSPORT Prediction: 19th

Crystal Palace

The Eagles have had the best two seasons in their history with FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League glory.



But Palace may find themselves going backwards this year, with star defender Lacroix following manager Oliver Glasner out the door.

Splashing what was briefly a club record £35m on Brennan Johnson in January only to swap him for Dwight McNeil half a year later doesn't evoke a heap of confidence from the Palace hierarchy.

With the added demand of Europa League football this term, new head coach Pierre Sage has had to contend with free transfers to shape his squad in Oscar Mingueza and Takehiro Tomiyasu.

Sage was sacked by Lyon halfway into his only managerial season juggling European football, and with Palace fans expecting another positive showing on the continent after last year, it could come at the cost of improving on their 15th-placed Premier League finish.



talkSPORT Prediction: 15th

Everton

Toffees fan and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has boldly predicted his beloved team to finish seventh.

Yet it's hard to forget Everton's dismal end to last season, which had them in the relegation zone from April 11th to their final game - as one of only three teams without a Premier League win in that spell alongside relegated Wolves and Burnley.

David Moyes has put a lot of trust in youngsters Tyrique George and Hayden Hackney to take to regular Premier League football quickly.

Iliman Ndiaye is in talks to join Al Hilal, while the bulk of the goalscoring burden will fall again to Beto and Thierno Barry - who have both never reached double figures in the Premier League.



talkSPORT Prediction: 13th

9 Everton were just three points off the Champions League places with seven games left last season but then imploded Credit: Getty

Fulham

Alvaro Arbeloa has already been tipped to be the first Premier League manager sacked this season before his first official game.

The Cottagers have even been tipped for relegation by talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor, such is the risk they've taken in appointing the Spaniard as Marco Silva's successor.

Arbeloa has just five months of senior managerial experience to his name and has spent the bulk of the club's transfer kitty on two youthful Real Madrid starlets in Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios.



Meanwhile, Fulham have lost their two leading scorers from last season with Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez departing as free agents; Alex Iwobi, in third, only managed four Premier League goals.

talkSPORT Prediction: 16th

Hull City

The Championship Play-Off final winners have so far only spent money on goalkeepers Jack Butland and Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Hull owner Acun Ilicali was bullish on talkSPORT about his side's chances of staying up, but a mixture of inexperience and the overall squad's quality make them heavy favourites to go back down.

The Tigers haven't played in the Premier League since 2017, and manager Sergej Jakirovic has never led a team at this level.



Sunderland, in similar circumstances this time last summer, became the fourth-highest-spending promoted club ever - which means Hull will need something pretty spectacular to give themselves a chance.

talkSPORT Prediction: 20th

Ipswich Town

talkSPORT.com is sadly predicting a return to the successive 2023/24 and 2024/25 seasons that saw all three promoted clubs relegated.

That latter campaign involved Ipswich, who returned to the Championship in 19th, and that recent experience might just be enough to stand the club in a better stead than Coventry and Hull.

The Tractor Boys have a new boss in Gary O'Neil following the departure of promotion-winning manager Kieran McKenna.



Abdul Fatawu, Daizen Maeda, and Issa Diop are all eye-catching signings to make a stab at survival, but the overall quality of the squad will likely still see them finish in the bottom three come May.

talkSPORT Prediction: 18th

9 Ipswich celebrated wildly by booking their place back in the top-flight Credit: Getty

Leeds United

Daniel Farke's side have plenty of reasons to believe that the possibility of replicating Leeds' ninth-placed finish in 2021 is in reach.

Having consolidated their place in the Premier League last season in 14th, the club then beat out plenty of competition to pick up Wilson.



The Welsh international scored 10 goals and assisted seven more last term, with Leeds also showing their intent by landing Tarik Muharemovic after his impressive showings in Serie A and breaking their transfer record to make James Trafford their new No.1.

All this points to the fact that simply avoiding relegation again is no longer the goal for the Whites: a top-half finish is more than possible.

talkSPORT Prediction: 9th

Liverpool

The Reds had a dismal season last year after finishing in fifth spot in the table - 25 points behind champions Arsenal - despite a record-breaking £446million splurge.

Arne Slot was sacked, and Andoni Iraola is the man tasked with bridging the gap and will need plenty of help in the market to do so - namely in a potential double transfer raid on Paris Saint-Germain for wingers Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.



There is no Mohamed Salah, who has joined Trabzonspor on a free transfer, but Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz both need and are expected to have far greater second seasons at Anfield.

Isak remains one of the world's best strikers - with injuries restricting him to just three goals in 14 Premier League outings last term - and an uninterrupted pre-season could see him reignite a squad who are just 14 months removed from winning the title.

Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo has been loaned as an emergency defensive reinforcement, but Iraola is still in dire need of further depth at both ends of the pitch, and failure to act before the window shuts could mean the difference between a title challenge or another fight to secure a European spot.

talkSPORT Prediction: 2nd

9 Isak managed just four goals in all competitions last season Credit: Getty



Manchester City

Pep Guardiola’s 10-year reign at the Etihad is over, and his former assistant Enzo Maresca has incredibly large shoes to fill as new head coach.

Bernardo Silva, John Stones, and Nathan Ake have all left a sizable hole of experience and leadership in the dressing room.

But the biggest miss will undoubtedly be the expected exit of irreplaceable Rodri to either Barcelona or Real Madrid.

The Spaniard, who won the Ballon d'Or in 2024, claimed the Golden Ball at the 2026 World Cup, and £116m man Elliot Anderson will instantly be under massive pressure to shoulder the midfield burden.



Last season's Golden Boot winner Erling Haaland will be sure to fire City into the title conversation whatever the makeup of Maresca's side looks like, but it does ultimately feel to be a season of transition.

talkSPORT Prediction: 3rd

Manchester United

Michael Carrick impressed after fixing the mess left behind by Ruben Amorim to guide the Red Devils to a third-place finish.

Yet the 45-year-old has been left very short in a bid to challenge on multiple fronts after qualifying for the Champions League.

United refused to engage in bidding wars for Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, with the club also beaten by City for Anderson.



Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans are shrewd midfield signings, but that area remains light after Casemiro's exit, and Manuel Ugarte, who is a long-term absentee through injury, with Mason Mount as well having a suspect fitness record.

Man United jumping from 15th to third in one year shows the value of not playing in Europe - and with that benefit going to two of the club's biggest rivals for a Champions League place in Chelsea and Spurs, it could be a major cause of concern if further recruitment isn't made.

talkSPORT Prediction: 5th

9 Michael Carrick is gearing up for his first full season as Manchester United manager Credit: Getty

Newcastle

The Toon Army may have had the summer from hell on paper, but there is plenty for fans to remain optimistic about.



Former club captain Guimaraes has departed to join Arsenal in a £75m deal to follow fellow high-profile players Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon in leaving for pastures new.

But the squad had grown stale under former boss Eddie Howe, and Matthias Jaissle has an opportunity to start the rebuild job at Newcastle in a season where fans won't be expecting much.

There is hope that Yoanne Wissa can take his World Cup form into his second season at St James' Park under Jaissle's favourable system.

The Magpies additionally won't have the added strain of playing in Europe this year, with a top-half finish and a cup run both reasonable expectations.



talkSPORT Prediction: 10th

Nottingham Forest

Forest are coming off a chaotic campaign that featured four managerial changes, a relegation battle, and a run to the Europa League semi-finals.

The arrival of Oliver Glasner as head coach is not only a major coup, but a chance for the club to enjoy some much-needed stability.

The loss of Anderson is undoubtedly a blow, but the overall squad assembled by Evangelos Marinakis was always more representative of one who finished seventh in 2024/25 than 16th last season.

Spearheaded by Morgan Gibbs-White, who bagged 18 goals in all competitions, Glasner will be itching to prove he can translate his success in cup competitions to the league.



talkSPORT Prediction: 8th

Sunderland

Regis Le Bris' men bucked all recent trends for Premier League promoted sides by qualifying for the Europa League last season.

But shocking the world for a second time will be an extremely tall order, with the squad looking very much the same as last campaign.

Sunderland did manage to keep signing of the season, Granit Xhaka, out of Chelsea's clutches, while adding Thomas Meunier's experience.

The demands of consistent Thursday/Sunday football on the Black Cats will take its toll on any domestic ambitions - with a comfortable finish away from a relegation fight enough for fans to really savour those European trips.



talkSPORT Prediction: 12th

Tottenham

Spurs have endured successive 17th-placed finishes in the Premier League, but there is genuine cause to hope brighter times are ahead.

For one, the Lilywhites have been the biggest spenders so far, splashing out nearly £250m, and they are not done yet.

The north London outfit have also broken their transfer record twice to revamp their midfield in the capture of Fernandes and Tonali.

Roberto De Zerbi won't have the extra demands of European football in his first full season at the helm, and he's demonstrated the impact he can make during his short stint in charge of Tottenham.



The issue for Spurs remains the lack of an elite goalscorer, with Richarlison their top scorer in all competitions last year with just 12 goals.

talkSPORT Prediction: 6th

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton complete rare swap deal as Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil trade places - after Eagles held clear-the-air talks with star's girlfriend
Sports.content:
Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil have completed their respective swaps to Everton and Crystal Palace and signed four year contracts.

Johnson will join David Moyes' side, eight months after Palace signed him from Tottenham for a then club record fee of £35million, while McNeil will move from Merseyside to South London.

McNeil had been set to join the Eagles on Deadline Day in the winter and underwent his medical, but a deal that involved an initial loan with a £20m obligation to buy collapsed at the last minute.

That led to a furious reaction from Megan Sharpley, girlfriend of McNeil, who took to Instagram in a lengthy series of stories to hit out at what went on, including accusing Palace of messing with the winger's mental health.

Reports in The Times on Monday suggested that the club's co-owner and chairman Steve Parish held clear the air talks with Sharpley ahead of the transfer going through this time.

Last season, the Eagles had submitted a deal sheet for McNeil's move, but then failed to complete the relevant paperwork in time. Everton sources said they fulfilled their part but Palace went quiet on finalising paperwork, effectively pulling out, and the transfer ran out of time.

Brennan Johnson has completed a move to Everton from Crystal Palace in a rare swap deal

As part of the transfer, Dwight McNeil has moved the other way to link up with the Eagles after his transfer to the club on Deadline Day in the winter collapsed at the last moment

In a searing statement following the collapse of the move, Sharpley described the 'cruelty' of the football world, saying that McNeil had been 'toyed with until the final minute' and subsequently 'left broken hearted with nothing but confusion'.

She said: 'Dwight, I've always been in awe of your job,' she began. 'The way you've committed most of your life to achieve what only the 0.1 per cent achieve.

'I know you love your job, the sport and you know how lucky you are to do what most people only dream of.

'We appreciate our lives, how fortunate we are, and the millions of football fans that keep the game alive and ultimately keep you in a job you adore. You've sacrificed a lot and most people don't have much of an idea of the difficult hardships you've suffered and dealt with in your personal life. And we crack on, that's who we are, we appreciate how blessed our lives are.

'But the world doesn't seem to accept that someone as fortunate as you is allowed to suffer hardships and feel sad. But you're a human, a beautiful incredible 26-year-old human being. And no matter about money or the success you've worked so hard to achieve, you are allowed to feel.

'Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you.'

Sharpley continued: 'To have something promised to you, to have been dragged along on an emotional rollercoaster, and to be toyed with until the final minute.

'To have 4-and-a-half-years of your life promised to you, traveling, medicals, agreements made... promises made. To have prepared to move your entire life, our life 100 of miles away in the space of a few hours.

'For it to be torn away from you at the last second, with absolutely no explanation. Going from everything - to radio silence, no phone call, no communication and be left, broken hearted with nothing but confusion, has hurt more than I can say.

'I sit with you, knowing in my heart and deep down into my soul that you will bounce back from this. I am your biggest supporter. And I know you will overcome this with a fire in your belly and a motivation that no one can stop. I have already seen it tonight, even whilst you're facing the lowest point of your career.'

McNeil's girlfriend Megan Sharpley hit out at the 'cruel' world of football after that move collapsed

After a lengthy series of Instagram stories from Sharpley, McNeil also spoke on the matter

Sharpley reaffirmed her support for her partner and revealed he had been left in tears by the collapse of the transfer.

'We live in a world where everyone is aware how big of a problem mental health is,' she added. 'So in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money, that it's okay to mess and toy with their mental health and that's just 'part of the job'?

'No matter of money, we all deserve to be treated with respect, kindness and fairly. So I really question the industry tonight. I only hope there's more done in the future to protect people from situations like what I've witnessed tonight.

'Football is brutal and yes, it's the nature of the beast, but messing with human beings feelings and emotions shouldn't be acceptable. People only see one side on the media, you don't see the tears, the emotion and the distress I've seen tonight.

'Dwight, to the present, and the future. Every single thing happens for a reason, I will always believe what is meant for you will find you, and with your hard work and determination I'll never doubt only the best will come your way, and I'm so excited to see what you can achieve...

'So here's to carrying on being an Everton player. The support we've had from this club, especially during my illness, has meant a lot on our journey, so let's keep grinding, keep working and grafting for this badge. Let's keep going Dwight, show them who you are. I'm right by your side.'

The emotional post from Sharpley referenced her own illness when she was diagnosed with a large, serious tumour on her ovary and was forced to undergo urgent open surgery in December 2023. McNeil was praised for his unwavering support at the time.

The winger, who has played 128 times for Everton since joining from Burnley in 2022, also weighed in on the situation in regards to his failed move.

Sharing the final story from his partner, McNeil added: 'Whilst even now I'm still left in the dark. What I do know, and have been supported with, I am an Everton player. I will use this as motivation.

'I love you moo, I couldn't thank you enough for all of your love and support.'

Meanwhile, after completing his move to Merseyside, Johnson told evertontv: ‘I'm so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it's a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.

'There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in. You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I'm a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.'

He becomes the fifth summer signing for David Moyes’ squad after Merlin Rohl’s loan obligation was activated along with the additions of Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Christian Norgaard.

McNeil has signed his four-year contract with Palace and said: 'The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It’s something that I want to be a part of, so I’m really looking forward to getting started.'

Sports.title: Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move - with Chelsea set for a windfall -as Napoli offer £2m loan fee for Blues defender Benoit Badiashile, and Liverpool teenager wanted on loan in Portugal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move - with Chelsea set for a windfall -as Napoli offer £2m loan fee for Blues defender Benoit Badiashile, and Liverpool teenager wanted on loan in Portugal: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Fulham snap up Southampton's Charles

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons.

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year contract, tying him to Craven Cottage until June 2031, with a club option to extend by a further 12 months.

Southampton also retain a 20percent sell-on.

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons

Speaking to FFCtv, Charles, who will wear the number 19 shirt, said: 'It’s a great club, with a really good vision – the manager explained that to me. To be here is a massive privilege.

'I hope to really kickstart my Premier League career. At such a good club as well, it’s perfect for me, and hopefully perfect for the fans as well.

'I’m buzzing to finally get it over the line. The club has got a really good foundation, from the bottom to the top really.'

Lukaku agrees Turkey move

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli.

The Belgium international has agreed a two year contract worth around £8.6m a season and has already passed his medical.

The deal includes further add ons based on performances.

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli

Chelsea are understood to have inserted a 40percent sell-on clause when they sold Lukaku for a knockdown £26m to Napoli two years ago.

He scored 14 goals in his first season but injury and the arrival of Rasmus Hojlund from Manchester United restricted him to just seven games last year.

Liverpool starlet wanted in Portugal

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move.

The 18-year-old who has joined the club from Austria Vienna in a £2.5million deal has stood out for the first team in pre-season friendlies.

But despite the promise he has shown, and Liverpool's dearth of defensive cover, post-Brexit rules mean Austria youth international Ndukwe doesn't have enough points to obtain a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE) to obtain a work visa.

He will start against Como in their last friendly but is unable to play a competitive match for the Anfield club.

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move

Now clubs from Germany, Spain, Denmark and France have been calling to take the 6ft 6ins centre back on loan but there is a sense Portugal may be his preferred destination.

After playing alongside him, captain Virgil van Dijk said: 'Big talent, big guy and he wants to learn. I had a brief conversation with him, especially in the last couple of days. For him, it is just progressing. I know he has to go on loan I think so let's see where he ends up.'

Napoli still in the hunt for Badiashile

Napoli have offered a £2m loan fee for Chelsea's £30million-rated centre-back Benoit Badiashile with obligation to buy.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs and the player's representatives to try and find a full agreement.

Chelsea have sold Trevoh Chalobah to Como and are also looking to sell Axel Disasi who has had interest from Crystal Palace and West Ham.

Napoli are continuing talks to sign Chelsea's £30m-rated centre-back Beniot Badiashile (right)

Mamadou Sarr, who suffered an injury at the weekend, is likely to go on loan to a Premier League side.

Keeper Filip Jorgensen has completed his move to Strasbourg on loan.

Wigan Athletic are closing in on their loan move for Chelsea midfielder Reggie Walsh while Portsmouth want 17-year-old Chelsea winger Ryan Kavuma-McQueen on loan.

Napoli remain keen on Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus also as talks continue. Arsenal want £20m for the Brazilian.

Villa defender wanted in Belgium

Aston Villa right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic is a target for Rangers along with Hugo Siquet of Bruges.

Nedeljkovic has had interest from a number of clubs including Osasuna but Rangers are exploring a £4million deal with initial loan for the Serbia international.

The 20-year-old had a spell with RB Leipzig last season.

Burnley after new keeper

Burnley are showing interest in OH Leuven goalkeeper Tobe Leysen.

The 24-year-old former Belgium U21 international has one year left on contract so Leuven are willing to listen to offers.

Click below for all the transfer developments over the last few days...
