Sports.title: Verstappen vs Hadjar: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar began his first full season at Red Bull knowing that the last driver in the same position as him lasted just two rounds before being booted out.

That must have been a daunting prospect to contemplate, though it bears pointing out that the senior race team management has changed significantly at Red Bull since Liam Lawson was shown the door after his pair of starts for the team last year.

The more experienced Yuki Tsunoda took Lawson’s place and became the latest in a series of drivers whose reputations took a brutal battering from occupying the garage adjacent to Max Verstappen’s. Tsunoda mustered just 7.2% of Red Bull’s points while alongside Verstappen.

This is the context in which to assess Hadjar’s performance this year. His 8-2 deficit in qualifying is nothing to brag about but he has been much closer to Verstappen over a single flying lap than his predecessors.

Hadjar has done vastly better at collecting points, too, claiming 38% of Red Bull’s score so far. True, compared to Tsunoda he’s had the benefit of a wider field spread between Red Bull and the midfield, but even so he’s already taken more than twice as many points as Tsunoda managed over his 22-race stint at the team last year.

He has achieved this alongside a formidable talent in a car which both drivers have termed “undriveable” on occasions. While the high level Verstappen operates at is so familiar it can almost be taken for granted (his superb second place in Hungary, for example), Hadjar has done a more than respectable job alongside him so far.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Which of Antonelli’s rivals is his biggest threat for the championship this year? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s strong position in the lead of the championship standings at the summer break is remarkable enough already for a driver in his second season in Formula 1.

But what makes his position all the more impressive is that, arguably, no single driver has yet emerged as his clear rival. Antonelli has won six of the 11 rounds so far, more than the rest put together, and only his team mate George Russell has taken multiple wins.

Despite that, Russell is not Antonelli’s closest rival in the standings: Lewis Hamilton is leading a resurgent Ferrari. Plus, the final round before the summer break saw McLaren claim their first victory of the season. Three of the last five grands prix were won by teams other than Mercedes – could Antonelli biggest threat come from one of them?

Lewis Hamilton

50 points behind

The possibility of Hamilton fighting for the championship against the driver who took the Mercedes seat he vacated last year is a compelling narrative. But is it a likely outcome? Hamilton is Antonelli’s closest rival in the points but has missed opportunities due to penalties in recent races.

George Russell

59 points behind

Russell should be Antonelli’s closest rival for the championship but various factors have left him well behind including unreliability (not that Antonelli has been immune), some misfortune and his risky first-lap lunge at Spa. He’s also on course to incur a power unit change penalty before his team mate. Still, Russell should have the equipment and the experience to put Antonelli under pressure.

Charles Leclerc

81 points behind

Hamilton may be closer to Antonelli in the standings but Charles Leclerc has arguably looked more competitive. Providing he avoids a repeat of the dip he fell into around Spain and Monaco, he could emerge as Antonelli’s biggest threat.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Lando Norris

91 points behind

Like Mercedes, unreliability has dogged McLaren this year. They often haven’t been quick enough either, though Norris has now won both a grand prix and a sprint race. The MCL40’s Hungaroring upgrade clearly paid off, and may prove enough to bring the McLarens into regular contention. The reigning world champion is a long way behind, though.

Max Verstappen

110 points behind

If last year demonstrated anything, it is unwise to write off Max Verstappen if he is not mathematically out of contention. Having been 104 points off the lead with 249 remaining, he eventually lost by the narrowest margin in F1 history (relatively). But lying 110 points behind in a car which hasn’t won a grand prix yet may be too much even for him.

Oscar Piastri

127 points behind

Oscar Piastri has proved a close match on pace for his team mate as usual but he’s even further behind in the standings. He went into the final round of last season with a shot at the championship but that doesn’t look likely to happen this year.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Isack Hadjar

151 points behind

Isack Hadjar has impressed with the quality of his performances alongside Verstappen and may yet recover the points he dropped after losing his podium finish in Monaco. But his points deficit to Antonelli is surely too large and the Red Bull not competitive enough yet for him to be a realistic title contender.

I say

Hamilton may be closest in the points but Russell surely has the better combination of opportunity and equipment at the moment. If he can stop the rot in the second half of the season I would back him to put Antonelli under pressure for the title.

Sports.title: Jerry Quarry Destroys Earnie Shavers in 141 Seconds
Sports.content:
Both fighters were 28. Quarry weighed 202 pounds, eight lighter than Shavers.

The buildup had almost guaranteed violence. Quarry predicted three rounds and believed he could finish Shavers in one if his opponent came after him. Don King, then part of Shavers’ management team, called it their easiest fight. Madison Square Garden matchmaker Teddy Brenner went further, predicting the shortest 12-round fight in history. He wasn’t far off.

Trainer Gil Clancy wanted Quarry to box, but Quarry abandoned that idea almost immediately. Instead of giving Shavers room to unleash his power, he attacked him.

Quarry drove Shavers toward the ropes and unloaded lefts and rights to the head. Shavers managed to move away, but Quarry followed him across the ring and dropped him with a left-right combination.

Shavers got back up, only to find Quarry waiting for him. Quarry poured on punches as Shavers struggled to defend himself. His eyes looked unfocused, and he was taking clean shots without answering effectively. Referee Arthur Mercante had seen enough and stopped the fight at 2:21 of the opening round. There would be no need for judges Jack Gordon and Bill Recht.

The result was stunning because Quarry had beaten the knockout artist by fighting him at his own game. George Foreman, Joe Frazier, and Muhammad Ali were among the prominent names at ringside. Foreman reportedly expressed surprise that Quarry had chosen to trade with Shavers and came away impressed by his aggression.

Ali and Frazier had another reason to be at the Garden. Their January 28, 1974 rematch was already set for the same arena and was promoted during the Quarry-Shavers telecast. Frazier discussed getting his weight down and preparing for Ali before the main event, while viewers were urged to buy tickets for their second fight.

Their rematch also strengthened Quarry’s position in the heavyweight picture. With Ali and Frazier committed to fighting each other, the broadcast team noted that neither man would likely be available for Foreman until around June. Quarry’s destruction of Shavers suddenly made him an obvious candidate to challenge the champion before then.

Quarry paid a physical price despite the short night. He injured his left wrist after landing a hook high on Shavers’ head, with reports raising concern over a possible fracture.

Shavers later admitted that the first heavy blows had left him unable to recover. He regretted rising so quickly after the knockdown, believing that taking more of the count might have given him enough time to survive the remaining seconds of the round.

Nearly 15,000 spectators had come expecting to see what happened when Shavers’ frightening power collided with Quarry’s durability and experience. They barely had time to settle into their seats.

The official attendance was 14,962, producing a gate of $201,564. Quarry was guaranteed $40,000 against 30 percent of the gate, while Shavers received $30,000 against 27½ percent.

The victory strengthened Quarry’s position near the top of a stacked division ruled by Foreman, but the championship opportunity never followed. Quarry instead met Frazier again the following year and was stopped in five rounds.

Shavers rebuilt his career and eventually challenged both Ali and Larry Holmes for the heavyweight championship.

Neither man’s later career changed what happened that December night. Shavers arrived with the reputation as a devastating slugger, but Quarry never gave him enough time to use it.

For 141 seconds, Quarry simply beat him to the punch.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Wants Haney To Stew In Loss
Sports.content:
“I’m not in a rush to make that fight happen. They have to sit with that loss,” Ryan told The Ring. “Why do I have to beg for it? I’m here. I’m about to beat up Conor Benn. I want Teofimo Lopez, Rolando Romero and Shakur Stevenson. I have a lot of options. I’m not really worried about Haney now. If it happens, it happens.”

What happened in April 2024 remains the source of the hostility. Garcia dropped Haney three times and won a majority decision before the victory was changed to a no-contest following his positive test for ostarine.

Devin and Bill Haney have repeatedly brought up the failed test since then, refusing to treat the original outcome as a legitimate defeat. Drug testing has also been a recurring subject whenever another fight with Garcia has been discussed.

Ryan’s refusal to rush into a rematch sounds personal. He has the WBC welterweight title, a September fight with Benn, and several lucrative opponents he can pursue without giving Haney an opportunity to settle the score.

“All these guys obviously have to come to me,” Ryan said. “I’m definitely the lottery fight. If you want to be a huge name, I’m the guy to do it [against]. You have to get through me.”

That is the position Garcia believes he occupies. After two years of hearing why his performance against Haney shouldn’t count, he doesn’t seem interested in helping Team Haney put it behind them.

They can sit with it.

Sports.title: Archie Moore Rallies To Stop Harold Johnson In 14
Sports.content:
Moore weighed 173 pounds to Johnson’s 172½.

Working behind his jab, movement and counterpunching, Johnson frustrated Moore through much of the early and middle rounds. His advantage grew in the 10th when a right hand behind the ear dropped the champion.

Moore rose quickly, but referee Ruby Goldstein continued counting, overlooking that the automatic eight-count had been waived for the championship fight. Moore recovered and continued pursuing Johnson.

The challenger remained in front as the fight moved into the late rounds. Two officials had Johnson leading after 13, putting Moore in danger of losing his championship on the scorecards.

Then Moore changed the fight. He hurt Johnson late in the 13th and attacked immediately when the 14th began. A barrage of rights and lefts drove Johnson into his own corner before sending him to the canvas.

Johnson regained his feet, but he was badly hurt. Moore followed him along the ropes and continued punching until Goldstein stopped the fight at 56 seconds of the 14th round.

The comeback preserved Moore’s championship and extended his winning streak to 19 fights. Johnson had come within two rounds of taking the title from a rival he had first fought in 1949.

Moore soon resumed his pursuit of heavyweight champion Rocky Marciano. He received the opportunity the following year, dropping Marciano before being stopped in the ninth round.

Johnson never received the sixth Moore fight he wanted. Years later, he became light heavyweight champion himself.

Their August 1954 battle closed a five-fight rivalry with its most dramatic ending. Johnson had the lead, but the Old Mongoose found the punches he needed before time ran out.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Escalates Fury-Joshua Fight Over MSG
Sports.content:
“We signed for this fight in the UK,” Hearn said to Fighthype. “We are desperate to deliver this fight for UK fans. However, everybody else wants the fight in America: Turki Alalshikh, Netflix. I can’t speak on behalf of Tyson Fury; I don’t see him kicking up a fuss. Madison Square Garden. So, they’re telling us this is the place it’s going to do the biggest numbers, this is the place it’ll be the biggest fight.”

Hearn has made his preference for Britain clear for weeks. What changes the discussion is how far he now sounds prepared to push the disagreement.

“I disagree. But at the end we’ll fight, and we’ll fight, and we’ll fight to a point where they’ve breached the contract by doing it in America, or we come to an agreement.”

That is strong language considering Hearn’s business relationship with Alalshikh and the number of major events Matchroom has staged with his involvement.

Hearn also admits the people on the other side of the venue dispute are key allies, making his willingness to discuss a potential breach of agreement more surprising.

His stated reason is loyalty to British boxing fans. But if Madison Square Garden really produces the bigger commercial event, Hearn’s resistance becomes harder to explain purely as a business decision.

There is also no indication that Fury shares Hearn’s resistance to New York. Hearn concedes he doesn’t see Fury “kicking up a fuss” about Madison Square Garden, potentially leaving Matchroom as the strongest opposition to the proposed move.

The dispute has therefore moved beyond a simple choice between Britain and New York. Hearn is now openly discussing how far Matchroom will go to enforce the agreement it signed.

Sports.title: Conor Benn Embraces Underdog Role Against Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Eubank was already in his mid-30s for those fights, yet bookmakers still favored him. That was understandable given how thin Benn’s resume was against top opposition before their rivalry.

The rematch also came with weight conditions affecting the naturally larger Eubank. More importantly, Eubank wasn’t the type of dangerous one-punch counterpuncher Benn will encounter against Garcia.

His previous opponent did much of his damage through combinations and was no longer at his peak. Garcia presents a different threat with a lightning-fast left hook that has produced some of his biggest knockdowns.

Benn’s aggressive style gives Garcia opportunities to land that shot. Charging forward into exchanges worked in earlier bouts, but those attacks can put him directly in range of Garcia’s best weapon.

The September fight will test Benn’s assertion that he performs best when doubted. This isn’t another meeting with an aging veteran. He’s facing a dangerous puncher in his own division with the exact weapon to punish the aggression he relies on.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Faces Oliver Zaren October 8
Sports.content:
The matchup gives Iglesias a challenger who has yet to lose as a professional. Zaren is 19-0 with one draw and seven knockouts and has spent most of his career fighting in Europe.

Iglesias, 15-0 with 14 knockouts, captured the vacant IBF title by stopping Pavel Silyagin in the eighth round in April in Montreal. The Cuban southpaw had already established himself as one of the division’s biggest punchers before winning the belt.

Zaren had been linked to Iglesias several weeks ago after withdrawing from negotiations for a European title fight against Jose Luis Navarro. Those talks never produced a fight, opening the door for his first world title opportunity.

The fight also keeps Iglesias at super middleweight after a possible meeting with WBC middleweight champion Carlos Adames failed to come together earlier this year.

Zaren faces a massive jump in competition. Iglesias has stopped 14 of his 15 professional opponents, including Silyagin, Petro Ivanov and Evgeny Shvedenko.

The Danish challenger has never faced anyone with Iglesias’ combination of power and experience at this level. Zaren will have to prove quickly that his success against European opposition prepared him for a champion who has rarely needed the scorecards.

Sports.title: WBC Blocks Carlos Adames From Denzel Bentley Fight
Sports.content:
That restriction rules out an immediate fight with Denzel Bentley. Adames recently called out the newly elevated WBO middleweight champion for a unification, a fight Bentley wanted as well.

Adames had also explored moving to super middleweight to challenge IBF champion Osleys Iglesias. Talks for that match stalled earlier this year, leaving Bentley as the immediate option at 160 pounds.

The sanctioning body has now taken that choice away.

Ramos has been chasing Adames and can secure the fight by defeating Nursultanov. The 25-year-old interim champion earned his position by beating Shane Mosley Jr. last year.

Nursultanov has plenty to gain beyond disrupting Ramos. Victory in September would send the Kazakh contender directly into a championship fight against Adames.

Adames last defended his WBC belt against Austin Williams in March, winning a unanimous decision. His next challenger will now come from the September 19 fight rather than one of the bigger-name alternatives he wanted.

A Bentley unification would have given Adames the opportunity to add a second middleweight championship belt.

The ruling prevents Adames from taking a voluntary defense while he waits. He must sit tight until Ramos and Nursultanov determine who gets him next.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield vs. Lucas Bahdi Get Another Week to Avoid Purse Bid
Sports.content:
“The purse bid for the vacant WBA Lightweight World Championship bout between Floyd Schofield and Lucas Bahdi, which was scheduled to take place this Tuesday, August 11, has been postponed at the request of both parties, who asked for additional time as they continue working toward an agreement,” the WBA stated Monday.

For Schofield, 23, this is a valuable opening in a lightweight division filled with difficult fights. He can become a world champion without having to go through WBC champion William Zepeda, WBO champion Abdullah Mason, or IBF champion Raymond Muratalla. At this stage of his career, getting a direct title opportunity without first eliminating another top contender is about as favorable a position as Schofield could want.

Bahdi has his own opportunity. The Canadian made his biggest impression by knocking out Ashton Sylve in the fifth round in July 2024. He now has the chance to turn that victory into something considerably bigger.

The fact that both camps requested the extension is encouraging for the fight getting made. They have until August 18 to complete an agreement before the purse-bid process resumes.

Ghana News.title: Police arrest four, intercept 118 bags of cocoa destined for Togo
Ghana News.content:
The North East Regional Police Command has arrested four suspects and intercepted 118 bags of cocoa beans destined for neighbouring Togo through the Bunkpurugu-Togo border.

The seized cocoa, weighing a total of 11,800 kilograms, was intercepted at Bunkpurugu on Sunday, August 9, 2026, following information received by the police about the suspected movement of the consignment towards the border.

According to the police in a social media post on Tuesday, August 11, the suspects have been identified as Dickson Asante, 35, the driver of the truck; Gideon Tab, 19, his mate; Mohammed Mumin, 22; and Ernestina Akugre, 23, who claimed ownership of the consignment.

According to the police, the consignment was being transported in a Hyundai Rhino truck with registration number AS-3272-25 and was loaded with plantain and cocoa.

Acting on the intelligence, a police patrol team intercepted the vehicle at the Bunkpurugu Police Snap Check Point and arrested the four occupants.

A subsequent search conducted at the Customs Office by a joint security team comprising the Ghana Police Service, Ghana Immigration Service, Defence Intelligence, GRA Customs Division and National Security uncovered the concealed cocoa.

The security agencies found that plantain had allegedly been placed in the truck as a decoy to conceal the cocoa beans.

The four suspects remain in police custody and are assisting with investigations.

The police said the suspects would be put before court to face the full rigours of the law as investigations continue into the attempted movement of the cocoa across the border.

The donation forms part of efforts to support grassroots football development and provide young players with the equipment they need to train and compete.

FC Basel, one of Switzerland’s most successful clubs, have a long-standing reputation for developing young talent and investing in football development.

Ghana News.title: Legal vacation is not lawyers’ vacation — Deputy Attorney-General
Ghana News.content:
Justice Srem-Sai, Deputy Attorney-General and Deputy Minister for Justice

The legal vacation should not be interpreted as a period during which lawyers can unilaterally determine whether court proceedings will continue, Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice Dr Justice Srem-Sai has said.

Dr Srem-Sai said the legal vacation, which runs from August 1 to September 30, is designed to significantly reduce the workload of the superior courts but does not mean that the judiciary ceases to function.

He said the period is traditionally a reduction in judicial activity rather than a complete shutdown of the courts.

His comments follow a letter from the Ghana Bar Association to Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie urging him to ensure that judges respect the established traditions governing the legal vacation.

The GBA has particularly objected to lawyers being directed to appear in court after indicating that they would be unavailable during the period.

The association said Vacation Courts were traditionally established to handle urgent and interlocutory matters and did not conduct trials. It further argued that where counsel indicates an inability to appear, the matter should be adjourned rather than proceed without them.

Dr Srem-Sai, however, said the legal vacation is not a “lawyers’ vacation” and that the courts continue to operate during the period.

He explained that the Chief Justice determines which judges sit during the vacation through warrants authorising them to perform judicial duties.

“The key point here, however, is that the courts scale down on work significantly – they do not shut down,” he said.

He said a Vacation Judge could hear both interlocutory and substantive proceedings in cases from the judge’s own court, while cases originating from another judge’s court could be limited to interlocutory matters.

Dr Srem-Sai said the distinction was necessary because only the substantive judge responsible for a case could ultimately determine it.

He maintained that the existing arrangement was designed to ensure continuity in the administration of justice while allowing judges to take their own vacation periods at appropriate times.

Ghana News.title: Lawyers can seek accommodation, but cannot declare court boycott – Deputy Attorney-General
Ghana News.content:
Dr Justice Srem-Sai

Lawyers who are unable to attend court during the legal vacation should seek an accommodation from the judge rather than unilaterally declare that they will not participate in proceedings, Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Justice Srem-Sai, has said.

He said the position was necessary to preserve the authority of judges to manage proceedings and ensure that the interests of all parties before the court were properly considered.

His comments follow concerns raised by the Ghana Bar Association in a letter to Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie on Monday, August 10.

The GBA said lawyers were not under any compulsion to appear before Vacation Courts after notifying the court of their unavailability during the legal vacation.

The association said the vacation period, which runs from August 1 to September 30, was intended to provide judges, lawyers and judicial staff with a period of respite.

It argued that Vacation Courts traditionally dealt with urgent and interlocutory matters and did not conduct trials, particularly where counsel was unavailable.

Dr Srem-Sai disagreed with the suggestion that a lawyer’s unavailability automatically prevents a court from proceeding.

He said judges have the discretion to consider requests from lawyers and determine whether an adjournment or other accommodation is justified.

He said this approach was preferable to allowing lawyers to make unilateral decisions about whether court proceedings should take place.

“Legal vacations, thus, may be a good opportunity for lawyers … to get that well-deserved rest,” he said, adding that judges often accommodate such requests “upon request, on case-by-case basis”.

According to him, a lawyer who wishes to take a break should attend the proceedings and make a plea to the judge, who can then decide whether to grant the request fully, partially or refuse it in the interest of justice.

“The Judge will, in turn, consider the plea and, in the interest of justice, either grant the request (either wholly or in part) or refuse it altogether,” Dr Srem-Sai said.

He cautioned that allowing lawyers to determine in advance that they would not attend court could shift control over the administration of justice away from the judiciary and create significant implications for the management of cases.

Ghana News.title: FirstBank Ghana deepens private education partnership with tailored financial solutions
Ghana News.content:
Enoch Adams, Acting Head, Retail Banking, FirstBank Ghana speaking at the event

FirstBank Ghana has strengthened its partnership with Ghana’s private education sector following an engagement with members of the Ghana National Union of Private Schools (GNUPS) to explore financial solutions to challenges confronting private schools.

The engagement brought together school proprietors and administrators to discuss access to finance, cash-flow management, infrastructure development, student transportation and other operational challenges affecting the sustainability of private educational institutions.

The initiative forms part of FirstBank Ghana’s SME Connect programme, which provides customised financial solutions to businesses operating across key sectors.

Ahead of the engagement, the Bank conducted a public awareness campaign through radio interviews and stakeholder engagements aimed at promoting sound financial management practices within the education sector.

Private schools seek affordable financing

During the engagement, private school proprietors highlighted access to affordable financing as one of the major constraints affecting their ability to expand and improve their operations.

They also raised concerns about cash-flow challenges, infrastructure development and the need to acquire safer and more reliable buses for transporting students.

Speaking on behalf of the Ghana National Union of Private Schools, Eastern Regional Chairman Francis Banzie commended FirstBank Ghana for developing financial products targeted at the specific needs of private schools.

He said access to affordable financing had remained a major challenge, particularly for schools seeking to invest in transportation and infrastructure.

“FirstBank has demonstrated that it understands the realities facing private schools. Access to affordable financing has remained a major challenge, especially for schools seeking to invest in safer buses and improve infrastructure,” he said.

Mr Banzie said the Bank’s FirstEdu product could help schools acquire modern buses and essential facilities without the heavy collateral requirements that had traditionally restricted their growth.

He said the partnership had the potential to improve student safety, strengthen school operations and contribute to the delivery of quality education.

FirstBank unveils integrated school solution

In response to the concerns raised by school proprietors, FirstBank Ghana showcased an integrated three-in-one solution comprising flexible financing through FirstEdu, digital collection and payment platforms, and its Junior Internship Programme (JIP).

Acting Head of Retail Banking at FirstBank Ghana, Enoch Adams, said the Bank was committed to supporting schools with solutions that extended beyond traditional banking services.

“Education remains one of the strongest pillars of national development, and schools deserve financial partners that understand their unique needs,” he said.

Mr Adams explained that FirstEdu provides financing aligned with school fee collection cycles, enabling schools to renovate and expand facilities, acquire school buses, invest in information and communications technology infrastructure, procure teaching and learning resources and finance other development projects without putting undue pressure on their cash flow.

The Bank’s digital collection and payment platforms also enable schools to manage school fee collections, dedicated school accounts, payroll and Point-of-Sale (POS) services, as well as secure digital payment channels.

According to FirstBank Ghana, the digital solutions are designed to improve transparency, reduce cash handling and simplify financial administration for schools.

Focus on students’ career development

Beyond financial services, the Bank introduced its Junior Internship Programme, which provides students with practical workplace experience while developing their financial literacy, leadership skills and career readiness.

The programme is intended to help bridge the gap between classroom learning and the world of work by exposing young people to practical professional environments.

Mr Adams said the combination of financing, digital payment solutions and youth development initiatives would enable schools to operate more efficiently while preparing students for future careers.

FirstBank Ghana said it would continue to work with stakeholders in the private education sector to provide innovative financial and non-financial solutions that support school growth, improve educational delivery and contribute to Ghana’s socio-economic development.

Ghana News.title: Start small and scale up gradually – Republic Bank Mortgage Manager advises Ghanaians
Ghana News.content:
The Manager in charge of Mortgage at Republic Bank, Frank Oppong Yeboah, has advised prospective homeowners to build according to their income and financial capacity rather than taking on large loans to construct expensive houses at once.

Speaking at the launch of the Republic Bank JoyNews Habitat Fair on August 11, Mr Yeboah said incremental housing development offers a more sustainable approach to homeownership, allowing individuals to start small and expand their homes as their incomes increase.

“You don't just go about taking a loan and developing a four-bedroom, two-storey house,” Yeboah said. “You can decide to have one bedroom, living and dining, with all the facilities, and then as you progress, or as your income increases, you add on.”

He explained that a homeowner could start with one bedroom and later add a second, third and fourth bedroom until the desired house is completed.

“The incremental development is to help you build without stress. Build with your income. Build with your resources,” he said.

Mr Yeboah noted that although many people aspire to live in large, luxurious homes, their financial circumstances may not immediately support such ambitions.

“We all would love to be living in Cantonments. We all want to be living in a five-bedroom house. You have one room as your study, and when you are tired of living in your room, you go to another room and rest. You cannot afford it,” he said.

He therefore urged individuals to live within their means and prioritise acquiring a home that meets their immediate needs.

“So you cut your coat according to your size. You get something for yourself and your family, and that's where you begin,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Dr Justice Srem-Sai: Legal vacations and trials — why GBA President is in error
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Justice Srem Sai

The President of the Honourable Ghana Bar Association (GBA) – in a letter to the Chief Justice dated August 10, 2026 – makes two claims. The first claim is that a vacation Judge does not take proceedings on the substance of the case or conduct trials during the legal vacation. More particularly, the President said:

“This notwithstanding, the Judiciary, with the consent of other stakeholders have by convention over the years, agreed to certain courts being designated as Vacation Courts to handle any emergencies arising during the vacation, usually interlocutory matters and never trials.”

The President’s second claim is that the decision, if any, to take proceedings on the substance of the case during the legal vacation lies with the lawyers in the case (and not the bench). More particularly, the President stated as follows:

“However, the overriding consideration in any matter brought before a Vacation Judge has always been the willingness/availability of Counsel to appear before the Court in any matter slated for conduct during the vacation. In other words, Counsel are not under any compulsion whatsoever to appear before a Vacation Court.”

None of the two claims is support by law, rules, practice, or optimal reason. I will explain. However, not before I give a brief background to the conversation:

Nature of Court Proceedings

A court case entails two types of proceedings. They are (1) proceedings on the substantive matter, and (2) proceedings on interlocutory matters. Proceedings on the substantive matter entail proceedings that are capable of finally determining the case. It often includes trials and hearings on the merits of cases.

Interlocutory proceedings, on the other hand, involve motions and summons which do not determine the matter finally. Kindly note this down.

The tradition of law practice (as well as the dictate of the civil procedure rules) is that the superior courts scale down significantly on work in the months of August and September. This is known as the “summer vacations” or “the long legal vacation”. In some jurisdictions, it is informally called “Judges’ vacation”. It is never called “lawyers’ vacation” anywhere in the world.

The key point here, however, is that the courts scale down on work significantly – they do not shut down. To continue operating partially, some judges – a few of them – are allowed to work over the vacation period. The person who determines which judge works over the vacation is the administrative head of the courts – in this case, the honourable Chief Justice and, of course, together with the inherent judicial power of a judge to manage and control his court’s work. One thing is, however, clear - a lawyer or a body of them do not determine that. Kindly note this, too, down.

The Chief Justice allows a Judge to work in the vacation by issuing what we call a “warrant” to the Judge. The Chief Justice’s warrant to a Judge to sit during the legal vacation allows the judge – known as a ‘vacation Judge’ – to hear two kinds of cases. The kinds of cases are (1) cases in his own court, and (2) cases in the courts of other judges who are on vacation. Note this, too, down.

In respect of cases in his own court, a vacation Judge is allowed to take both interlocutory proceedings and substantive proceedings. In respect of cases from other courts, however, a vacation Judge is allowed to take interlocutory proceedings only. This is based on the law and the understanding that it is only a substantive Judge (not a holding Judge) who could determines a case finally.

Now, I turn back to the GBA President’s claims of allegation on court proceedings during the legal vacation.

The Power over Court Proceedings

Contrary to the GBA President’s claim, the power to decide whether to take proceedings on the substance of a case during a legal vacation is for the bench, not for the bar. This is why:

A lawyer’s primary duty is, in fact, to his client – not to the client of another lawyer. If allowed to determine how justice is administered in the courts, a lawyers will decisively make decisions which will promote his client’s interest over the interest of another lawyer’s client. In fact, this is the only reason courts and judges exist – to balance the interests of litigants.

It is, therefore, fundamentally disturbing to suggest, as the GBA President has suggested, that “the overriding consideration in any matter brought before a Vacation Judge has always been the willingness/availability of Counsel to appear before the Court in any matter slated for conduct during the vacation.”

Let us, for a minute, turn to England, where the practice of legal vacation originates. There, it is emphatically the decision of the bench to determine how to run the courts, both in term-time and during vacations.

The Civil Procedure Rules Practice Direction 2F regulates the English High Court’s vacation work. There, one will notice that the Practice Direction is filled with phrases like “if the senior judge of that Division determines …”, “if the Court is satisfied …”, “as the Court may direct”, “Subject to the discretion of the Judge”, etc.

This has always been the case in Ghana, too. As we have known it, it is the Chief Justice who determines when and where a Court should work. She may, as we have come to know it, upon a warrant, determine and direct that a Judge sits even on weekends. We are also aware that Courts have customarily conducted trials over legal vacation.

Nowhere, either in England or in Ghana, is a lawyer or a body of them given the power to determine how court proceedings should go. Thus, one is not particularly certain where the GBA President gets the alleged tradition of this version of legal vacation practice from.

Trials During the Vacations

Contrary to the GBA President’s claim, vacation Judges take proceedings on the substance of the case and do conduct trials during the legal vacation. Here is why:

As stated above, a vacation Judge takes both interlocutory and substantive proceedings on cases in his own court. The reason for this is that a vacation Judge is entitled to and does, eventually, take his share of the vacation but in term-time. When he does, another Judge – a term Judge – takes his (the legal vacation Judge’s) cases.

As in the case of vacation, a term Judge too will – when the vacation Judge goes on leave – take only interlocutory proceedings on cases from the court of the Judge who is now on vacation. Under such circumstances, too, substantive proceedings on cases from the vacation Judge will be on hold until the vacation Judge returns from leave. This is for the same reason and law that only a substantive Judge (not a holding Judge) could determine a case finally.

The net effect of this arrangement is that cases in the vacation Judge’s courts do not suffer disproportionate delays simply because he has served as a vacation Judge.

This has been the practice in our court. So, again, one is not particularly clear what the GBA President grounds the allegation that courts “never” conduct trials during legal vacations on.

Conclusion

Law practice is a difficult job. It drains you, both physically, mentally and emotionally. Many lawyers end up developing serious physical, behavioural and mental illnesses from law practice. Some manage life, sadly, with indulgences and addictions. Legal vacations, thus, may be a good opportunity for lawyers – who are either unwilling or, for any reason, unable to take control of their lives – to get that well-deserved rest.

It is for this reason that many Judges, accommodate the pleas of lawyers to scale down work during judges’ vacation. This accommodation is, however, always upon request, on case-by-case basis, and is subject to the consideration of the Judge who, for the time being is, conducting a case.

What the GBA President’s proposition in her letter to the honourable Chief Justice seeks to do is grave. It seeks to move the power to manage and control court proceedings and to do justice from the hands of the Judge into the hands of a lawyer. This has a severe and far-reaching policy implication for justice administration in Ghana.

On the face of it alone, it distorts the very reason courts exist. If one adds to it the fact that the claim is also not backed by law, rules, practice or optimal reason, then the matter gets even more unhealthy.

Now, a lawyer who wishes to take a rest during legal vacation knows exactly what to do. He attends proceedings and makes a plea to the Judge for accommodation.

The Judge will, in turn, consider the plea and, in the interest of justice, either grant the request (either wholly or in part) or refuse it altogether. What a professional lawyer is not entitled to do, and cannot do is to, in vacuo, beforehand, declare that he will not attend proceedings at all.

Ghana News.title: NACSA educates students on firearm safety and gun violence prevention
Ghana News.content:
The National Commission on Small Arms and Light Weapons (NACSA) has intensified efforts to educate young people on firearm safety and gun violence prevention through school-based public education programmes.

The Commission recently engaged students of Nungua Senior High School in the Greater Accra Region and Ghana Senior High School (GHANASS) in the Eastern Region, where participants received practical education on firearm safety, preventing gun violence and responsible citizenship.

According to the Commission in a social media post on Monday, August 10, the sessions sought to help students understand how peer influence, exposure to firearms and unresolved conflicts could contribute to unsafe situations in schools and communities.

Students were encouraged to make responsible choices, avoid violent behaviour and seek appropriate assistance when confronted with suspicious activities, firearms-related incidents or potential threats.

NACSA said young people had an important role to play in efforts to prevent gun violence and promote safer communities.

The Commission noted that equipping students with the knowledge to identify risks and respond appropriately could help reduce exposure to firearm-related dangers in schools and communities.

Through the school-based engagements, NACSA is positioning young people as active partners in promoting peace, responsible citizenship and safer school environments.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
