FrontPage Africa/New Narratives has documented suspected corruption and lack of capacity under the Weah administration that led to four-year delays in the US$10 million Climate Information System project which would warn communities about hazardous weather, and the US$27 million Monrovia Metropolitan Climate Resilience Project which is intended to protect West Point’s coastline from sea-level rise– just two of the many projects that had been approved.

Hundreds of thousands of Liberians were left without rainfall and temperature warnings over four years that may have saved them from crop failure and flooding. On the coast many homes were swept away that would have been saved had the project proceeded as expected.

But there was some progress documented in the report. Between 2021 and 2024, Liberia reported 105 megawatts of hydropower capacity and 5.6 megawatts of solar-energy production. It also recorded 175 electric vehicles contributing to the NDC’s goal of cutting transport emissions Nearly 46,000 hectares of forest were restored through natural regeneration on pace to meet its goal of reforesting an average of 12,285 hectares annually through 2030.

A Plan Liberia Cannot Fund Alone

The gap between ambition and capacity runs through nearly every part of NDC 3.0. Implementing the plan will cost as much as US$3 billion by 2035, according to experts. Of the 64 percent emissions reduction Liberia has pledged, only 10 percent are classified as “unconditional,” meaning they can be achieved using the country’s own resources.

Farmer Rickson Johnson sits on a log on his farm in Nimba County and prays for rain to come down in 2024. Photo credit: Jerome Saye

In an interview Benjamin S. Karmorh, the EPA’s chief technical adviser and Liberia’s national focal point to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change,

said the EPA had not completed its assessment to determine the full cost of its commitments, but he warned it would be big.

“For the next nine to 12 months, we will be able to come up with the real cost of our NDC,” he said, adding that implementing the second NDC alone required more than US$400 million.

Karmorh said the Boakai administration had moved quickly to catch up ground lost under the Weah administration where government failure to provide co-financing and meet the project deadlines required of donors blocked the release of global funds. He cited a 20-megawatt solar facility at the Mount Coffee Hydropower Plant, recently inaugurated to complement the plant’s 88-megawatt hydropower capacity.

He cited President Joseph Boakai’s visit to the Environmental Protection Agency to inaugurate its new headquarters and laboratory as evidence of “the strongest political will on the part of the government in ensuring that the EPA fulfills its mandate.”

A resident affected by flooding makes her way home through standing water on 13th Street, Sinkor, Monrovia, in July.

The 2026 national budget allocated US$2.9 million to the EPA. It includes US$900,000 that the government is required to provide as co-financing for two initiatives backed by the Green Climate Fund. Louis Kuukpen, Deputy Liberia Representative for the United Nations Development Program, which is implementing the coastal defense project, confirmed to FrontPage Africa/New Narratives that the government had disbursed $800,000 co-financing required for the coastal defense project and progress should be seen soon.

Karmorh said the real evidence of the government’s commitment will come in next year’s budget. “We expect that there will be an increase for the EPA,” Karmorh said. “And with that increment, we expect that we’ll be able to do a lot.”

Lack of Data Collection Capacity Also a Handbrake on Global Funding

If money is the headline problem, data is the quieter crisis—and Yarkpawolo devoted much of his address to it.

“We cannot properly manage what we do not measure,” he told the meeting. “We cannot convincingly report progress without credible and consistent data.”

Without reliable data, he said, Liberia cannot determine where resources are most needed, meet its transparency obligations to the United Nations or make a credible case to international climate funders demanding proof of results.

Ongoing solar facility in Voinjama, Lofa County, supporting Liberia’s clean energy and climate goals. Photo credit: RREA

Yarkpawolo said the sectoral officers responsible for gathering data across ministries—from transport and agriculture to energy—are being asked to work without adequate funding, transportation, equipment or reliable internet access.

“This is not sustainable,” he said.

He appealed directly to Liberia’s international donors to establish a dedicated fund for data collection and reporting, separate from project financing. He said such a fund would support field travel, data systems, training and verification—the less visible infrastructure that makes accountability possible and would allow them to employ Liberians to meet the requirements that would unlock funding.“Our partners should not only finance climate projects,” Yarkpawolo said. “They should also invest in institutions and people responsible for measuring and reporting their results.”

A fleet of electric vehicle that are contributing to the Country’s goal of reducing emission by 64 percent. Photo supplied by Spencer Taylor of the Ministry of Transport.

Mobilizing Government Ministries to Meet Climate Targets

Yarkpawolo outlined the EPA’s priorities for the year: finalize a 2026–2027 work plan, validate new coordination tools and reporting templates, and clearly identify which ministry is responsible for providing particular data and when. He said climate reporting is broader than the responsibility of the EPA alone.

“It is not solely an environmental issue,” Yarkpawolo said. “It is a development, economic, social, health, security, and government issue.” Addressing it, he said, will require “a whole-of-government and a whole-of-society approach.”

World.title: Liberia: Auditor General Cites Missing Audit Committee, Non-Competitive Procurement, Unverified Assets, Delayed Projects and Undelivered Digital Lending Platform
World.content:
Monrovia – Liberia’s General Auditing Commission (GAC) has uncovered a series of governance, procurement and project implementation weaknesses in the Smallholder Agriculture Transformation and Agribusiness Revitalization Project (STAR-P), warning that the deficiencies exposed the World Bank and IFAD-supported initiative to weak oversight, poor asset accountability and potential value-for-money risks.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh, [email protected]

The findings are contained in a Management Letter issued on June 29, 2026, following the audit of STAR-P’s financial statements covering the period ending October 31, 2025.

The audit, addressed to Agriculture Minister J. Alexander Nuetah, identified weaknesses ranging from the absence of a functional audit committee to procurement irregularities, poor asset management, incomplete infrastructure projects and delays in implementing key digital services intended to benefit farmers.

No Functional Audit Committee

The GAC found that the National Project Steering Committee failed to establish an audit committee as required under Liberia’s Public Financial Management (PFM) Act.

Auditors also reported no evidence that the Steering Committee reviewed internal audit reports or monitored the implementation of audit recommendations. According to the report, the committee met only once during the audit period to approve the project’s annual budget and work plan.

The GAC warned that the absence of an audit committee weakens internal oversight and could delay corrective actions on audit findings.

In response, STAR-P management acknowledged the recommendation but said the Ministry of Agriculture has instead established an Audit Recommendation Implementation Committee chaired by the Minister to monitor audit recommendations. The Auditor General, however, maintained that a formal audit committee remains necessary and said implementation would be reviewed during future audits.

Procurement Without Competition

The audit also questioned the procurement process surrounding a US$27,000 consultancy contract awarded to OA & A Consult Limited.

Auditors found no evidence that the consultancy was competitively procured, noting the absence of s, expressions of interest, technical evaluations or financial proposal assessments as required under project procurement rules and World Bank regulations.

The GAC cautioned that bypassing competitive procurement could undermine value for money and increase the risk of procurement fraud.

Management accepted the finding and pledged to ensure future grantees follow competitive procurement procedures consistent with IFAD and World Bank guidelines.

Weak Fixed Asset Controls

The report identified widespread weaknesses in STAR-P’s asset management system.

Among the deficiencies were incomplete fixed asset registers, failure to update newly acquired assets, lack of periodic physical verification, and absence of asset coding.

The audit cited assets valued at US$46,719, including laptops, printers, projectors, office furniture and computers, that were either improperly recorded or omitted from the register.

Although management submitted an updated asset register after the audit, the Auditor General said it still lacked critical information required under public financial management regulations.

Missing and Unverified Beneficiary Assets

Field verification exercises also uncovered concerns regarding assets purchased for beneficiaries under the Liberia Agriculture Commercialization Fund (LACF).

The audit reported that assets worth US$33,500, including cold storage facilities, solar systems, greenhouses and motorcycles, could not be physically verified.

Another US$1,680 solar system procured for a beneficiary had not been put into use, while assets worth US$68,000 supplied to a beneficiary in Grand Bassa County—including trucks, motor tricycles, processing equipment and palm oil machinery—had not been coded for identification.

The GAC concluded that management failed to adequately account for the missing assets or explain why some equipment remained unused.

Management attributed the challenges to decentralized project implementation, incomplete records and logistical difficulties, and said it has begun reconciling assets, strengthening asset tracking and revising its fixed asset management policies.

The Auditor General maintained the findings and called for a joint physical verification exercise with the GAC within one month after submission of the report to the Legislature.

Construction Projects Behind Schedule

The audit further found that US$57,960 had been paid for construction projects that remained incomplete well beyond approved timelines.

The affected projects include a warehouse in Lofa County and a palm oil factory in Grand Bassa County, both of which were still unfinished during GAC’s field verification in May 2026.

Management blamed contractor capacity limitations, adverse weather, rising construction costs and logistical challenges, and said stronger contract monitoring and milestone-based payment systems have since been introduced.

Digital Lending Platform Still Missing

One of the audit’s most significant findings involved an online digital lending platform intended to support farmers through CitiTrust Savings and Loans.

According to the report, US$36,768—representing full payment under the service agreement—was disbursed for the design and implementation of the platform.

However, during physical verification in May 2026, auditors found no evidence that the integrated digital lending system had been deployed or was operational, despite contractual deadlines indicating it should have gone live by May 2025.

Management acknowledged implementation delays, citing software customization requirements, connectivity problems and technical capacity constraints. Officials said the software would be fully integrated before the service agreement expires.

Dashboard and Project Assets Not Handed Over

The GAC also found that the Liberia Agriculture Commercialization Fund’s reporting dashboard and other digital assets were never formally transferred to the Ministry following the expiration of the Fund Manager’s contract.

Auditors warned that the missing dashboard could undermine institutional memory, beneficiary tracking and project reporting.

Management said discussions are underway with the former Fund Manager to complete the handover of databases, user credentials and reporting tools, while committing to strengthen future contractual handover requirements.

Auditor General Maintains Key Findings

While STAR-P management accepted most of the recommendations and outlined corrective measures, the Auditor General maintained several key findings, particularly regarding missing beneficiary assets and incomplete documentation.

The GAC said it will conduct follow-up reviews during subsequent audits to determine whether the Ministry of Agriculture has implemented the recommended reforms aimed at strengthening governance, procurement, financial accountability and project oversight.

World.title: Liberia: Boakai Replaces Biago, Taps Ex-Defense Chief Ziankahn to Lead LDEA Amid Cocaine Probe
World.content:
MONROVIA — President Joseph Nyuma Boakai has appointed retired Major General Daniel Dee Ziankahn Jr. as Director General of the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA), replacing Deputy Police Commissioner Fitzgerald T. M. Biago, who had been serving as the agency’s officer in charge amid a widening cocaine investigation.

By Jaheim T. Toby

The appointment, announced Monday by the Executive Mansion, is subject to confirmation by the Liberian Senate.

Ziankahn, a former Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of Liberia and former Minister of National Defense, most recently served as President Boakai’s Military Advisor. His appointment comes as the government faces mounting pressure over Liberia’s handling of major narcotics seizures, including the interception of nearly four tons of cocaine in Paynesville valued at about US$317 million.

The Executive Mansion said the appointment reflects Boakai’s determination to strengthen Liberia’s response to drug trafficking and transnational organized crime.

“His appointment reflects the President’s confidence in his leadership, integrity, and operational experience, and signals the Administration’s determination to elevate Liberia’s fight against drugs to a new level,” the statement said.

Under the new arrangement, Ziankahn will report directly to the President in consultation with the Minister of Justice.

Boakai also appointed Precious Rue as Deputy Director General for Operations and Prince Mulbah as Deputy Director General for Administration. Both appointments are also subject to Senate confirmation.

The three appointees have been directed to assume their responsibilities immediately in an acting capacity pending legislative confirmation when the Senate returns later this year.

Ernest Tarpeh, who previously served as Deputy Director General of the LDEA, will return to his former assignment at the National Security Agency.

Biago Suspended Amid Ethical Concerns

The leadership change follows the decision by Biago to step aside earlier this week and submit himself to investigation after allegations emerged that he had received a vehicle as a gift from Leroy Harris, a suspect in the US$317 million cocaine case.

Biago has denied the allegation and said he voluntarily stepped aside to allow the investigation to proceed.

According to the Executive Mansion, President Boakai has now indefinitely suspended Biago from the Liberia National Police over what it described as “ethical transgressions” and ordered a more detailed investigation.

The President’s decision followed a review of the Ministry of Justice investigative report.

The report, according to the Executive Mansion, did not establish Biago’s involvement in illegal narcotics trafficking, but raised ethical concerns requiring further scrutiny to determine whether additional administrative or other appropriate action should be taken.

The development comes against the backdrop of a series of high-profile cocaine seizures that have placed Liberia’s law enforcement and security institutions under intense scrutiny.

The government has maintained that the fight against narcotics trafficking is a national security priority, with President Boakai repeatedly describing drug trafficking as one of the gravest threats to Liberia’s security, public health and future development.

‘No Safe Haven’

Following a marathon meeting of the National Security Council on Monday evening, Boakai reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to investigating allegations of misconduct while respecting due process.

The President said allegations should not be treated as proof of wrongdoing, but stressed that public officials must remain accountable when questions about their conduct arise.

“No individual will be condemned without evidence, but no public official will be exempt from accountability where questions of integrity arise,” the Executive Mansion quoted the President as saying.

Boakai directed the new LDEA leadership to work with the Joint Security, the Ministry of Justice and international partners to dismantle drug trafficking networks, strengthen border security and improve intelligence and enforcement capabilities.

He also called for stronger measures to protect Liberian communities, particularly young people, from the impact of illicit drugs.

“Our fight against drugs is a fight for the future of Liberia,” Boakai said.

“We will continue to strengthen our institutions, hold public officials to the highest ethical standards, and pursue those who seek to poison our communities. There will be no safe haven for drug traffickers or those who aid and abet them.”

The appointments mark the latest major shake-up of Liberia’s anti-narcotics apparatus as authorities continue investigations into the country’s increasingly high-profile cocaine cases.

World.title: Liberia: EU-Funded Seeds4Liberia Project Hands Over Agricultural Inputs to Boost Local Certified Seed Production
World.content:
Speaking at the event , the project’s National Coordinator /AfricaRice Country Representative to Liberia Moustapha Gaye described the event as more than the distribution of agricultural inputs, saying it reflects the strong partnership between the Government of Liberia, the European Union and the consortium of AfricaRice, the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) and WorldFish

MONROVIA –The European Union-funded Seeds4Liberia Project and partners recently handed over improved seeds, seedlings, fish fingerlings and agricultural machinery to local seed enterprises.

Items handed over included power tillers, lowland and upland rice seeders, rice reapers, hermetic cocoons with ECOWAS monitoring systems, hermetic bags, catfish fry, tilapia fry, mixer machines for fish feed production, a feed pellet mill, hapa net, sechi disks, a scale, foundation seeds, and cuttings.

The hand over ceremongy took place last week at the Central Agricultural Research Institute (CARI), with stakeholders calling on farmers to use the inputs responsibly to strengthen Liberia’s food security and agricultural productivity.

Speaking at the event , the project’s National Coordinator /AfricaRice Country Representative to Liberia Moustapha Gaye described the event as more than the distribution of agricultural inputs, saying it reflects the strong partnership between the Government of Liberia, the European Union and the consortium of AfricaRice, the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) and WorldFish.

“Today’s event represents much more than the distribution of agricultural inputs,” Gaye said. “It reflects the strong partnership between the Government of Liberia, the European Union and the consortium of AfricaRice, IITA and WorldFish, working together to strengthen Liberia’s agricultural sector and improve the livelihoods of farmers across the country.”

He thanked the European Union for financing the Seeds4Liberia Project, saying the investment is helping strengthen Liberia’s seed systems, improve farmers’ access to quality planting materials, promote sustainable agricultural technologies and create opportunities for increased productivity and food security.

Gaye also acknowledged national partners including, the Ministry of Agriculture, CARI, the Seed Development and Certification Agency (SDCA), the Liberia Agricultural Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA), the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority (NAFAA), county authorities and other development partners, for supporting the project’s implementation

Gaye also acknowledged national partners including, the Ministry of Agriculture, CARI, the Seed Development and Certification Agency (SDCA), the Liberia Agricultural Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA), the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority (NAFAA), county authorities and other development partners, for supporting the project’s implementation.

He urged beneficiaries to maximize the use of the agricultural inputs distributed under the project.

“The seeds, seedlings, and equipment being handed over today are not an end in themselves. They are tools that will enable farmers, seed enterprises and producer organizations to increase production, improve quality, create businesses and generate income,” Gaye said.

He emphasized that the project’s long-term success will depend on continued collaboration among research institutions, government agencies, the private sector, extension services and farmers to ensure that improved technologies remain sustainable beyond the life of the project.

Also speaking, the European Union Programme Officer for Agriculture Antonio Di Clemente said the Seeds4Liberia Project is intended to build resilient seed systems for rice, cassava, soybean, coffee and fish value chains to strengthen food security and promote economic diversification.

According to Di Clemente, the project seeks to strengthen institutional capacity to produce and regulate high-quality breeder seeds, seedlings and fish while empowering private-sector and community-based enterprises to produce, store and market certified seeds and quality fish fingerlings

He said the initiative has also operationalized the Seed Development and Certification Agency to improve national quality assurance systems, promote high-yielding and climate-resilient crop varieties, provide practical training for farmers and students, and strengthen market linkages through partnerships between seed producers, buyers and financial institutions.

Additionally, the Assistant Minister for Planning and Development at the Ministry of Agriculture, Francis Mulbah, described the ceremony as another demonstration of the Liberian government’s commitment to revitalizing the country’s agricultural sector.

Mulbah reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to working with development partners to improve agricultural production through the distribution of quality seeds and planting materials.

The EU-funded Seeds4Liberia Project is jointly implemented by Africa Rice Center (AfricaRice), the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA), and WorldFish in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA), the Central Agricultural Research Institute (CARI), the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority (NaFAA), the Seed Development and Certification Agency (SDCA), and the Liberia Agricultural Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA)

Also speaking, Farmers Union of Liberia Director Josephine Francis urged farmers’ cooperatives and federations to take ownership of agricultural projects to ensure their long-term sustainability.

“I always tell our farmers and their families to take ownership,” Francis said. “When you take ownership of projects that come to your cooperatives and federations, that is what makes them successful.”

She encouraged farmers to use the improved planting materials responsibly and highlighted the growing economic potential of soybean production, noting that Liberia has an existing market that imports thousands of tons annually.

Francis also praised the introduction of seven improved cassava varieties under the project and urged farmers to learn the characteristics of each variety to maximize yields.

Project organizers commended CARI, under the leadership of Director General Dr. Arthur Bob Karnuah, for hosting the ceremony and serving as a key technical partner in strengthening Liberia’s national seed systems and promoting improved agricultural technologies.

They also recognized the contributions of SDCA, LACRA, NAFAA, IITA, WorldFish and other implementing partners for supporting the initiative.

Beneficiaries, in turn, thanked the Ministry of Agriculture, the European Union and project partners for providing the agricultural inputs and equipment, pledging to use them to improve production and strengthen their livelihoods.

The EU-funded Seeds4Liberia Project is jointly implemented by Africa Rice Center (AfricaRice), the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA), and WorldFish in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA), the Central Agricultural Research Institute (CARI), the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority (NaFAA), the Seed Development and Certification Agency (SDCA), and the Liberia Agricultural Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA).

The initiative aims to strengthen food production, improve rural livelihoods and reduce Liberia’s dependence on imported agricultural commodities through improved seed systems, climate-resilient technologies and stronger public-private partnerships.

World.title: Liberia: Rep. Fahnbulleh Reaffirms Support for China Union Workers in Bong Mines Engagement
World.content:
The lawmaker said his engagement with the workers and residents was also aimed at strengthening cooperation between his office and the people of the district. He maintained that meaningful representation goes beyond legislative duties and requires regular consultation with constituents, particularly workers and communities whose livelihoods are directly connected to economic activities taking place within the district

BONG MINES, Bong County — Representative Foday Fahnbulleh of District Seven in Bong County has reaffirmed his commitment to protecting the interests of residents and Liberian workers in his district, following an engagement Saturday with members of a local cooperative and workers of the China Union Concession Company in Bong Mines, Fuamah District.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

Rep. Fahnbulleh, who represents Fuamah and Sanoyea Districts, the two administrative districts that constitute electoral District Seven, held the engagement as part of his continued interaction with constituents to hear directly from them about the challenges confronting them and to discuss possible ways of addressing issues affecting their livelihoods and welfare.

During the meeting, Rep. Fahnbulleh said the engagement was intended to provide an opportunity for residents and workers to speak openly about their concerns while giving him a better understanding of the challenges they face. He said as an elected representative, he considers it his responsibility to remain accessible to the people and to ensure that their concerns are not ignored after they have brought them to his attention.

“As your representative, my responsibility is to listen to you, understand the challenges you are facing and stand with you as we work toward finding fair and lasting solutions. I want you to know that you have my fullest support, particularly when it comes to protecting your rights and interests,” Rep. Fahnbulleh told the gathering.

The lawmaker said his engagement with the workers and residents was also aimed at strengthening cooperation between his office and the people of the district. He maintained that meaningful representation goes beyond legislative duties and requires regular consultation with constituents, particularly workers and communities whose livelihoods are directly connected to economic activities taking place within the district.

Rep. Fahnbulleh said he would continue to engage relevant stakeholders whenever issues affecting workers and residents arise, stressing that accountability and fairness must remain central to efforts to address concerns in the community. He said he would work alongside the people to seek practical solutions rather than simply listen to their complaints without follow-up.

“We cannot claim to represent our people effectively if we are not prepared to stand with them when they raise legitimate concerns. I am committed to engaging the appropriate stakeholders, advocating for fairness and ensuring that the voices of our people are heard,” he said.

The Bong County lawmaker further assured the workers that his support for them would not be limited to a single meeting, emphasizing that he intends to maintain an open channel of communication with workers and residents.

According to him, sustained engagement is necessary to identify problems early, encourage accountability and prevent issues affecting workers and communities from being left unresolved.

He said the people of Fuamah and Sanoyea deserve representation that is responsive to their concerns and focused on advancing their collective interests. Rep. Fahnbulleh also encouraged residents and workers to continue communicating their challenges to his office, noting that constructive engagement provides an avenue for issues to be addressed through dialogue and appropriate institutional channels.

“My commitment is to work with you, not above you. I want our people to feel that their representative is available to them, that their concerns matter and that there is someone willing to carry their issues to the appropriate level whenever necessary,” Rep. Fahnbulleh said.

The lawmaker also called for unity among residents and workers, stressing that the collective interests of the district should remain at the center of discussions involving employment, workers’ welfare, community development and other issues affecting the people. He said disagreements and challenges should be addressed through constructive dialogue and a shared commitment to finding solutions that are fair to all sides.

“Our collective interest must guide us. Where there are challenges, we should sit together, identify the issues, demand accountability where necessary and work toward solutions that protect the dignity and interests of our people,” Rep. Fahnbulleh added.

The engagement was welcomed by Liberian workers who described the lawmaker’s willingness to meet with them and listen to their concerns as an important part of effective representation. The workers said Rep. Fahnbulleh’s presence demonstrated a willingness to maintain direct contact with constituents and to understand the realities they face in their workplaces and communities.

One of the workers said Rep. Fahnbulleh’s engagement was encouraging because it gave them an opportunity to communicate their concerns directly to their elected representative rather than relying solely on intermediaries.

“We appreciate Representative Fahnbulleh for coming to meet with us and giving us the opportunity to speak about the issues that concern us. It is important for workers to know that their representative is willing to listen,” the worker said.

Another worker praised Rep. Fahnbulleh for what the worker described as his continued willingness to stand with Liberian workers and residents of the district. The worker said the engagement demonstrated that the lawmaker was interested in understanding the challenges facing ordinary people and advocating for their interests.

“We are encouraged by the fact that our lawmaker is engaging us directly. We want him to continue standing with the workers and carrying our concerns to the appropriate authorities whenever necessary,” the worker said.

A third worker said the meeting had strengthened their confidence that their concerns could receive attention through sustained engagement and advocacy. The worker stressed that workers need representatives who are prepared to listen and follow up on issues affecting their welfare.

“What we need is someone who will listen to us and help ensure that our concerns are properly addressed. We thank Representative Fahnbulleh for coming to us, listening to us and reassuring us of his support,” he said.

World.title: International Rights Groups Raise Alarm Over Freedom of Religion and Expression in South Korea
World.content:
SEOUL, South Korea — Human Rights Without Frontiers (HRWF), together with CAP Liberté de Conscience (CAP LC), which has accredited ECOSOC status at the United Nations, FOREF, CESNUR and Bitter Winter, held a press conference today at the Seoul Foreign Correspondents’ Club on Freedom of Religion or Belief and Freedom of Expression in South Korea.

The issues addressed included concerns about the treatment of elderly religious leaders in pretrial detention, including questions of proportionality, humanitarian considerations, and due process.

The organizations called on South Korean authorities to review the detention of 95-year-old Shincheonji Chairman Lee Man-hee and to ensure that the legal and administrative response to religious minorities remains neutral, proportionate, and consistent with South Korea’s international human-rights obligations, including with respect to 83-year-old Mrs. Hak-ja Han Moon of the Family Federation.

The issues discussed form part of a broader pattern of Freedom of Religion or Belief concerns in South Korea. Concerns have also persisted regarding Segero Church in Busan, which has reportedly continued to face harassment and official scrutiny even after Pastor Son Hyun-bo was released from detention.

Reporting has also raised questions about conscientious objection, public hostility toward a mosque project in Daegu, and religious accommodation in educational settings.

Over the past decades, HRWF has documented the imprisonment of hundreds of Jehovah’s Witnesses in South Korea as conscientious objectors, and although alternative civilian service was later introduced, critics maintain that it has been implemented in a punitive manner rather than as a genuine rights-respecting alternative, notably because it requires 36 months of service in correctional facilities, twice the length of regular military service. Recent court decisions have also upheld key features of that system against constitutional challenge.

Opening the conference, Hans Noot, Associate Director of HRWF, said the issues at stake “lie at the heart of democratic society,” warning that when religious communities are stigmatized, peaceful gatherings are restricted, and dissent is treated as a problem to be contained, the consequences “extend far beyond any single group or case.”

He said the conference was not about defending any one theology or movement, but about “defending a principle: that fundamental rights apply equally to all.”

Thierry Valle, President of CAP Liberté de Conscience, addressed the legality of Chairman Lee’s detention under international law. Referring to South Korea’s ratification of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights in 1990 and the Convention against Torture in 1995, he questioned whether placing a 95-year-old in pretrial detention is consistent with those obligations. He stressed that the presumption of innocence must prevail over any presumption of guilt.

There are alternative more proportionate and more humane measures respecting the presumption of innocence and human dignity in democratic countries. And he cited precedents including Cardinal Joseph Zen’s 2022 release on bail in Hong Kong and Vietnam’s decision to place Buddhist Patriarch Thich Quang Do under house arrest rather than in prison.

Michael Langhans, Executive Director of FOREF Germany, presented a legal analysis questioning whether pretrial detention for Chairman Lee of the Shincheonji Church was necessary given evidence already sufficient for an indictment, and whether that evidence was gathered neutrally rather than through a narrative framing the defendant’s community as a “sect” or “cult.” He argued that the case raises a broader question for lawmakers: whether measures meant to protect fair elections can be applied without nullifying the constitutionally and internationally guaranteed right to freedom of religion.

Márk Nemes, Deputy Director of CESNUR, shared his thoughts on the effects of ongoing persecution and its possible ramifications for minority faiths.

He noted three recent scholarly investigations conducted in selected Shincheonji congregations in Europe, Argentina, and Australia, each finding worrisome increase in hostility toward the otherwise peaceful and cooperative religious movement. He stressed that Shincheonji is not simply a South Korean minority church but a global religious movement with congregations worldwide.

The disproportionate persecution in South Korea affects the lives of those congregants abroad, whose freedoms for expressing and practicing faith, enshrined in ICCPR Articles 18 and 19, are inalienable rights and must be considered during this current process.

Massimo Introvigne, Managing Director of CESNUR and Editor-in-Chief of Bitter Winter, said South Korea “has crossed a worrying line” by arresting Chairman Lee, arguing that international standards such as the Mandela Rules would call for house arrest rather than imprisonment for a 95-year-old accused of a non-violent offence.

He said the charges, tied to ordinary political participation by members of a religious minority, “appear legally and conceptually overstretched,” and warned that the case fits a broader pattern of pressure against minority faiths in the country.

The organizations called on South Korean authorities, the media, and the international community to examine these developments with close attention to due process, proportionality, and the equal protection of fundamental rights, and made further documentation available to support continued reporting.

At the conclusion of the press conference, the scholars in attendance signed an official letter calling on the Government of the Republic of Korea to immediately release Chairman Lee from custody.

World.title: Nakonde election preps advance
World.content:
Electoral stakeholders in Nakonde district in Muchinga Province have commended the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) for promoting transparency and ensuring peace during the preparations for Thursday’s general elections.

Nakonde Forum for Persons with Disabilities Chairperson, Martin Gondwe, thanked ECZ for exhibiting transparency and hoped this would be maintained throughout the electoral process.

Speaking in an interview with the Zambia News and Information Services (ZANIS), Mr Gondwe called on all political parties to preach peace in communities ahead of the polls.

Mr Gondwe further appealed for inclusion of persons with disabilities in the voting process and asked if braille tactile jackets will also be available during the verification exercise.

“Make sure you preach peace wherever you are going, in our camps. Persons with disabilities and women inclusive, we want to participate in a violence-free election this year,” he said.

And United Party for National Development (UPND) Chairperson for Nakonde District, Derick Banda, said the process had been peaceful.

He expressed optimism that the same peaceful mood will prevail as poll staff are deployed and dispatched to polling stations tomorrow.

He also expressed gratitude to other stakeholders who have been available from inception, to ensure transparency.

“So far so good, the process has been peaceful for us. The most important thing we always preach is peace. Even from the time we received the ballot papers it has been peaceful,” he said.

And National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) Mwenzo Constituency Chairperson, Frederick Siame, called for continued transparency during the dispatch of poll staff and verification of election material.

Mr Siame also expressed satisfaction with how the election preparations have been conducted in the district.

“So far so good. As we do the verification exercise when dispatching poll staff, we need to verify what the contents are. What we are asking for is the same transparency that has prevailed to continue,” Mr Siame said.

World.title: ZAF, NAPSA, LWSC seal deal
World.content:
Ministry of Defense Permanent Secretary Maambo Hamaundu has described the signing of a contract for the design and construction of a bulk water pipeline system for several housing developments in Lusaka as a significant step towards improving access to reliable water supply.

The pipeline will serve Kingsland Housing Estate, Zambia Air Force Twin Palm Base, Datong and River View Park, respectively.

Speaking during the signing ceremony, Mr Hamaundu said the project underscores the beginning of a transformative development initiative, aimed at providing sustainable infrastructure and improving the quality of life for citizens.

He said the initiative demonstrates what can be achieved when government institutions and strategic partners work together towards a common national purpose.

Mr Hamaundu said the government remains committed to improving the lives of Zambians through deliberate investment in infrastructure, housing, water supply and sanitation.

He said access to clean and reliable water is a fundamental human necessity and an important driver of national development, as it supports public health, education, economic productivity, environmental sustainability and social well-being.

Mr Hamaundu said the project aligns with the government’s broader development agenda of ensuring that citizens have access to essential services that promote dignity, good health and economic opportunity.

He noted that improved access to safe water and sanitation can reduce disease outbreaks, improve productivity and make housing developments more attractive to investors.

Mr Hamaundu commended the multi-sectoral partnership involving the Zambia Air Force, the National Pension Scheme Authority (NAPSA) and the Lusaka Water Supply and Sanitation Company Limited.

Lusaka Water Supply and Sanitation Company Managing Director Jilly Chiyombwe said the project represents an investment of approximately 150 million kwacha by NAPSA through Sable Projects, will include the construction of about 12 kilometres of a 450-millimetre diameter water pipeline, a 1,000-cubic-metre ground reservoir and associated project infrastructure.

And NAPSA Acting Director General Joshua Malipenga described the project as an important milestone in efforts to provide sustainable infrastructure to support residential and commercial development in the rapidly growing area.

World.title: We will expand student loans-HH
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema says his administration plans to expand student loans, bursaries and meal allowances, to accommodate more students beyond just public universities.

President Hichilema has assured that his administration will continue to invest in the education sector as this will not only contribute to job creation, economic growth, but also increase national revenue.

The President said that once re-elected for a second term, he intends to introduce a student internship programme for students to be attached to various institutions, in order to help them secure jobs once they graduate.

The Head of State said this during an engagement with students from over 50 higher institutions of learning in the country, at State House, in Lusaka.

“It does not matter whether you are from a private university or public university because a student from a private university is no different from a student in a public university. Why? They are all citizens of Zambia”, he stressed.

The President also indicated that his administration has transformed education into an economic sector, in order to generate more income for the nation and support delivery of various services such as health and infrastructure, among others.

He noted various reforms scored by his administration in the education sector, such as the signing of free education into law, re-introduction of meal allowances, infrastructure development as well as distribution of desks.

Earlier, students’ representatives commended the government for various achievements scored in the education sector over the last four years, plus.

Nelson Nyirenda, a fifth year student at Levy Mwanawasa Medical University thanked President Hichilema for signing free education into law, increasing the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) and student loans.

And a representative from the National Council of Student Unions (NACOSU), Vincent Sakala noted that students and the health sector in the country are the biggest beneficiaries of CDF.

“Students are the biggest community in the country, sponsored by CDF. Come August 13th, we have resolved to give 5.8 million votes to President Hichilema”, he pledged.

Another Student of Levy Mwanawasa University, Brian Malambo expressed confidence that if given another term, President Hichilema would drive the country towards economic stability through his strategies aimed at boosting production.

World.title: IBA cautions broadcasters to adhere to election guidelines ahead of Thursday elections
World.content:
The Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA), has cautioned broadcasters to adhere to outlined guidelines and not publish unverified information ahead of this year’s General Election.

Speaking during a press briefing in Lusaka today, IBA Director General, Webster Malido, who urged broadcasters to exercise caution when handling information, noted that elections results should only be broadcasted once they have been announced by the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ).

Mr Malido states that this is to ensure that the public receives accurate, reliable and verified information concerning the elections.

“Broadcasters are urged to avoid content that promotes hurt speech, violence or the dissemination of unverified information,” he stated.

He emphasised that all election related content should be accurate, verified and in a manner that represents public interests in order to avoid the spread of misinformation.

The Authority further encouraged members of the public as well as political parties and other stakeholders to make use of the complaint’s procedure established under the election guidelines.

“Complaints relating to the coverage of political parties, candidates or electoral issues should first be submitted to the broadcasting station concerned which is required to respond within two days’ o during the election period,” he stated.

Mr Malido highlighted that where no response is received during that period, only then can the matter be escalated to the Authority in accordance with the law.

The authority has since assured the public and electoral stakeholders of continued monitoring of election throughout the election period aimed at support compliance with the law, address complaints and ensure that all election coverage serves public interests among others.

World.title: Nkana UPND candidate gunners support
World.content:
United Party for National Development (UPND) Nkana Constituency candidates have urged voters to support the party’s candidates at all levels in the upcoming elections to promote development in the constituency.

Speaking at a public engagement, UPND aspiring Nkana Member of Parliament Francis Mukuka says the constituency needs leaders who will work closely with President Hakainde Hichilema to address challenges facing residents and improve development in the area.

Mr Mukuka said, if elected, he will prioritise creating more jobs and business opportunities for young people and ensure that residents benefit from economic activities in Nkana constituency.

“We need to work together. Nkana is the only constituency that has most of the industries, the mines, mining dump sites, most of the progressive things are in Nkana. But many of these things do not benefit us, the Nkana people,” he said.

And UPND Copperbelt Provincial Trustee Scrieviner Bwalya has urged voters in Nkana to turn out in large numbers on election day and exercise their democratic right by voting for candidates they believe can deliver meaningful development.

Mr Bwalya said residents should consider the development needs of their communities when choosing leaders and elect representatives who will remain responsive to their concerns and improve their livelihoods.

Meanwhile, Nkana Constituency Chairman David Luneta said although residents of Nkana voted for President Hakainde Hichilema in the 2021 general elections, they did not vote for a Member of Parliament or councillors.

Mr Luneta has therefore appealed to Nkana residents to support UPND candidates in the upcoming elections.

UPND Aspiring Ward Councillors have also appealed for support from voters in their respective wards, pledging to prioritise local development and address challenges affecting their communities if elected.

World.title: Chipata election preps progress well
World.content:
Chipata District Electoral Officer (DEO) Jovax Ngoma says preparations for the 2026 general elections in Chipata district are progressing well.

Mr Ngoma says ballot papers were received last week and the distribution to polling stations will be conducted tomorrow to ensure that the sensitive election materials are not left unattended for a prolonged period.

He also updated that accreditation of election stakeholders is also ongoing and is expected to close tomorrow.

He has assured residents of Chipata that the ECZ is fully prepared for the general elections scheduled for Thursday, August 13th, 2026.

“We want to assure the citizens of Chipata that everything is set in preparation for the general elections scheduled for August 13th, 2026,” he said.

The DEO said the ECZ is encouraged by the high turnout of citizens who have shown interest in participating in the electoral process by casting their votes.

Meanwhile, Mr Ngoma said the South African SADC Electoral Observation Mission is also in Eastern Province monitoring preparations and activities ahead of the elections.

And residents of Chipata have expressed readiness to participate in the August 13th general elections, saying they are prepared to turn up at polling stations and exercise their right to vote.

Mary Banda, a first time voter says she is excited about voting this Thursday.

“I want to encourage everyone who is registered to vote to turn up to vote, especially fellow young people. It is through the vote that we speak,” she indicated.

World.title: Austin Liato accorded official funeral
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has accorded former Movement for Multiparty Democracy (MMD) Cabinet Minister, Austin Liato, an official funeral.

President Hichilema has since declared Tuesday, August 11, 2026, as a one-day period of national mourning in honour of the late Mr Liato, in recognition of his contribution to national development during his tenure as minister.

Secretary to the Cabinet Patrick Kangwa disclosed this in a press statement issued to the media in Lusaka this evening.

Mr Kangwa said the late former cabinet minister will be put to rest tomorrow at Leopards Hill Memorial Park in Lusaka.

He said the burial will be preceded by an official funeral church service at the Anglican Cathedral of the Holy Cross in Lusaka at 10:00 hours.

He said the national mourning will be observed from 06:00 to 18:00 hours, during which all flags are expected to fly at half-mast.

The late Mr Liato aged 60, died on August 6, 2026, after an illness at Maina Soko Medical Centre in Lusaka.

He served as Minister of Labour and Social Security from 2008 to 2011 in the MMD administration.

World.title: ZMD predicates temperature reduction
World.content:
The Zambia Meteorological Department (ZMD) has issued a weather alert forecasting a reduction in temperature over Western, Lusaka, Central, Southern, Eastern and Muchinga provinces.

ZMD indicated that the reduction in temperature is being influenced by a high-pressure system over the Indian Ocean, which is currently driving strong, moist, and cool airflow across Zambia.

“A high-pressure system over the Indian Ocean is currently driving strong, moist, and cool airflow across Zambia. The system is expected to remain active throughout the forecast period, resulting in windy conditions across the country.

“A reduction in temperature is expected over Western, Lusaka, Central, Southern, Eastern and Muchinga provinces,”

This is according to the weather alert issued by ZMD valid from 11th to 15th August 2026.

Owing to the anticipated drop in temperature, ZMD has advised the public to dress warmly, especially during the cooler night and early morning hours.

While individuals with respiratory conditions, the elderly and children have been encouraged to limit exposure to dust and use appropriate protective measures where necessary.

ZMD has further urged Parents and guardians to closely supervise children and ensure they are kept safe from open fires, braziers, and other heating sources to avoid unnecessary burn injuries during the cold weather.

And users of water transport have been advised to exercise extreme caution when operating on water bodies due to anticipated hazardous windy conditions.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 11, 2026
World.content:
Zambia Election Set for Closely Fought Opposition Battle

Zambia's 13 August election has become a closely contested battle between the ruling United Party for National Development and the Tonse-Pamodzi opposition alliance, led by newcomer Brian Mundubile and backed by former Patriotic Front structures. The election is expected to test the opposition's strength and serve as a referendum on President Hakainde Hichilema's record. The government has made progress on debt restructuring, economic growth and inflation. But the high cost of living remains a big concern for voters. The poll is also taking place amid concerns over alleged state interference, restrictions on opposition activity and controversial legislative changes, making it a key test for Zambia's democracy.

WHO Warns DR Congo Ebola Response Falling Behind

More than 1,900 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak. 60-70% of deaths occur in communities before patients reach treatment centres. The WHO said that the concentration of healthcare services in Bunia, Ituri province, is forcing patients to travel long distances and seek care too late. Poor transport systems may also increase transmission. The agency plans to expand treatment facilities closer to communities, add 400 Ebola beds and strengthen public awareness and early referrals. WHO is also looking to the town of Aru, where no new cases have been reported for two weeks after authorities expanded surveillance and response beyond individual patients to surrounding communities.



Nigeria Lassa Fever Cases Reach 1,000 in 2026

Nigeria has reported 1,000 confirmed cases of Lassa fever and 237 deaths in 2026, with cases reported in 23 states and 116 local government areas. Five states, Ondo, Bauchi, Taraba, Edo and Benue, account for 86% of confirmed cases. At least 53 healthcare workers have also been infected, prompting the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention to introduce a 30-day protection plan for frontline staff. The agency has said that late presentation, high treatment costs, poor sanitation and limited awareness are contributing to the outbreak and high fatality rate. Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic disease transmitted primarily through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected rodents.

Malawi Land Audit Flags Irregular Plot Allocations

Malawi's Ministry of Lands is set to release findings from a pilot land ownership audit in Lilongwe that reportedly uncovered irregularities in the allocation of plots in the affluent Area 3 and Area 10. The audit was launched in February 2026 to improve transparency and accountability in land administration. It is said to have identified politically exposed individuals, including current and former ministers, judges and MPs, among those allegedly linked to irregular land acquisitions. The findings could trigger political controversy, with questions remaining over whether those implicated will be publicly named or face legal or disciplinary action.

UN Somalia Auction Raises Security Concerns

The UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) has opened a tender to auction vehicles, generators, IT equipment, medical supplies, construction machinery and other assets. This comes as Washington moves to end funding for the mission's logistical support by the end of 2026. UNSOS provides critical transport, fuel, food and other supplies to about 12,000 African troops and police serving under AUSSOM in the fight against al-Shabab. The auction has raised concerns among civil society groups over transparency and oversight. Regional leaders have warned that any premature reduction in international support could create a security vacuum as al-Shabab continues to operate in parts of Somalia.

Close 

Climate Change Shifts Africa's Malaria Risk

Climate change is reshaping malaria risk across Africa, with rising temperatures making parts of southern Africa and high-elevation areas of East Africa increasingly suitable for transmission, according to a new Nature study. Some parts of West and Central Africa may have become too hot for optimal malaria transmission. The region still bears about 95% of the global malaria burden. But experts warn that climate change is only part of the equation, with funding gaps, drug and insecticide resistance, and weak health systems still major threats. They are urging countries in emerging risk areas to step up malaria prevention and surveillance while maintaining elimination efforts in high-burden areas.

World.title: South Africa: Gauteng Gets 500,000 Grade 1 and 8 Applications - South African News Briefs - August 11, 2026
World.content:
Gauteng Records Nearly 500,000 Grade 1 and 8 Applications

Almost half a million applications have been submitted for Grade 1 and Grade 8 places in Gauteng for the 2027 academic year since the online application system opened, reports EWN. The Gauteng Department of Education has said that improvements have been made to streamline the process. Education MEC Lebogang Maile has urged parents to apply early. The department also says learners awaiting specialised placement should receive interim support rather than remain on waiting lists, with officials focusing on successful placements and resolving outstanding cases.

Strong Winds Damage Homes in Free State

The South African Red Cross Society is assessing damage caused by strong winds and heavy rainfall in Koppies and other parts of the Free State, reports SABC News. Several homes have reportedly been damaged, including roofs blown off, as severe weather persists. Red Cross volunteers are working with disaster management authorities and municipalities. Assessments continue, with humanitarian assistance being provided to affected households.

Fadiel Adams Unlikely to Testify at Madlanga Commission

National Coloured Congress leader Fadiel Adams is unlikely to testify before the Madlanga Commission, reports EWN. This comes after the commission received his affidavit and supporting documents late. Adams was expected to testify about his involvement in an Investigating Directorate Against Corruption probe into alleged corruption within Crime Intelligence. In 2024, he asked IDAC to investigate claims that the Political Killings Task Team had misused secret service funds for luxury accommodation and vehicles.

World.title: South Africa: Immigrant Traders See Their Livelihoods Destroyed By March and March
World.content:
Traders with documents and permits chased away, leaving Bellville bus terminus market almost empty

Dozens of immigrant traders who usually traded at the Golden Arrow terminus in Bellville are staying away because of anti-immigrant protests.

When we visited the once bustling site last week, it was quiet with only a handful of traders. Many stalls were deserted.



Some traders we spoke to said they had tried to set up shop in other areas but were stopped. They have not traded at the bus site since the March and March 30 June "deadline" demanding "illegal immigrants" leave South Africa.

"I need to pay rent, put food on the table, and pay the bills," a Zimbabwean man who asked to remain anonymous told GroundUp.

He said he has been selling clothes in Bellville for about five years. He left Zimbabwe in 2008 when its economy collapsed.

While he has not been directly threatened, he has witnessed others being harassed.

"They will take your stuff and throw it on the ground," he said.

"It hurts, but as much as it hurts, it's their country, and they're also marginalised people."

Another trader, who introduced herself as Meye, said she has had a permit to trade since 2010. She fled the DRC in 2003.

"We are legal; everything is correct. But they say we are foreigners and we need to go back to our country."

A single mother of three, she says she is now struggling to feed and school her children.

Another single mother, Safia, says she has been unable to trade despite having refugee status and a trading permit. She came from Somalia in 2010.

She said law enforcement needs to protect the traders better.

"I can't sleep at night because of what is happening. I can't even pay my rent. I can't support my children," she said.

Abdulhakim Husein, Western Cape director of the Somalia Association of South Africa, told GroundUp that he had been assisting traders since the start of July.

He said many asylum seekers and refugees are traders as they have to rely on being self-employed. They came from Somalia, DRC, Zimbabwe, Angola and Burundi.

He said that at a meeting on 13 July (which the City confirmed), it was agreed that traders with valid permits should be allowed to trade. But on 14 July, they received a message warning them about a March and March protest in the area.

Close 

Husein said they have approached a legal NGO for assistance.

City spokesperson Luthando Tyhalibongo said foreign nationals whose immigration status has been verified by Home Affairs are permitted to trade with a valid permit. These cost R78 per month.

"It is a concern whenever permitted traders, whether South African citizens or foreign nationals lawfully permitted to trade, are prevented from engaging in legal economic activity," he said.

He said intimidation and threats should be reported to SAPS.

World.title: Somalia: UN Puts Somalia Mission Assets Up for Sale As U.S. Funding Cutoff Looms
World.content:
Mogadishu, Somalia — The United Nations Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) has opened a tender seeking licensed auctioneers to sell off a wide range of its vehicles, generators and other equipment in Somalia, a notice published on the UN Global Marketplace shows.

The call for expressions of interest, issued August 6, comes as Washington moves to cut off funding for the UN's logistical support mission by the end of 2026, deepening uncertainty over the future of international backing for Somalia's fight against al-Shabab.

The tender matters now because it lands at the center of a widening rift between the United States and the United Nations over how and whether, to keep supporting Somalia's security transition. UNSOS underpins the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), supplying transport, fuel, food and other non-lethal supplies to roughly 12,000 African troops and police fighting a resilient insurgency. Any wind-down of that support network would strike at the core of the mission's ability to operate.

Under the terms of the tender, UNSOS is looking to establish a local contract for the "commercial sale" of UN-owned property. The initial deal would run three months, with up to three additional three-month extensions depending on performance and operational need.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The list of items up for sale is extensive: vehicles, generators, computers and IT equipment, office equipment, shipping containers, security watchtowers, wastewater treatment plants, prefabricated accommodation materials, medical and laboratory equipment, electrical appliances and heavy construction machinery. UNSOS said the list is indicative and may grow.

Interested firms have a narrow window to respond, with registration required by August 11 -- just five days after the notice was published.

Civil society analysts in Mogadishu have indicated that the auction notice does not lay out a clear mechanism for independent oversight, warning that disposing of mission assets without transparency could weaken public trust and open the door to diversion of state property.

The auction notice does not link the sale to the funding dispute. But it follows a July 1 letter in which the United States cited concerns over Somalia's performance against al-Shabab and its handling of security and governance issues, and comes as Washington has pushed back against extending UN logistical support for AUSSOM beyond current arrangements.

Somalia has fought al-Shabab for nearly two decades, and the group still holds sway over parts of the country. Leaders of AUSSOM troop-contributing nations have warned that a premature drawdown in support could open a security vacuum.

World.title: Malawi: Bombshell Land Audit to Name Ministers, Judges and MPs Over Illegal Plot Grabs
World.content:
Malawi's Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development is set to hold a highly anticipated press briefing this Wednesday to unveil the findings of a pilot land ownership audit conducted in Lilongwe - findings that are set to implicate some of the country's most powerful figures.

According to an invitation letter seen by this publication, Minister of Lands Chimwemwe Chipungu will personally preside over the briefing, which is expected to shed light on widespread irregularities uncovered during the audit process.

'The Ministry embarked on the Land Ownership Audit exercise in February 2026 as part of efforts to strengthen land administration systems, promote accountability in land ownership and enhance transparency and efficiency in the management of land resources,' the invitation reads.

The audit is understood to have uncovered significant irregularities in the allocation of plots specifically within Lilongwe's Area 3 and Area 10, two of the capital's most sought-after and valuable residential districts.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Most explosively, the audit has reportedly named a string of politically exposed individuals - including ministers serving in both the current and former administrations, sitting judges, and members of parliament - among those alleged to have acquired plots in the affected areas without following proper procedure.

The revelations, if confirmed at Wednesday's briefing, threaten to ignite a fresh political storm in Malawi, given the seniority of those reportedly implicated and the sensitivity surrounding land allocation in a country where access to prime urban plots has long been a source of controversy and allegations of favouritism.

The findings also land amid a period of intense scrutiny over transparency and accountability in public institutions more broadly, following separate controversies including the stalled parliamentary probe into the K128 billion Amaryllis Hotel purchase and mounting pressure over undisclosed presidential travel costs.

It remains to be seen whether Wednesday's briefing will name the individuals implicated publicly, or whether further legal or disciplinary action is being considered against those found to have benefited from irregular land allocations.

Ministry officials have not yet responded to requests for further comment ahead of the scheduled press briefing.

World.title: Actress Swell Ariel Or takes advocacy for Israeli women further in new film ‘Tankistas’
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Israeli actress Swell Ariel Or has long cared about championing Israeli women and Jews, but her new role playing an Israel Defense Forces unit captain during the deadly Oct. 7 Hamas attacks has her taking her advocacy to the next level.

Since the Tel Aviv-born star of Netflix’s Israeli television series "The Beauty Queen of Jerusalem" hit Hollywood’s radar in 2021, she’s been on a mission — and it doesn’t involve chasing award nominations or lucrative brand endorsements like many rising young actresses in Tinseltown.

Instead, Or told Fox News Digital, her mission focuses on authentic storytelling and meaningful narratives that accurately represent her people.

"I think that, of course, the Oscars matter and Hollywood, I mean, like, it's like the Olympics for films and TV, right? But I've seen what it does to the industry to be driven by getting an award or getting accepted to an elite circle of intellectuals and art people," she said. "I just feel as a storyteller that it hurts — that's not what we’re telling stories for."

IDF CLAIMS TO HAVE TAKEN OUT HAMAS COMMANDER WHO PARTICIPATED IN OCT 7

The 27-year-old actress recently went viral for echoing that sentiment on Instagram for ARISE for Israel, an alliance whose mission is to "reinforce Israel’s security and economy," while promoting her new film, "Tankistas." The plural form of "tankista," the title means "tank crew members" or "tankers" in several languages.

"I don’t care about the Oscars. I don’t care about Hollywood. I don’t care about doing the biggest, greatest career… I care about honest representation of who we are," Or said about her upcoming film, which wrapped production earlier this year and is being edited in both English and Hebrew versions and is set for release next year.

The war drama, directed by Ayelet Menahemi ("Seven Blessings") and inspired by true events, follows the IDF’s first all-female tank unit and its 17-hour defense during the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks. As the unit’s captain, Or’s character leads three armored vehicles and engages Hamas militants in battle.

Or served in the IDF in real life before moving to Hollywood to pursue an acting and modeling career. She, along with fellow cast members, spent a good deal of time with the real-life women of the combat unit on which the film is based.

She also spoke about why the movie stands out among other combat films and female-focused superhero movies.

"The world is obsessed right now with female heroes, but so often, I feel like it's from the wrong reasons, because it sells or whatever," she said. "This film is very unique because if it was an American film about an all-female team company in World War II or whatever, it checks all the boxes of everything the world wants to see. But this is a feminist film written by women, based on a true story that actually happened, but it's Israeli."

CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM

"It's not a typical war film, thank God, because unlike so many films that try to bring a female hero to the front, the characters here are based on real women," she continued. "They are diverse and human and complex, and it captures what the world so often fails to understand about Israeli women, especially about Israeli women in combat."

Or has made a habit of sharing her convictions while appearing prominently on podcasts and in viral clips of media commentary, where she’s addressed antisemitism and the importance of authentic representation for Jewish and Israeli women in entertainment.

She’s appeared on the "Stars of David with Elon Gold" podcast and "Reel Talk," and joined Tablet Magazine’s "Unorthodox Podcast" to discuss relocating to the U.S. shortly before Oct. 7 and what it’s like to be an Israeli artist abroad.

ARISE for Israel called her "one of the most powerful voices for Israelis and Jews in Hollywood."

Roz Rothstein, co-founder and CEO of the international, nonpartisan Israel education organization StandWithUs, called her an "important voice for a new generation at a time when too many Jews feel pressure to hide their identity, soften their connection to Israel, or remain silent in the face of antisemitism."

"Swell is standing tall and using her platform to tell the diverse stories of the Jewish people while encouraging others to do so," she added.

FREED HOSTAGE ROM BRASLAVSKI DETAILS ABUSE, STARVATION DURING 738 DAYS IN GAZA CAPTIVITY

"I feel like this community — it's so misunderstood," Or told Fox Digital about portraying Israeli women in a combat role. "You don't have a lot of stories who portray so many layers at the same time of a woman who's a commander in combat — the values, who they are, their humanity, the profound gap between how the world sees them and what their motives are and what they carry with them."

Besides "Tankistas," the actress can be seen in a new season of her Netflix show, which she said focuses heavily on the year 1948 and the Israeli War of Independence.

"This is a year that is very much relevant for people to learn more about," Or said.

She also recently finished shooting her first short film, "The Divide," which she said is being developed into a feature.

Despite her representation of her homeland, Or said she’s no stranger to facing backlash or listening to those who raise concerns about the tragedy of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

"Last week, I walked in LA and a person approached me, and she's like, ‘I watched ‘Beauty Queen.’ I have to tell you, I define myself as Palestinian, but I watched the whole thing because I wanted to see Jerusalem of that day because my family came from there too’," Or recalled.

Regarding Oct. 7, Or said she knew six people who were murdered at the Nova music festival that day.

"You can have debates from here ‘til Russia and back about what happened on October 7. But the festival, it's like something that you can't debate about," she said.

"Growing up in Israel, you are born at a crossroads of so many identities and histories of your own people, so you got to love storytelling because your family's going to tell you all of them, and for me, it's my passion, and it's like my purpose in life," Or continued.
