However, there will be no slogan shouting or demonstrations as part of the protest,â Valarmathi said.

Key demands

The LPST rank holders have been protesting for over a month, demanding appointments from the Kerala Public Service Commission's rank list for Lower Primary School Teacher posts, published in May 2025.

They have also sought greater transparency in reporting vacancies and changes to the recruitment process.

The protesters are seeking a reduction in the teacher-student ratio to 1:25, creation of additional teacher posts and the transfer of appointments in aided schools to the Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC). They argue that lowering the ratio would create more teaching posts and help facilitate appointments for rank holders.

The government had also proposed a two-month salary concession if the protesters called off the agitation, but the proposal was rejected.

World.title: ‘Women are coming for signatures, at least dress properly’: Delhi CM targets AAP MLA over viral video
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Monday took a dig at Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLA Anil Jha Vats over a viral video showing him sitting in his undergarments while signing documents for people in his constituency.

The video, which has surfaced on social media, shows the AAP MLA from Kirari in northwest Delhi seated cross-legged in a chair, wearing a vest and shorts, with a saffron cloth draped across his lap.

The video was reportedly recorded while Jha was signing application forms from constituents for a Delhi government scheme providing financial assistance to women. Several people, including women, can be seen waiting in a queue in front of Jha's desk as he signs the documents.

Referring to the video during the Monsoon Session of the Delhi assembly, Rekha Gupta criticised the MLA over his attire and said public representatives should maintain decorum, particularly when interacting with women constituents.

"Your behaviour is shameful. You should at least dress properly when women come to you to get their papers signed," the chief minister said.

"Tell them to get the signboard removed in such a situation.





I saw their reel. Delhiâs people are questioning you. You should be ashamed. I have seen the recordings. This is not how a Vishakhyak (public representative) should behave," she added.

The BJP leader further said that the dignity and respect of women must be protected in public life and that indecent behaviour or objectionable gestures towards women were inconsistent with democratic values and the dignity of the House.

She added that protecting women's dignity was the collective responsibility of all elected representatives and said the Delhi government was committed to safeguarding the rights and dignity of women.

Rekha also accused Jha of making obscene gestures during the assembly proceedings and demanded action against him.

âThe House is the supreme forum for democratic decorum and dignity. The uncivil behavior of the Aam Aadmi Party and their MLA will not be tolerated under any circumstances.

A complaint will be lodged at the appropriate level in this regard,â she said while speaking to reporters.

Anil Jha Vats denied allegation

Jha denied the chief minister's allegation and challenged her to produce video evidence of him making any such gestures.

What is the âzombie drugâ?

NEW DELHI: BJP Rajya Sabha MP and former cricketer Harbhajan Singh came under fire after he shared a video of two apparently intoxicated men on Monday, claiming it showed the sorry state of Punjabâs youth. Punjab Police and AAP leaders later said the footage was actually from Rajasthan.âvery sad to see the situation of Punjab,â Singh wrote on Monday night.âPunjab and its youth deserve better. This issue needs honesty, accountability, and urgent action - not denial,â he added.In a longer message accompanying the video, Singh questioned successive governments over the drug situation in Punjab.âWhat have the governments done to Punjab and its Punjabi youth? Where have they brought Punjab to? The Punjab that was once known for its high spirits, courage and bravery, today that same Punjab's youth has been engulfed by drugs. There is still time - save my Punjab,â he said.Singh had quit the AAP and joined the BJP in April.The post quickly drew criticism from AAP leaders, who accused Singh of using a video from another state to portray Punjab in a negative light.âZombie drugâ commonly refers to xylazine, a veterinary sedative found in illicit drug supplies and also known as âtranqâ or âtranq dopeâ. The video went viral on social media, with users claiming the two men appeared to be under the influence of drugs, including what was described as a âzombie drugâ.However, Singh did not use the term in his post while sharing the clip.The claim was challenged by Punjab Police, which said the video was not from Punjab but from Sri Ganganagar in Rajasthan.âThe video being circulated is from Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan - not Punjab,â Punjab Police said in a post on X.The police urged social media users to verify the location and facts before sharing such material.âWe urge users and social media accounts to verify the facts and location before posting misleading content or tagging Punjab Police. He is sharing a video from Rajasthan and lying that it is from Punjab.âYou will do anything for 'BJP ki dalali', even if it means ruining Punjab's image. World.title: 'Speak impeccable Tamil' vs 'I have my own style': Grammar jibes set off row in Tamil Nadu assembly
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A row over Tamil Nadu finance ministerâs language and pronunciation skills during his budget speech triggered a political row in the state assembly on Monday, with the opposition members criticising his use of English and "grammatical errors".

The controversy began when MDMK MLA T M Rajendran, who won from Kadayanallur assembly constituency on the DMKâs Rising Sun symbol, pointed out "gramatical errors" in TVK minister N Marie Wilsonâs August 5 budget speech.

'Several grammatical errors'

Rajendran said Wilson had skipped several Tamil sentences and used English extensively during the speech. âAs a Tamil enthusiast, I observed in his (Marie Wilsonâs) speech that he had skipped many of the Tamil sentences.

There were several grammatical errors too,ââ Rajendran said.

âAtleast in the future, when he gets the opportunity the finance minister should speak in impeccable Tamil,â he added.

Rajendran also asked school education minister A Rajmohan to help Wilson improve his Tamil. Rajmohan, however defended the finance minister, saying there was nothing wrong with his speech. He also pointed out that leader of opposition

spoke in a plain and simple language.





'I would speak in my own style'

The remarks drew an angry response from Wilson, who defended his communication style and said his focus was on governance and the stateâs development rather than linguistic formalities.

âThe government under chief minister C Joseph Vijay has made significant achievements in the past 60-75 days, successfully bringing Rs 15,000 crores into the treasury through various reforms,â Wilson said, without elaborating.

Wilson said he had worked in the education sector for 25 to 30 years and had primarily communicated in English during his professional career.

âEarlier they were body shaming other and were insulting others based on caste and gender. Now they are insulting us over language,â Marie Wilson said.

The minister said he felt that members were targeting his communication style and background instead of focusing on his work.

He said he could not change the way he spoke simply to satisfy others.

Citing the Bible, Wilson said that while he might not be well-versed in Tamil, Christianity had taught him several languages, including the âlove language, peace language and the language of kindnessâ.

He added that he could not change his pronunciation for others and said âI would speak in my own style and that I could not change it to suit others.â

Speaker J C D Prabhakar intervened and advised Wilson to sit down and avoid getting angry.

'Tamil and English both allowed'

DMK senior leader and former minister E V Velu sought to defuse the issue, pointing out that Tamil has several dialects across the state, including differences between north and south Chennai.

Velu also stressed that Tamil Nadu followed a dual-language policy of Tamil and English.

The Speaker also noted that Rajendran himself had used the English word âbudgetâ in his speech instead of its Tamil equivalent.

Prabhakar urged members to treat the matter lightly and avoid turning language into a source of conflict in the House. He said the Assembly was a forum where multiple languages were permitted under its rules and members should focus on policy discussions rather than personal remarks.

The Speaker cited an earlier instance when then chief minister J Jayalalithaa allowed a Congress member to speak in Telugu in the Assembly.

He also pointed out that former finance minister P Thiaga Rajan had used English during earlier budget sessions.

Prabhakar said Assembly Rule 86 allows members to conduct proceedings in Tamil or English, or in both languages. He stressed that the focus should be on the intent and substance of what is being said rather than the language used.
